title: Star Trek actor Patrick Stewart dies at 86, colleagues post tributes
content: As we all begin to absorb the bitter news of Patrick Stewart's death at the age of 86, a flood of personal tributes are pouring in, reflecting this global treasure's wonderful life lived with a dignity and bravado that few mortals possess. We’re getting just a hint of what Patrick Stewart meant to those who worked with him or knew him throughout his stellar career. Whether on stage with the Royal Shakespeare Company, on TV as the dashing Captain Jean-Luc Picard in " Star Trek: The Next Generation," and in Hollywood spectacles like 1984's "Dune," four " Star Trek " feature films, and the many "X-Men" movies in which he portrayed Professor Charles Xavier, Stewart was always the consummate professional. His final screen performance arrives on Dec. 18 with "Avengers: Doomsday" where he’ll present his Charles Xavier character once more. "Before everything else, Patrick was defined by being born and bred in Yorkshire, the proud county in the north of England which he loved to the end," Ian McKellen wrote on Instagram of his "X-Men" co-star and friend. "You could hear it in his accented voice and in the stern honesty with which he told you what he thought and felt. Yorkshiremen have no truck with half-truths or avoidance of big issues. He wore his heart on his sleeve, which made him a man to rely on, to admire and, in my case, love." Patrick Stewart and Ian McKellan in 2000's "X-Men." (Image credit: 20th Century Studios) William Shatner, a fellow Enterprise captain, offered his profound sense of loss on Stewart's passing. The legends shared the screen in 1994's "Star Trek: Generations." "What a heartbreaking week it has been. Sir Patrick Stewart was a friend, a colleague, and a magnificent actor," Shatner posted on Facebook. "From the stage to the bridge of the Enterprise, he brought intelligence, grace, and a deep sense of humanity to everything he did. Captain Picard stood for the best of us, and so did the man who played him. I was filled with affection and admiration for him and his work. My heart goes out to Sunny and his family. He will be deeply missed." Patrick Stewart and William Shatner star in 1994's "Star Trek: Generations." (Image credit: Paramount) Akiva Goldsman, co-creator of Paramount+'s " Star Trek: Picard " and "Star Trek: Strange New Worlds," delivered a sorrowful message in the aftermath of Stewart's death "Patrick was not only a true lion of the profession, he was the rarest of alchemists, one who could literally turn the written word into flesh and blood," Goldsman wrote. "Patrick was kind, strong, fiercely intelligent, collaborative, vulnerable and wise. His Captain Jean-Luc Picard permanently expanded the universe of 'Star Trek' without measure. He will be deeply missed by this one fan and by so many more." Stewart's "Star Trek: The Next Generation" family shared their grief and offered up poignant words to try to describe what effect he had on their lives and profession. "There's no one on this planet that I have acted with or directed more often than my late great friend Patrick Stewart," revealed actor and director Jonathan Frakes, who co-starred for over 35 years with Stewart as Commander Will Riker, in a touching statement. "He will be with me forever. May he rest in Peace." Jonathan Frakes and Patrick Stewart share a laugh in "Star Trek: The Next Generation." (Image credit: Paramount) Finally, Marina Sirtis posted a teary-eyed video in which she explained how much of an impact Stewart had on her life during their time together on "The Next Generation" series and films, in which she portrayed Counselor Deanna Troi beside him. "Patrick, I loved you with all my heart," she said on Instagram. "I know you're up there now, reunited with all those that you've loved. But to say that you'll be missed down here is probably the understatement of the century. It was an honor to work with Patrick. It was more than an honor; it was the privilege of my life to work with him."
summary: Star Trek actor Patrick Stewart dies at 86, colleagues post tributes.
author: Space.com

title: Exeter’s Tom Hooper: ‘Sometimes you’ve just got to suck up a little bit of pain’
content:
Exeter Chiefs director of rugby Rob Baxter has commented on the club’s history of attracting Australian players, noting that many Wallabies have found a "spiritual home" in Exeter. The article highlights a long list of former Australian players who have played for the team, including Dean Mumm, Dave Dennis, Nic White, Scott Sio, Greg Holmes, Julian Salvi, Ben White, Mitch Lees, Lachie Turner, and Len Ikitau. Baxter observed that these players have generally relished their time in the south-west of England, humorously suggesting they "seem to like the pasties and the cider."

While the piece mentions that local surfing opportunities and beaches may contribute to the appeal, Baxter offered an alternative theory regarding the attraction. He suggested that Exeter and Devon are more similar to Australia than other parts of England, citing the region's open spaces and the club's "old-school" character. Baxter stated that Australian players appear to prefer this specific environment. The article title indicates that the featured player, Tom Hooper, also discussed coping with the English weather, the benefits of rehabilitation, and Australia’s chances in the upcoming World Cup.
summary: Chiefs’ latest Wallaby Tom Hooper discusses dealing with English weather, the positive side of rehab, and Australia’s World Cup chances. Exeter’s director of rugby Rob Baxter notes that Australian players often find a spiritual home in the club's old-school environment.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Alex de Minaur reaches 350th career win in Vienna quarter-final
content:
Alex de Minaur reached a career milestone at the Vienna Open by recording his 350th tour-level win, becoming the ninth Australian man to achieve this feat. The world No. 10 defeated Matteo Berrettini 7-6 (7-4), 6-2 in the quarter-final of the ATP 500 event held at the Wiener Stadthalle. This victory marks the second consecutive year that de Minaur has beaten the Italian in this tournament stage.

The result secures a semi-final match for de Minaur against Alexander Zverev, who is described in the report as the world No. 1-elect.
summary: Alex de Minaur defeated Matteo Berrettini 7-6 (7-4) 6-2 in the quarter-final of the Vienna Open. This victory marked the 27-year-old's 350th tour-level win and secured a semi-final match against Alexander Zverev.
author: Guardian Sport

title: England crush USA 55-12 to extend 35-year winning streak
content:
England defeated the United States 55-12 in the WXV Global Series, extending a 35-year winning streak against their opponents. The Red Roses secured their 22nd consecutive victory over the USA, a run that dates back to the 1991 Rugby World Cup. Claudia Moloney-MacDonald was a standout performer for England, scoring four tries during the match.

The United States entered the game in strong form, having won five consecutive matches, including victories over Wales and Ireland. Freda Tafuna, the USA’s No 8, had been a notable performer throughout the tournament. However, England managed to contain Tafuna’s influence. Despite contributions from Alev Kelter and Hope Rogers, the hosts lacked the necessary firepower to challenge the world No 1 team, highlighting the gap between the top three sides and the rest of the competition.
summary: England defeated the United States 55-12 to maintain their 35-year winning streak against the USA. The Red Roses secured the victory with four tries from Claudia Moloney-MacDonald.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Aston Villa to sue Jamie Carragher over 'unacceptable insults'
content: Villa chair announces plan on social media Carragher said club will ‘never be Man United’ Aston Villa have announced plans to take legal action against Jamie Carragher following his “unacceptable insults” about the club and its supporters. Carragher told Villa fans to “shut the fuck up” after facing criticism for suggesting Unai Emery should consider taking the Manchester United job. Villa responded on Friday evening with a statement on X signed by their chair, Nassef Sawiris.
summary: Aston Villa announced plans to take legal action against Jamie Carragher following his "unacceptable insults" toward the club and its supporters. Carragher told Villa fans to "shut the fuck up" after suggesting Unai Emery should consider the Manchester United job.

title: 9th Circuit rejects Trump bid to set aside 20,000 California ballots
content: A split panel of the U.S. Court of Appeals for the 9th Circuit has again rejected the Trump administration’s request to set aside 20,000 California ballots. The 2-1 majority upheld a lower court’s finding that the list of likely noncitizens is not credible, denying the administration’s bid to hold those ballots until verification is complete.
summary: A split federal appeals court panel rejected the Trump administration's request to suspend 20,000 California ballots pending verification. The 2-1 majority upheld a lower court's finding that the list of likely noncitizens was not credible.

title: Federal debt tops GDP for fiscal 2026, BEA reports
content: According to new data from the Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA), the U.S. national debt surpassed the gross domestic product for fiscal 2026. The BEA’s non-seasonally adjusted statistics indicate that the country’s economic output exceeded $32.2 trillion from the fourth quarter of 2025 through the third quarter of this year.
summary: The national debt topped the entire gross domestic product (GDP) for fiscal 2026, according to new data from the Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA). From the fourth quarter of 2025 through the third quarter of this year, the country’s economic output was more than $32.2 trillion, according to the BEA’s non-seasonally adjusted statistics.

title: Cleveland Clinic study links active platelets to glioblastoma progression
content: New Cleveland Clinic research published in Cancer Cell indicates that individuals with glioblastoma exhibit more active platelets. These cells, primarily involved in blood clotting, also communicate with other cells and influence immune activity. The study finds that this heightened platelet activity slows the function of cancer-fighting T cells, a process that may contribute to tumor growth and cancer progression.
summary: Research published in Cancer Cell indicates that people with glioblastoma have more active platelets that can influence immune activity. These overactive platelets slow the activity of cancer-fighting T cells, contributing to tumor growth and cancer progression.

title: Welsh study links congenital anomalies and deprivation to children's educational achievement
content: New research from Wales has examined how congenital anomalies, socioeconomic deprivation, and other health and educational factors collectively influence children's academic attainment. The study highlights the combined impact of these various circumstances on student achievement.
summary: New Welsh research reveals how congenital anomalies and socioeconomic deprivation influence children's attainment. The study examines how these factors, combined with other health and educational circumstances, impact educational outcomes.

title: Study finds blocking molecular interaction reduces heart scarring and abnormal rhythms
content: Researchers from Baylor College of Medicine and the University of Oxford reported that blocking a specific molecular interaction reduced atrial fibrosis in mouse models and human patient cells. The study found this approach also reversed established atrial fibrosis and reduced abnormal heart rhythms in the mouse models, suggesting potential for future therapies.
summary: Researchers from Baylor College of Medicine and the University of Oxford found that blocking a specific molecular interaction reduced atrial fibrosis in mouse models and human cells. In mouse models, this approach also reversed established atrial fibrosis and reduced abnormal heart rhythms.

title: How mental health and cancer survivorship intersect
content: A Stanford Medicine study highlights a period of vulnerability for cancer survivors, finding that mental health disorders identified two to five years after diagnosis are associated with a 119% higher rate of cancer-related death. This increased mortality risk was observed in patients with documented mental disorders compared to those without such conditions during the same timeframe.
summary: A Stanford Medicine study identified a vulnerable period for cancer survivors. Mental health disorders diagnosed two to five years after a cancer diagnosis were associated with a 119% higher rate of death from cancer compared with patients without documented mental disorders during the same period.

title: Study: Older men with overdose hospitalizations face higher acute kidney injury risk
content: Research published in the CDC’s Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report indicates that acute kidney injury occurs more frequently among older patients and men hospitalized for drug overdoses. The study further notes that severe inpatient courses disproportionately affect younger patients.
summary: Research published in the CDC's Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report indicates that acute kidney injury is more common among older patients and men hospitalized for drug overdoses. The study also notes that severe inpatient courses disproportionately affect younger patients.

title: New swab test could spare some women a painful biopsy for endometrial cancer
content: A new vaginal swab test could potentially allow women experiencing abnormal bleeding to determine if they have endometrial cancer without undergoing a painful biopsy. This diagnostic method aims to spare patients the discomfort associated with traditional biopsy procedures.
summary: A simple vaginal swab may one day help women with abnormal bleeding learn whether they have endometrial cancer without first going through a painful biopsy.

title: Novel chemical reaction expands options for building DNA-encoded libraries
content: DNA-encoded libraries (DELs) facilitate drug discovery by screening extensive compound collections. Each molecule in a DEL is tagged with a short DNA sequence that serves as a molecular barcode, enabling researchers to identify compounds that interact with specific biological targets.
summary: The new chemical reaction expands options for building DNA-encoded libraries. DNA-encoded libraries attach a short DNA sequence to each molecule, serving as a barcode that lets researchers identify promising compounds.

content: The piece notes that the spooky is a hugely popular phenomenon in British culture, evident in a month‑long Halloween celebration, a rich tradition of horror cinema, and a growing interest in the uncanny. It also points out that there are other manifestations of haunting.
summary: Hauntology examines how past events and what did not happen shape the present. content: Four new frog species discovered in Peru have been named, expanding knowledge of the country’s biodiversity. The species were identified and named by FIU biologist Alessandro Catenazzi, underscoring that science cannot study or unlock a species’ potential until it is known to exist.
summary: Science cannot study a species until people know it exists. Four new frog species in Peru have been named by FIU biologist Alessandro Catenazzi.

content: The piece describes a scenario in which someone has begun an online conversation with an attractive stranger, feels uncertain about what to say, worries that the other person’s patience may be wearing thin, and looks for guidance. content:
A new gene‑editing system, SmartPE, was developed by researchers in China.  

It improves prime editing efficiency in several dicot plants, making it easier for researchers to introduce precise genetic changes into crops such as tomatoes, soybeans and rapeseed, addressing a major limitation of the technique.

content:
Spanish Transport Minister Oscar Puente faced calls to resign after a high‑speed train crashed in Toledo province on Wednesday, killing 69 people. The incident marks Spain’s second high‑speed rail disaster this year.  

Puente ruled out stepping down on Friday, despite the pressure, according to FRANCE 24 correspondent Sarah Morris.
summary: Spanish Transport Minister Oscar Puente faced calls to resign but ruled out stepping down on Friday. The Wednesday crash in Toledo province killed 69 people and is the country’s second high-speed rail disaster this year.

arts24 reports that Le Fantôme de l'Opéra returns to French cinemas.

content: A Greek container ship sank after being struck by three drones, possibly of Russian origin, in the Black Sea off the Bulgarian coast on Wednesday, October 28. The incident underscores rising concerns for commercial shipping amid the ongoing Ukraine‑Russia conflict.
summary: A Greek container ship sank after being hit by three drones, possibly of Russian origin, in the Black Sea off Bulgaria on Wednesday, October 28. The attack raises concerns for commercial shipping amid the ongoing Ukraine‑Russia conflict.

title: France deploys 70,000 police as interior minister warns of very high disorder risk
content: France’s interior minister warned Thursday of a “very high risk of public disorder” and said roughly 70,000 police officers will be deployed for a new wave of protests scheduled for the weekend. The announcement follows nationwide demonstrations on October 17 that escalated into some of the country’s worst rioting in years, reflecting widespread anger over rising living costs and inequality. FRANCE 24’s International Affairs Editor Rochelle Ferguson Bouyahi provides further details.
summary: France's interior minister warned of a very high risk of public disorder and announced the deployment of around 70,000 police officers for protests this weekend. The protests follow nationwide demonstrations on October 17 that turned into some of the country's worst rioting in years amid anger over the cost of living and inequality.
author: France 24

title: Israel election deadlocked as opposition bloc ties with Netanyahu camp
content: Israel’s wartime election appeared deadlocked on Tuesday, according to exit polls. The polls showed Gadi Eisenkot’s opposition bloc running neck‑and‑neck with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s camp, leaving neither side with a clear path to power. The projections suggested a setback for Netanyahu’s coalition and indicated that weeks of political wrangling may be required to form a government. France 24’s Jerusalem correspondent Noga Tarnopolsky reported on the developments.
summary: Exit polls on Tuesday showed Israel's wartime election deadlocked, with Gadi Eisenkot's opposition bloc neck and neck with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's camp. The results give neither side a clear path to power and may lead to weeks of political wrangling to form a government.
author: France 24

title: Tennessee inmate Christa Pike says she lives in constant pain after botched execution
content: Tennessee death‑row inmate Christa Pike, convicted of murder, said she remains in constant pain after surviving a botched lethal injection in September. In her first public statement since the failed execution, she thanked the people who saved her life and urged compassion for the victim’s family.
summary: Christa Pike, a convicted murderer on Tennessee's death row, said she lives in constant pain after surviving a botched lethal injection in September. In her first public statement, she thanked those who saved her life and urged compassion for her victim's family.

title: Former PM Ehud Barak says Netanyahu lost dramatically in Israeli election
content: In an interview with FRANCE 24, former Israeli prime minister Ehud Barak said Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu "did not win" this week's election in Israel but "lost dramatically", and that his rival Gadi Eisenkot should ally with Arab parties. Barak also suggested that claims of Qatari funding for an Arab party aimed to distract from an ongoing corruption scandal, and warned that Netanyahu was ready to strike Iran to stay in power.

title: Pastor Caleb Campbell, former neo‑Nazi, warns midterms as evangelical critic of Trump
content:
A poll shows that 82 percent of white evangelical Protestants voted for Donald Trump in the 2024 presidential election, making pastor Caleb Campbell a notable outlier. The former neo‑Nazi pastor has been one of the few evangelical critics of the Trump administration, first speaking out during Trump’s initial term against plans to place “kids in cages” as part of an immigration crackdown. Campbell recalls being told he was “possessed by a demon” for his opposition.

As the 2026 midterms approach, Campbell says he believes U.S. politics and the current administration have moved farther from the Bible’s teachings.

content:
Javits Frimpong, a 15‑year‑old from Ghana, was chased and fatally shot on his way to school in the Bronx on Thursday. His father says the boy had been bullied at school before the incident.

The New York City Police Department received a report Thursday morning of a shooting near Corona Park. Officers responded at about 9:24 a.m. and found Frimpong with a gunshot wound to his stomach.

content: Rex Patrick’s latest transparency fight is over what he calls ‘most open secret in the history of Australian spying’ – maybe even the world Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast A campaign to uncover any documents relating to whether Australian spies bugged Timor-Leste to gain the upper hand in sensitive oil and gas negotiations will be a little less secret after a critical win by the former senator Rex Patrick. title: US cancels G20 family photo after Australia, UK refuse to appear with Russia
content:
The U.S. has cancelled the customary “family photo” that opens the G20 foreign ministers’ meeting.

The decision follows refusals by several countries, including Australia and the United Kingdom, to stand beside Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov in the snapshot.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio ended the photo op after European officials, the UK and Australia announced they would boycott or walk out of the session.

title: ‘There’s a new chapter to write’: Le Bris upbeat as Sunderland eye Coventry reunion
content:
Sunderfield manager Le Bris expressed optimism as his team prepares for a potential reunion with Coventry, noting that while European football has stretched resources, the busy schedule is not something to complain about. This sentiment follows a recent 2025 Championship playoff semi-final second leg, where Sunderland secured a 1-1 draw to eliminate Coventry on a 3-2 aggregate score.

The decisive moment came with twenty seconds of stoppage time remaining, when Enzo Le Fée delivered a right-footed corner that dipped into the penalty area. Dan Ballard subsequently powered a header off the crossbar to secure the result, ending Coventry’s campaign in the semi-final stage.
summary: ‘There’s a new chapter to write’: Le Bris upbeat as Sunderland eye Coventry reunion.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Searle leads Leicester to 22-16 win over Bristol for Prem top spot
content:
Leicester secured a 22-16 bonus-point victory over Bristol to take the top spot in the Premiership. The match was described as an error-strewn contest between two teams that started the evening in second and third position. Despite the mistakes, Leicester emerged as the clear winner, scoring four tries to one in the shootout for the league lead.

The performance was highlighted by fly-half Billy Searle, who was named the game’s outstanding player. Searle’s left boot set up all three of his side’s tries and he also landed two conversions, masterfully steering the Tigers to victory. This result followed on from Leicester’s commanding second-half display against Northampton the previous Saturday.

Bristol, who began the night in third, had moments of promise but struggled with possession. The home side was reduced to 13 players during the second quarter after receiving a brace of yellow cards. Ultimately, Bristol coughed up possession too often, allowing Leicester to maintain control and claim the spoils.
summary: Leicester defeated Bristol 22-16 in a match for the top spot in the Premiership, scoring four tries to one. Fly-half Billy Searle set up all three of Leicester's tries and kicked two conversions in the error-strewn game.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Carrick tells players ‘hard truth’ in attempt to turn Manchester United’s season around

United have not won in their past eight games and start the weekend in 16th place of 20 in the league, one point above the relegation zone.
summary: Carrick tells players ‘hard truth’ in attempt to turn Manchester United’s season around.

summary: England beat Papua New Guinea 34-12 at the Rugby League World Cup in Wollongong, but look set to miss out on the semi-finals following their opening loss to Tonga.

title: Sketch Stadium enables AI agents to play Pictionary via Wakeshift SDK
content:
Sketch Stadium is a new platform that allows artificial intelligence agents to play Pictionary. The project was initially developed as a proof-of-concept for delivering push notifications to AI agents but has been released as a standalone demonstration. Users can connect their own agents to the platform or simply observe ongoing games via a provided link.

In the game, agents subscribe to game events and take turns either drawing or guessing clues. The scoring system awards one point for easy clues, two for medium, and three for hard. The developer noted that the initial version allowed agents to draw lines ten at a time to mimic real Pictionary, but this method proved ineffective. The platform now permits agents to use a subset of SVG for drawing, which has improved performance even for lower-cost models.

To integrate an agent, users do not need to create an account; they only need to add the MCP and authorize it. The project serves as a technical demo for Wakeshift, a cross-harness SDK designed to provide push notifications for agents. This tool attaches to an MCP to allow consumers to subscribe to real-time events and uses specific methods per harness to wake dormant agents.

The developer explained that agents often initiate processes with indeterminate completion times, such as continuous integration or waiting for approvals. Currently, there is no consistent method to wake agents via webhook or push notification, forcing reliance on polling or bespoke integrations. The developer previously addressed this challenge with Clawvisor, where long-polling was the best-supported method for recognizing out-of-band approval actions. Wakeshift aims to solve this by providing a simple SDK that upgrades automatically as harnesses adopt MCP events.
summary: The platform allows agents to subscribe to game events and take turns drawing or guessing using a subset of SVG. The project serves as a tech demo for Wakeshift, an SDK designed to provide push notifications for AI agents.
author: Hacker News

title: Demo Shows FlashAttention Kernel Derived from ~25 Lines of SQL Using New SQL Extensions
content:
A developer has shared a demonstration on Hacker News that automatically deduces a FlashAttention kernel using approximately 25 lines of SQL. The SQL code expresses vanilla attention, a feat made possible by three portable SQL extensions currently under development. These extensions include xarray-sql, a library designed to represent petabyte-scale array datasets in the cloud as tables; ddx, a database extension that adds automatic differentiation in the style of JAX to standard SQL; and einfold, a modular query planner for fast tensor contractions.

The project is built on the thesis that separating logical layers in tensor programs from physical layers is both more correct and more scalable. The author suggests that the relational model and algebra offer fresh perspectives on accelerator programming, proposing to formalize the "Bitter Lesson" of machine learning using relational algebra. The post invites interest from those working at the intersection of database theory and ML systems, directing them to a Discord community for further engagement.
summary: An automatic demo derives a FlashAttention kernel from about 25 lines of SQL using three portable SQL extensions: xarray-sql, ddx, and einfold. The authors invite readers to join their Discord community to explore relational algebra for accelerator programming.

title: Rare meteorite from Mars gives us a view into its ancient crust
content:
A team of scientists led by Yang Liu of NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory has identified a third genuinely ancient Martian meteorite, Teghaza 001. Discovered in the Sahara Desert in Mali in 2022, the rock formed at least 4.1 billion years ago. This discovery adds to the limited number of known ancient Martian samples, which previously included Allan Hills 84001 from Antarctica and a rock from northwest Africa known as Black Beauty. The finding provides a new perspective on Mars’ ancient crust, as most other Martian meteorites on Earth are significantly younger, dating to 2.4 billion years or less.

Liu noted that the rarity of old Martian rocks on Earth may be due to the physical conditions required for a rock to leave the planet. A large impact is necessary to launch material into space, but not all rocks can survive such an event. Weak or loose material may fail to cement into a solid rock capable of overcoming Mars’ gravity. Consequently, the impact process itself acts as a natural filter, preventing weaker rocks from reaching Earth.
summary: Crater counts tell us that most of the Martian surface is more than 3 billion years old, but pieces of Mars we have on Earth tell a different story. The three main classes of Martian meteorites—shergottites, nakhlites, and chassignites—are all 2.4 billion years old or younger.
author: Ars Technica

title: DoorDash CEO: AI agents generate only several hundred orders per quarter
content: As AI tools and agents have continued their march across all aspects of digital life, many companies are trying to use LLMs to improve the experience of purchasing goods and services on the Internet. Thus far, though, a vanishingly small number of people seem to be taking advantage of those capabilities, at least when it comes to using the popular food delivery app DoorDash with an outside AI agent. In a third-quarter earnings call Thursday, DoorDash co-founder and CEO Tony Xu responded to an analyst question by noting that "AI agents are generating several hundred orders [on DoorDash] across the time that they've been up and running." In a marked understatement, Xu called this a "very low use case" for a company that handled just shy of 1 billion orders total in the third quarter of 2026 alone. Speaking generally, Xu said he sees the potential for AI agents to be genuinely helpful for "long consideration purchases" and major decisions where agents would be "doing work on your behalf proactively in the background." However, Xu added, "when it comes to a task that's as simple as ordering food, we tend to see that come directly to DoorDash." Read full article Comments
summary: DoorDash co-founder and CEO Tony Xu stated that AI agents have generated only several hundred orders for the platform since their launch. He described this as a very low use case compared to the nearly 1 billion total orders handled in the third quarter of 2026.

This week, Schnell discovered the depths of the problem himself as he resigned from the university after an advisory committee found that he failed to disclose significant AI use in an academic paper and in the Washington Post op-ed, even though publishers required such disclosure. Schnell didn't make it especially easy for the committee to investigate his AI use; the report uses the term "insufficient cooperation." He did turn over his Dartmouth laptop, but he did not turn over logs from his personal LLM accounts related to the writings in question. Nor did he agree to meet with the committee. The committee did get access to the Claude enterprise account Schnell had used through Dartmouth, though. This shows him using the LLM as a tool for revising his papers, finding and fixing bugs in code, and editing or generating figures. content: Boom Supersonic CEO Blake Scholl recently declared “it’s time for a renaissance in energy and in supersonic flight” as the supersonic airliner company unveiled a Colorado factory dedicated to making gas turbines for AI data centers. One of the company’s first customers, United Airlines CEO Scott Kirby, has expressed doubts about Boom’s original plan to deliver the first Overture supersonic airliner in 2029. title: Ars Staff Mourns Sir Patrick Stewart, Who Died at 86 in Los Angeles
content:
Ars staff is mourning the death of Sir Patrick Stewart, the award-winning actor renowned for his roles as Captain Jean-Luc Picard in Star Trek: The Next Generation and Professor Charles Xavier in the X-Men franchise. Stewart passed away yesterday at the age of 86. A statement from his representatives announced that he died at his home in Los Angeles while in the care of his wife, Sunny. The statement noted that Stewart had been undergoing a brief journey with Alzheimer’s Disease and Lewy Body Dementia, and that he was surrounded by family, friends, live music, and prayer at the time of his passing.

The family described Stewart as having inspired profound emotion through a lifetime of devotion, leaving behind an enduring reminder of his "invincible grace." In lieu of flowers, the family has requested that memorial contributions be directed to the Johns Hopkins Alzheimer’s Disease Research Center Fund and the Alzheimer’s Foundation of America Caregiver Resources. This request was shared through the actor’s X account.
summary: Sir Patrick Stewart, age 86, died yesterday at his home in Los Angeles after a brief journey with Alzheimer’s Disease and Lewy Body Dementia. His representatives requested memorial contributions to the Johns Hopkins Alzheimer’s Disease Research Center Fund and the Alzheimer’s Foundation of America Caregiver Resources.
author: Ars Technica

title: New World Screwworm Infestation Spreads to Arizona, 74 Animal Cases Reported
content:
The report notes that four dogs and a cat were attacked this week by flesh‑eating screwworms. The New World Screwworm (NWS) infestation has now spread to a third state, Arizona, joining New Mexico and Texas as the only U.S. states plagued by the parasites. Since the flies re‑invaded the country in June, authorities have identified 74 animal cases.

The flies lay hundreds of eggs in wounds and moist orifices of animals. The resulting maggots, which resemble screws, bore and twist into living flesh, causing severe and sometimes fatal wounds. After feeding, the maggots drop to the ground to develop into adult flies.

The infestation is described as a genuine fright this Halloween, with the maggots festering along the southern border and continuing to threaten pets in the affected states.
summary: New World Screwworm Infestation Spreads to Arizona, 74 Animal Cases Reported.

title: French port strikes may win better conditions, uncertain impact on militarisation
content:
Carys Garland welcomed Renaud Foucart, Senior Lecturer at the Department of Economics ECARES at Lancaster University, to discuss an international dockworkers’ strike that highlights the link between organized labor, technological change and Europe’s expanding military investment.

Foucart said port workers have a strategic position in global supply chains that gives them exceptional leverage, noting, “They know how powerful they are.” He questioned whether they could influence military policy, but expects the leverage to secure concessions on automation and working conditions, adding, “They can get those concessions. And I think they will get them.”
summary: Renaud Foucart, Senior Lecturer at the Department of Economics ECARES at Lancaster University, says the strategic position of French port workers in global supply chains gives them exceptional leverage during the international dockworkers’ strike. He expects they can secure concessions on automation and working conditions, but doubts they can curb Europe’s expanding military investment.

content:

content: Mary Peltola denies knowledge as party accused of recruiting spoiler candidate with same name as sitting Republican Alaska Senate race: what to know about Democrats’ alleged ballot-stacking effort The top federal prosecutor in Alaska confirmed on Friday the existence of a criminal and a civil investigation into an alleged scheme by Democrats to confuse voters by recruiting a spoiler candidate on the ballot for US Senate who shares a name with the Republican incumbent, senator Dan Sullivan. title: BP quarterly profit hits 18-year high of $8.46bn as Middle East war lifts oil prices
content: Oil giant comes under fire from climate campaigners, as its earnings reach $8.46bn while ‘innocent civilians suffer’ BP’s quarterly profits have been labelled “obscene” after they hit an 18-year high of $8.46bn (£6.3bn), as the war in the Middle East drove up oil and gas prices. The energy company hailed a “banner quarter” on Friday, with its underlying ​replacement ⁠cost profit – a key measure of its income – almost quadrupling in the three months to the end of September, from $2.2bn in the same period ​a year ​ago. The jump meant BP’s quarterly profits hit their highest level since the $8.9bn recorded in 2008.

title: Scotland and Wales leaders say local devolution decisions lie with Holyrood and Senedd
content:

Their comments came as a response to the prime minister’s proposal to extend English‑style regional powers across the United Kingdom.

Burnham met Swinney and ap Iorwerth in Glasgow to discuss powers for localised employment and reindustrialisation. Downing Street later described the discussion as constructive.
summary: John Swinney and Rhun ap Iorwerth told Andy Burnham that decisions on local devolution rest solely with the Scottish and Welsh parliaments, not Westminster. Downing Street described the Glasgow discussion on local employment and reindustrialisation powers as constructive.

title: On this day in space! Oct. 30, 1964: NASA's weird Lunar Landing Research Vehicle takes 1st test flight to help Apollo astronauts land on the moon
content: On October 30, 1964, NASA's Lunar Landing Research Vehicle, or LLRV, took to the skies for the first time. The LLRV was a bizarre, four-legged flying contraption commonly known as the "Flying Bedstead." NASA used it to simulate moon landings and liftoffs on Earth to prepare for Apollo 11, the first crewed lunar landing. The first person to give it a whirl was the X-15 pilot Joe Walker. During this test flight, he reached an altitude of about 10 feet, and he hovered there for about a minute. He did this two more times that same day. In all, he completed more than 30 test flights with the LLRV. These test flights took place at NASA's Dryden Flight Research Center in Edwards, California. That facility has since been renamed the Armstrong Flight Research Center after Neil Armstrong, who also piloted — and famously crashed — the "Flying Bedstead" before he went to the moon. The first Lunar Landing Research Vehicle is pictured during a test flight at NASA's Dryden Flight Research Center in California. (Image credit: NASA) Why it mattered Over 60 years ago this LLRV test flight was a critical step toward landing humans on the moon for the first time, a historic moment that both served an important political purpose while also showcasing the result of monumental scientific and technical progress. While images from this test flight might look like the team are having a bit of fun out in the desert, and perhaps they were, it was also deadly serious. The astronauts who signed onto these crewed missions were doing something that had never been attempted. They were putting their lives on the line for this progress, and this testing was a major piece in reassuring them and NASA that lunar landing could be accomplished, and safely. Today, as we return humans to the moon with NASA's Artemis program, we see parallels between testing done over 60 years ago and testing today. Right now, SpaceX and Blue Origin are testing their lunar landers for crewed lunar landings in the near-future. While we have now been to the moon and have safely and successfully landed humans before, these tests remain critical for the safety and success of the missions. Want more space history? Check out our full On This Day In Space Story archive and watch our On This Day In Space videos on YouTube.
summary: On October 30, 1964, NASA's Lunar Landing Research Vehicle, or LLRV, took to the skies for the first time. The LLRV was a bizarre, four-legged flying contraption commonly known as the "Flying Bedstead." NASA used it to simulate moon landings and liftoffs on Earth to prepare for Apollo 11, the first crewed lunar landing.

title: A Few Good Men review – Aaron Sorkin’s legal drama makes unwelcome return to stage
content:
Aaron Sorkin’s 1989 courtroom drama, A Few Good Men, has returned to the Broadway stage at Lincoln Center’s Vivian Beaumont theater in New York City. The revival features a retooled version of the classic play, which centers on a cocky military attorney defending two young marines who followed an illegal order with fatal results. The production’s reception has been mixed, with critics noting that unconvincing performances and an ill-fitting big stage have made the current iteration feel like a missed opportunity.

The narrative explores the tension between critiquing a hallowed institution and imbuing it with dignity, a theme comparable to how Sorkin’s The West Wing portrayed the Oval Office. The story is set at the US military base at Guantánamo Bay, where a marine has died under troubling circumstances. Colonel Jessep, the hardliner in command, serves as the ultimate enemy to the protagonist, navy lawyer Daniel Kaffee.

The source suggests that audiences seeking crackling drama and sentimentality about the military would be better served by watching the 1992 film adaptation rather than purchasing tickets to the stage production. Directed by Rob Reiner, the movie is described as a clever, old-fashioned crowd pleaser that received an Oscar nomination. It starred Tom Cruise as Kaffee and Jack Nicholson as Jessep, with the film culminating in a classic trial scene featuring the memorable line, “You can’t handle the truth!”
summary: A Few Good Men review – Aaron Sorkin’s legal drama makes unwelcome return to stage.

title: Sampa the Great: Nu Zamrock review – a full-circle moment for a world-class act
content:
Sampa Tembo, known professionally as Sampa the Great, has released her third album, Nu Zamrock, which is described as a genre-hopping record that meets the moment with charisma and cheek. The project marks a full-circle moment for the world-class act, reflecting her journey after returning to Africa to live and record.

Tembo’s career began in Australia, where she was based between 2013 and 2019. During that period, she achieved significant recognition, becoming the first woman to win an Australian Recording Industry Association award for hip-hop or rap in 2019. She is also noted as the first and only person to win the Australian music prize twice.

Despite her accolades in Australia, Tembo has consistently emphasized her Zambian birth and Botswana upbringing. In a 2022 interview with the Guardian, she explained that she was frequently misidentified as Australian, which compelled her to actively defend Zambian music and culture. She noted that her background in Botswana and the music she heard while growing up there were often overlooked in these discussions.
summary: Sampa the Great: Nu Zamrock review – a full-circle moment for a world-class act.

title: Patrick Stewart, Star Trek and X-Men actor, dies at 86
content:
Patrick Stewart has died at the age of 86. The actor was widely recognized for bringing gravitas and complexity to the screen, particularly through his roles as Jean-Luc Picard in Star Trek and Charles Xavier in the X-Men franchise. His Shakespearean training and sonorous voice established him as a unique charismatic force in Hollywood.

Stewart was a member of the Royal Shakespeare Company’s 1970s stage generation and had previously held small screen roles, including an intimidating portrayal of Sejanus in I, Claudius opposite Derek Jacobi. He achieved significant pop culture stardom by securing the role of Captain Jean-Luc Picard, the leader of the Federation starship USS Enterprise, in Star Trek: The Next Generation. The series, which served as a reboot of the original Star Trek, ran from 1987 to 1994 and spawned four feature films and a subsequent series, Star Trek: Picard.

Colleagues such as William Shatner have paid tribute to Stewart, noting that he stood for the best of humanity. His career demonstrated the commercial potential of British classical training in American cinema and television, showcasing the technique and style of Shakespearean actors within the industry.
summary: Patrick Stewart has died at the age of 86, leaving behind a legacy that included iconic roles as Jean-Luc Picard and Charles Xavier. His Shakespearean training and distinctive voice established him as a charismatic force in Hollywood, bridging British classical theater with American pop culture.

title: SCTV: The Canadian Sketch Show That Launched Stars and Influenced The Simpsons
content:
SCTV, short for Second City Television, is described as one of the most influential comedy shows ever created, having launched the careers of Eugene Levy, Catherine O’Hara, and John Candy. The Canadian sketch series, which aired in the 1970s and 1980s, is noted for influencing The Simpsons and maintaining a dedicated following among comedy enthusiasts, even while Saturday Night Live held mainstream popularity in North America. The show was characterized by its weird, dark, and multilayered style, which was considered years ahead of its time.

Dave Thomas, an original cast member and head writer who was present from the start, discussed the show’s unique approach to humor. He recalled that Conan O’Brien once stated he believed the show was written specifically for him because it contained references O’Brien was certain only he understood. Thomas explained that the writers created content at the top of their reference level, with the intention of seeing if the audience would meet them at that intellectual height.
summary: The Canadian sketch show SCTV influenced The Simpsons and launched the careers of actors including Eugene Levy, Catherine O’Hara, and John Candy. Head writer Dave Thomas stated that the show was written at a high reference level, which Conan O’Brien later said felt specifically tailored for him.

title: Chancellor allocates £7m to study northern England Olympic bid
content:
The article notes that the Prime Minister, known for his love of sport, is prepared to risk a north‑south rift over the prospect of hosting table tennis in Teesside.  

During this week’s budget day, the chancellor of the exchequer announced a £7 million allocation to explore a possible Olympic bid for the north of England. The author admits a limited grasp of the country’s finances, but points out that this sum is only a preliminary step and a small fraction of the cost of a full bid; Tokyo and Paris each spent more than £50 million on theirs.  

The earmarked money has already sparked speculation about future events, with some imagining beach volleyball in Morecambe Bay or a British eight rowing to victory along the Tyne.
summary: The chancellor of the exchequer allocated £7 million to assess a possible Olympic bid for the north of England. The funding, far smaller than the more than £50 million spent by Tokyo and Paris, has sparked ideas such as beach volleyball in Morecambe Bay and a British eight rowing on the Tyne.

title: Putellas' arrival boosts London City Lionesses ahead of Manchester City match
content: Ballon d’Or winner’s move to WSL has transformed the Lionesses on and off the pitch with belief soaring ahead of Manchester City clash As Martin Semmens, the London City Lionesses chief executive, sits down is his office he looks like the cat that got the cream. He says he has just learned that the club’s Instagram page has generated 34m hits since Alexia Putellas won the Ballon d’Or on Monday evening, and it is only Thursday afternoon. On Sunday, two clubs with seven of the top 30 players in the Ballon d’Or rankings will go head-to-head when Manchester City visit Hayes Lane, Bromley. It is, Semmens, says, “awesome for the WSL”. From the outside, it can feel slightly surreal. The independent women’s club, owned by the businesswoman Michele Kang, are third in the top flight, two‑and‑a‑half years after finishing eighth in tier two, and Semmens believes signing the world’s best player has helped change the mindset of everyone at the club.
summary: London City Lionesses chief executive Martin Semmens says Ballon d'Or winner Alexia Putellas has transformed the club's mindset. The team is third in the WSL and will face Manchester City, with both clubs possessing seven of the top 30 Ballon d'Or ranked players.

title: Jack Grealish dropped from Everton squad after breach of club discipline
content: After being dropped for ‘a breach of club discipline’, the winger must face the same questions about respect and self-awareness For the biggest game in Manchester City’s history, Jack Grealish was given a starting berth while Phil Foden, Julián Alvarez and Riyad Mahrez were on the bench. Grealish played the full 90 minutes of the Champions League triumph against Inter because Pep Guardiola had the greatest faith in the attacking midfielder, but three years on he is at risk of being yesterday’s man. That trust dwindled, not helped by injuries, and Grealish made only 17 Premier League starts over the next two seasons under Guardiola. City wanted him to leave in the summer of 2025, and Everton provided the solution, taking him on loan and borrowing him again for this season. Six Everton appearances into this campaign he was left out of the squad for Thursday’s Carabao Cup win against Newcastle after missing training on Monday. Everton went public with the fact that there had been “ a breach of club discipline ”.
summary: Jack Grealish was left out of Everton's squad for their Carabao Cup win against Newcastle after missing training on Monday. The club publicly confirmed that his omission was due to a breach of club discipline.

title: Study: Wildlife trade involves twice as many species as previously estimated
content:
A study published in Science Advances reveals that the number of plant and animal species involved in the global wildlife trade is more than twice as high as previously estimated. The research indicates that over 100,000 species are currently traded, encompassing illegal smuggling, ornamental sales, and industries including fisheries, timber, and fashion.

The authors warn that significant gaps exist in global assessments of wildlife trade, noting that past estimates have failed to account for recent developments. Specifically, the study highlights the rapid expansion of the online exotic pet trade, where sellers can easily offer to ship spider eggs internationally or facilitate the clandestine transport of reptiles on aircraft.
summary: A study published in Science Advances found that more than 100,000 species are traded globally, a figure more than double previous estimates. Researchers warn that past assessments have failed to account for the growth of the online exotic pet trade.

title: Iran war drives US heating oil bills up 50% as winter approaches
content:
Mark Wolfe argues that the war in Iran is exacerbating the United States’ energy affordability crisis, with heating oil serving as a primary indicator of the growing strain. According to Wolfe, families relying on oil for home heating face potential winter bills that are 50% higher, adding approximately $900 to the cost of keeping their homes warm. This significant increase compounds existing financial pressures on households that were already struggling before the conflict began.

Wolfe highlights research conducted by his organization, previously reported by The Guardian, which found that electricity shutoffs in ten states rose by 28% over the last two years. Millions of Americans have been falling behind on utility bills, forcing difficult choices between paying for energy, food, medicine, and rent. The current situation presents these households with another round of rising costs for gasoline, electricity, and home heating. In response, Wolfe calls on Congress to take action to ensure families can afford to heat their homes before the winter season starts.
summary: Families using oil for home heating face bills that could be 50% higher this winter, adding nearly $900 to their costs. Mark Wolfe urges Congress to act to ensure families can afford to heat their homes before the season begins.

Glioblastoma (GBM), the most common malignant primary brain tumor in adults, is characterized as one of the most aggressive and deadly forms of cancer. The condition presents significant surgical challenges because the tumor often extends microscopic "tentacles" into healthy brain tissue, making complete removal difficult. Additionally, GBM is resistant to therapy due to its ability to create an immunosuppressive microenvironment that helps the cancer evade immune attacks.

summary: Glioblastoma is the most common malignant primary brain tumor in adults and is difficult to treat due to its microscopic tentacles and immunosuppressive microenvironment. The development of space-grown glioblastoma organoids could help advance treatments for this aggressive cancer.

title: Study finds host protein albumin fuels inflammation in vaginal yeast infections
content:
Up to three‑quarters of women will experience a genital yeast infection at least once, and recurrent cases can markedly affect quality of life. While symptoms such as itching, burning and pain stem from the yeast Candida albicans, they are driven largely by an excessive immune response.  

An international research team led by the Leibniz‑HKI has identified that the host protein albumin amplifies the inflammatory cascade and concurrently protects the fungal pathogen from immune attack. The study detailing this mechanism was published in Nature Communications.
summary: An international research team led by the Leibniz-HKI discovered that the host protein albumin drives the inflammatory cascade in vaginal yeast infections. The protein also shields Candida albicans from the immune system, and the findings were published in Nature Communications.

title: Tech sell-off erases nearly $1tn from Nasdaq after weak earnings
content:

The decline has reduced the value of the tech-heavy Nasdaq exchange by nearly $1 trillion in one week and erased approximately $2 trillion in a month. Investors are reportedly questioning whether the billions of dollars being invested in artificial intelligence can generate returns quickly enough.

The S&P 500, an index of the 500 most valuable US companies, fell by more than 1% on Friday, losing hundreds of billions in market value. Despite setting an all-time high during October, the index is on track to erase its gains for the month. The weakness in technology stocks dragged the Nasdaq composite down by more than 3%, further erasing hundreds of billions in value. Meanwhile, the Dow Jones Industrial Average experienced a smaller decline.
summary: Disappointing earnings from leading tech companies drove US markets down by hundreds of billions of dollars, wiping nearly $1tn from the Nasdaq in one week. The S&P 500 fell by more than 1% and the Nasdaq composite dropped over 3% as investors questioned returns on AI investments.

title: Iberian copper mines linked to Late Bronze Age trade reaching Scandinavia
content:
New research published in the journal Antiquity suggests that mines in modern-day Spain and Portugal were a significant source of copper during the Late Bronze Age. The study indicates that copper from these Iberian sites traveled extensive distances, with some material reaching as far as Scandinavia. This finding highlights the region’s potential role in broader Bronze Age trade networks.

Copper is essential for producing bronze, which shaped tools, weapons, and ornaments across Europe. While many Bronze Age mines have been identified, researchers continue to determine which sites were most active at specific times and how far their resources were distributed.
summary: New research in Antiquity suggests that mines in modern-day Spain and Portugal were an important source of copper during the Late Bronze Age. Copper from these sites was found as far away as Scandinavia, highlighting Iberia's role in Bronze Age trade networks.
author: Phys.org

title: University of Southampton historian reveals 17th-century witchcraft trials
content: University of Southampton historian research reveals that in one English city approximately 400 years ago, individuals functioning as magical equivalents to modern private investigators were prosecuted for witchcraft and wizardry.
summary: Research by a University of Southampton historian indicates that magical private investigators were prosecuted in an English city 400 years ago. These individuals were found on the wrong side of the law for witchcraft and wizardry.

title: Global wildlife trade involves over 107,000 species, double prior estimates
content: New research indicates that over 107,000 species are used and traded globally, a figure more than double previous estimates. The study suggests the actual scale is likely even larger due to significant gaps in available wildlife trade and collection data.
summary: New research finds more than 107,000 species are used and traded worldwide, more than double previous estimates. The study suggests the true scale may be far greater because of major gaps in trade and wildlife collection data.

title: Kuopio University examines dissertation on deep learning air quality monitoring
content: A doctoral dissertation by Andrea Porcheddu, MSc in Technical Physics, will be examined at the Faculty of Science, Forestry and Technology, Kuopio campus. The work focuses on deep learning–enhanced air quality monitoring using satellite data.
summary: A doctoral dissertation by Andrea Porcheddu, who holds an MSc in Technical Physics, will be examined at the Faculty of Science, Forestry and Technology. The work is conducted at the Kuopio campus and focuses on deep learning-enhanced air quality monitoring using satellite data.

title: Drone-based AI system tracks cattle growth without stressful trips to scales
content: Determining the optimal time to sell beef cattle is critical for managing producer costs, as animals cease significant weight gain upon reaching their natural growth limit. Continuing to hold cattle in a feedlot beyond this point results in feed expenses without corresponding meat production.
summary: A drone-based AI system tracks cattle growth to help producers determine the ideal time to sell. This method avoids stressful trips to scales and prevents costs associated with feeding animals past their natural growth limit.

title: Rediscovered 1935 recordings reveal earliest known spoken audio of endangered Louisiana Creole
content: The earliest spoken-word recordings of Louisiana Creole, a language at risk of extinction, have been uncovered and analyzed for the first time. These 1935 recordings reveal the unique American tongue that defined the docks and saloons of New Orleans for well over a century.
summary: Rediscovered 1935 recordings reveal earliest known spoken audio of endangered Louisiana Creole.

title: Rusty crust may have kept Mars warm enough for flowing water
content: A new hypothesis suggests that rust located beneath the surface may explain how Mars once became warm enough to permit water flow. This idea addresses the unresolved question of how and why the planet achieved temperatures suitable for surface water.
summary: A new theory suggests that rust below the surface helped make Mars warm enough to allow water to flow. It remains unclear how and why the planet became warm enough to support surface water.
author: New Scientist

title: Scientists Confirm Global Warming Accelerated to 0.35°C Per Decade Since 2015
content: Scientists have confirmed that global warming is accelerating faster than ever recorded, with a major increase in temperature rise detected since around 2015. A new study indicates the warming rate has surged to approximately 0.35°C per decade, nearly double the average pace from 1970 to 2015. After accounting for natural climate fluctuations, researchers verified this acceleration with over 98% statistical confidence.
summary: A new study reveals that the global warming rate has surged to approximately 0.35°C per decade since around 2015. Researchers confirmed this acceleration with more than 98% statistical confidence after removing natural climate fluctuations.
author: Science Daily

title: UC San Diego study links chronic back pain to brain's self-awareness network
content:
Researchers at UC San Diego have discovered that chronic lower back pain may become integrated into the brain’s sense of personal identity. Their findings indicate that movement-triggered pain activates a brain network linked to self-awareness and memories, a response that contrasts with ordinary acute pain, which typically suppresses this network.

This distinction offers a potential explanation for why standard pain medications often yield limited relief for chronic conditions. Furthermore, the activation of these self-referential networks may account for how fear, anticipation, and past experiences can intensify the perception of chronic pain.
summary: Researchers at UC San Diego found that chronic lower back pain activates a brain network associated with self-awareness, unlike acute pain which shuts it down. This discovery may explain why conventional medications offer limited relief and why fear and past experiences can intensify the condition.
author: Science Daily

title: Astronomers rule out giant planets in nearby 16‑light‑year binary, habitability still possible
content: Astronomers have resolved a 170-year-old mystery in a nearby two-star system located 16 light-years from Earth. They determined that a previously observed wobble was caused by stellar activity rather than a giant planet. While Jupiter-sized worlds have been ruled out in key regions, smaller, potentially habitable planets may still exist in the system.
summary: Astronomers have solved a 170‑year‑old planetary mystery in a nearby two‑star system, finding that a mysterious wobble was caused by stellar activity rather than a giant planet. While Jupiter‑sized worlds have been ruled out in key regions, smaller potentially habitable planets could still be awaiting discovery 16 light‑years from Earth.
author: Science Daily

title: Scientists find hidden aggressive cells in lower‑risk rhabdomyosarcoma tumors
content: Scientists discovered hidden aggressive cancer cells in children whose tumors were previously considered lower‑risk, explaining why some rhabdomyosarcoma cases become unexpectedly deadly. The finding may help doctors detect dangerous tumors earlier and develop personalized treatments that improve survival while reducing unnecessary chemotherapy.
summary: Scientists have uncovered hidden aggressive cancer cells in children whose tumors were previously considered lower risk, revealing why some cases of rhabdomyosarcoma become unexpectedly deadly. The discovery could help doctors identify dangerous tumors earlier and develop personalized treatments that improve survival while reducing unnecessary chemotherapy.
author: Science Daily

title: NASA Explores Potential Commercial Servicing for Hubble Telescope
content:
NASA issued a Request for Information (RFI) on October 29 to assess industry capabilities for in-space servicing of the Hubble Space Telescope. The agency seeks to identify commercial options that could extend the telescope’s operational life or support its end-of-life procedures. NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman stated that Hubble has significant science ahead and that the agency should explore every reasonable opportunity to keep it delivering for as long as possible. He emphasized that if innovative and cost-effective methods exist to extend the life of an asset already in orbit, it is a duty to the American taxpayer and the scientific community to investigate them.

The RFI specifically seeks commercial interest in three potential mission profiles: boosting Hubble to a higher altitude to extend its science lifetime, servicing the telescope to enhance its capabilities, or performing a safe, controlled re-entry into Earth’s atmosphere or orbital disposal at the end of its mission. Nicky Fox, associate administrator of the Science Mission Directorate at NASA Headquarters in Washington, noted that Hubble is a national icon that has changed how humanity views the universe for more than 35 years. Fox highlighted the rapid evolution of the commercial industry in offering new capabilities for in-space satellite capture and servicing, stating that NASA is eager to explore possibilities to boost Hubble to a higher orbit while developing the flagship mission to follow.

Technical constraints drive the urgency of these efforts. Like all spacecraft in low Earth orbit, Hubble’s altitude is slowly decreasing due to atmospheric drag because the telescope lacks a propulsion system to maintain its own orbit. Analysis predicts that Hubble is likely to re-enter the atmosphere between 2033 and 2034. Consequently, NASA anticipates that any servicing or boosting mission would need to take place by 2032. The RFI remains open for responses until 3 p.m. EST on Monday, November 30, and is available online.

The Hubble Space Telescope has been operating for more than three decades and continues to make discoveries that shape the fundamental understanding of the universe. It is a project of international cooperation between NASA and the European Space Agency (ESA). NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center in Greenbelt, Maryland, manages the telescope and mission operations, with support from Lockheed Martin Space, based in Denver. The Space Telescope Science Institute in Baltimore, operated by the Association of Universities for Research in Astronomy, conducts Hubble science operations for NASA.
summary: The Hubble Space Telescope returns to orbit as an improved telescope after its second servicing mission in February 1997. NASA NASA issued a Request for Information Oct.
author: NASA News

title: NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope Captures Eerie Cat’s Head
content:
NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope released a mid-infrared image of the Cat’s Head Nebula on October 29, 2026. The image, processed by Joseph DePasquale at STScI, reveals intricate structures within the nebula. According to the release, the distinctive feline shape was likely sculpted by intense ultraviolet radiation and winds from massive stars in the Carina Nebula.

As this stellar feedback erodes surrounding gas and dust, denser material within the pillar resists erosion. The image was credited to NASA, ESA, CSA, and STScI.
summary: NASA, ESA, CSA, STScI; Image Processing: Joseph DePasquale (STScI) Intricate structures within the Cat’s Head Nebula are illuminated in this mid-infrared view from NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope released on Oct. 29, 2026.
author: NASA News

title: Google's Fourth-Gen Nest Learning Thermostat Drops to $219.99 at Major Retailers
content:
Google’s fourth-generation Nest Learning Thermostat is currently available for $219.99 at Amazon, Best Buy, and The Home Depot. This price represents a $60 discount from the regular cost of $279.99 and matches the product’s best price of the year, sitting just $10 above its all-time low. The sale applies to all three available colors of the device.

The latest model is described as Google’s most capable thermostat to date, featuring capabilities designed to reduce energy consumption while maintaining comfort. Similar to previous versions, the device learns user heating and cooling preferences over time to automatically generate schedules based on habits. It can suggest schedule modifications to save energy and adjusts temperatures automatically when occupants are away from home. The package includes a remote temperature sensor, allowing users to optimize the climate in specific rooms such as the bedroom.

The fourth-generation thermostat features an adaptive display that presents temperature settings, weather, and time from a distance. When a user approaches the device, the screen reveals additional details, including outdoor air quality and humidity levels. The device is Matter-ready and supports more HVAC systems than the third-generation model. It is also compatible with various humidifiers, dehumidifiers, and ventilation equipment. Unlike many smart thermostats, it does not require a C-wire in most homes, although using one can help ensure consistent power.

Other discounted smart home and tech items are also on sale. The black Casio WS-B1000 digital watch is priced at $23.88 at Amazon and Walmart, a $41 reduction that marks its best price to date. This retro-style watch includes basic fitness tracking features such as a step counter, Bluetooth connectivity for syncing activity data, a stopwatch, and alarms, but lacks advanced health sensors and contactless payment capabilities.

Apple’s second-generation AirTag is available in a four-pack for $69.99 at Amazon, Best Buy, and Walmart, which is a $30 discount and the lowest price observed. This AirTag model is noted for precise tracking that can guide users to lost items, with location sharing capabilities for Apple Watch Series 9 or later and participating airlines like United and Delta.

SwitchBot’s 12-inch RGBICWW Ceiling Light is available for $36.99 at Amazon with a coupon, or directly from SwitchBot using code HWHW26. This Matter-compatible light offers 26 preset scenes and eight lighting effects. A 15-inch version is also discounted, with the primary difference being brightness; the 15-inch model provides up to 3,200 lumens, whereas the 12-inch model delivers 2,000 lumens.
summary: Google's fourth-gen Nest Learning Thermostat is currently available for $219.99, a $60 discount from its regular price. The sale is available at Amazon, Best Buy, and The Home Depot, matching the device's best price of the year.
author: The Verge

title: Vizio Mini LED Quantum TV discounted at Walmart with option to disable smart OS
content:
Walmart is currently offering discounts on the Vizio Mini LED Quantum TV, with the 65-inch model priced at $358 and the 85-inch model at $698. These prices represent savings of $40 and $100, respectively, off their original retail values. While the article primarily highlights these two sizes, it also lists a 55-inch model available for $248, down from $278.

A key feature of this television is the ability to bypass its built-in smart features. Although the TV ships with Vizio OS, users can disable the operating system during the setup process by pushing past manufacturer warnings about missing out on smart TV capabilities. This allows consumers to use external streaming devices, such as a Roku or Apple TV 4K, without engaging with the TV’s internal software or associated data collection practices.

In terms of performance, the Vizio Mini LED Quantum TV utilizes quantum dots and a mini-LED panel to deliver vivid colors and high brightness. Testing indicated that the set can reach 936 nits when calibrated. However, the IPS panel has limitations, including black levels that are not as deep as those found on more expensive sets and some motion blur during fast-paced scenes.

The television includes three HDMI ports, all of which are version 2.0. Despite this, the limitation is not considered detrimental to the user experience because the screen only supports a maximum resolution of 4K at 60Hz. The Vizio Mini LED Quantum TV offers a bright image for a low price point, though it requires some compromises in contrast and motion handling.
summary: The Vizio Mini LED Quantum TV is discounted at Walmart, with the 65-inch model priced at $358 and the 85-inch model at $698. Users can bypass the built-in Vizio OS during setup to use their own streaming devices, though the IPS panel has limited black levels and motion blur.

title: Apple returns to gadget experimentation with touchscreen MacBook and new iPhone screens
content:
Apple is entering a period of gadget experimentation, featuring new features such as additional iPhone screens, a touchscreen MacBook, and CarPlay apps on HomeView. The Vergecast hosts David and Nilay discuss these developments, noting that while the results are not always perfect, it is enjoyable to see the company try new things.

Nilay specifically debates the merits of a touchscreen laptop and states that he intends to purchase the new MacBook Pro equipped with the PROLED XDR Display. The episode highlights Apple’s approach to innovation, which in this instance involves adding a touch panel to the new MacBook Pro to test user engagement.
summary: Apple is in a period of unabashed gadget experimentation, introducing features like a touchscreen MacBook Pro and more iPhone screens. The Vergecast hosts David and Nilay debate the merits of these new hardware additions.
