title: Starbucks CEO Says Company Will Explore AI Personalized Drive-Thru Menus
content:
Starbucks CEO Brian Niccol stated on Thursday’s earnings call that the company plans to explore technologies that recognize participating customers at the drive-thru. He noted these systems could present personalized digital menus and streamline the payment process. The remarks were initially reported by More Perfect Union.

Niccol’s description aligns with similar initiatives by other fast-food chains. Taco Bell is currently testing technology that modifies digital menu board layouts, content, and visuals for each approaching vehicle. Additionally, McDonald’s has recently demonstrated an AI-powered feature it is piloting at a limited number of drive-thru locations.
summary: Starbucks CEO Brian Niccol stated on an earnings call that the company will explore experiences that recognize customers and present personalized digital menus. This initiative aims to make payment more effortless at the drive-thru.
author: The Verge

title: Google satellite AI server transmits first response from space
content: Google's AI chip-equipped satellite has generated its first response from space. In a blog post on Friday, Google says it successfully booted up the satellite's Tensor Processing Units (TPUs), allowing the on-board Gemma 4 model to follow through on a prompt to create a haiku about being in space: Blue marble below Data streams in silent grace Starlight feeds my core. ✨ Google says it tried out other space-themed limericks and telemetry prompts as well. The test is part of Google's Project Suncatcher, an experimental initiative that could eventually put AI data centers in space. Google launched the satellite into orbit earlier this …
summary: Google's AI chip-equipped satellite successfully booted its Tensor Processing Units and generated its first response from orbit. The on-board Gemma 4 model produced a space-themed haiku, and Google also tested other limericks and telemetry prompts as part of Project Suncatcher.
author: The Verge

title: Binance suspends withdrawals after $6.3 billion crypto hack
content:
Binance has suspended all withdrawals following what appears to be the largest cryptocurrency heist in history. The world’s largest crypto exchange reported an estimated total impact of approximately $6.3 billion. Of this amount, roughly $3 billion in affected assets, primarily stablecoins, was frozen.

However, analysts at Elliptic stated that the attacker converted about $3.3 billion into digital assets that cannot be frozen. The attacker is reportedly working to cash out these assets as traditional currency.
summary: Binance suspends withdrawals after $6.3 billion crypto hack.
author: Ars Technica

title: GM to pay $220 million settlement for selling Smart Driver data
content:
General Motors has agreed to pay $220 million to settle a lawsuit brought by the District of Columbia and 35 states. The legal action followed revelations in 2024 that GM shared customer data from its Smart Driver system with data brokers. The brokers subsequently sold this information to insurance companies, leading some drivers to report increased insurance costs despite claiming they had not consented to such data sharing.

Prior to this settlement, GM and its OnStar subsidiary reached an agreement with the Federal Trade Commission, which was finalized in January of this year. That FTC settlement prohibited the companies from sharing geolocation and driver behavior data with third parties for five years. Concurrently with the FTC agreement, GM discontinued the Smart Driver system across its entire vehicle range. The new settlement with the states resolves their separate lawsuit against the automaker regarding the sale of customer data.
summary: General Motors has agreed to pay $220 million to the District of Columbia and 35 states after they sued the company over the sale of Smart Driver data. The settlement follows a prior FTC agreement that banned GM and OnStar from sharing geolocation and driver behavior data for five years.
author: Ars Technica

title: Quilty Space: Global rocket launch shortage more severe than anticipated
content:
A new report from analytics firm Quilty Space indicates that the world, excluding China, faces a significant rocket shortage over the next five years. The firm estimates a shortfall of approximately 150 launches between now and 2030 relative to demand from satellite operators and civil space agencies. This deficit could double if US military demand is included and SpaceX does not extend its Falcon 9 and Falcon Heavy programs to meet increased national security needs.

Caleb Henry, director of research at Quilty Space, stated that the analysis aimed to determine the severity and resolution timeline of the launch crisis. Henry noted that the crisis is more severe than previously thought and will not resolve within the current decade. He added that the shortage might not abate until the late 2030s.
summary: The analytics firm Quilty Space estimates a shortfall of about 150 launches between now and 2030, excluding China. The crisis is expected to persist until the late 2030s, with the shortage potentially doubling if US military demand is included.
author: Ars Technica

title: DOJ charges five in ghost student crackdown, seizes $750k crypto linked to Kenyan nationals
content: The US has charged five individuals as part of the first broad federal crackdown on “ghost students”—fraudsters who steal the identities of hundreds of Americans to pose as fake college students and steal student loans. In a press release Thursday, the Department of Justice said it had uncovered a large-scale scheme relying partly on AI. The DOJ seized more than $750,000 in cryptocurrency from “a network associated with Kenyan nationals" after data analysis helped flag likely fraudsters. Assistant Attorney General Colin M. McDonald of the DOJ’s National Fraud Enforcement Division credited new fraud-detection measures implemented by the Trump administration for the arrests. He said that “this is the first international seizure of its kind in Kenya,” while warning fraudsters that the crackdown has only just begun. “If you steal American identities, if you steal taxpayer dollars, if you exploit programs meant to help students build a future—we will find you,” McDonald said. “Whether you are in Nebraska, New Jersey, Virginia, or Nairobi, we will pursue you.” Read full article Comments
summary: The US has charged five individuals as part of the first broad federal crackdown on “ghost students”—fraudsters who steal the identities of hundreds of Americans to pose as fake college students and steal student loans. In a press release Thursday, the Department of Justice said it had uncovered a large-scale scheme relying partly on AI.
author: Ars Technica

title: Fujifilm to boost tape production 5x as AI fuels archiving demand
content:
Fujifilm announced on Thursday that it will invest approximately 10 billion yen, or about $63 million, to expand its magnetic tape production capacity by fivefold. The company stated that this expansion is driven by increased archiving demand resulting from the spread of generative AI, which Fujifilm noted is causing "exponential growth" in global data needs. The new production capacity will be measured against fiscal year 2025 levels.

The investment is focused on Fujifilm’s Kanagawa Factory in Odawara, which the company described as the largest investment it has made to date in dedicated LTO tape facilities. The project is scheduled to run from fiscal years 2026 through 2028. Funds will be used for manufacturing expansion and the hiring of additional personnel, with the primary goal of producing the latest-generation "FUJIFILM LTO Ultrium10" tape.
summary: Fujifilm to boost tape production 5x as AI fuels archiving demand.
author: Ars Technica

title: Survival experts advise buying wind‑up radio and chocolate for emergencies
content:
UK survival experts are advising households to stock essentials like wind-up radios and chocolate to prepare for emergencies. This guidance aligns with the government’s “Be Ready” campaign, which launched in October to help citizens prepare for potential disruptions such as floods, power cuts, and cyber-attacks. The initiative includes a specific list of recommended items to keep at home, encouraging people to consider practical readiness measures.

While opinions vary on the extent of necessary preparation, from keeping extra tins of beans to maintaining comprehensive kits, specialists emphasize the importance of having reliable power sources and sustenance. The campaign aims to address the growing public focus on being practically ready for unexpected events, providing clear directives on what supplies are most helpful during critical situations.
summary: UK government launched its Be Ready campaign in October, providing guidance and a list of suggested emergency items. Survival experts recommend having a wind‑up radio, chocolate, power banks, extra tins of beans, or a full prepper’s kit at home.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Union leader’s billionaire tax idea becomes defining issue of California midterms
content:
A union leader’s initial proposal for a one-time 5% billionaire tax in California has evolved into a defining issue for the state’s midterms. What began as a bold response to Donald Trump’s healthcare cuts has transformed into one of the most contentious ballot measure fights in state history. The measure is now attracting national attention from political heavyweights and hundreds of millions of dollars in opposition from Silicon Valley.

The tax proposal has intensified internal conflicts, pitting Democrats against Democrats as the state’s super-rich mobilize in strong opposition. Californians are set to vote on the measure, marking a significant shift from its origins as a desperate policy answer to a major political battleground.
summary: California voters will decide on a one‑time 5% billionaire tax that was originally proposed by a union leader. The measure has sparked a heated ballot fight, drawing national attention and massive Silicon Valley opposition, and was framed as a response to Donald Trump’s healthcare cuts.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Ghost Hunters Amy Waine and Jarrad Cutting Release First AI Ghost Hunting Tool
content: Ghost hunting has changed in recent years due to AI chatbots, and paranormal enthusiasts are concerned Ghost hunting is a tech-heavy pursuit. When Amy Waine and Jarrad Cutting investigate haunted locations, they’re loaded up with software of their own design, such as an app that assigns signals from a phone’s sensors to different words in a database. In the age of ChatGPT, the ghost-hunting pair is probing the world of AI. They describe one of their latest inventions, an app called GhostTube Seer, as “the world’s first AI Ghost Hunting tool”. In the hands of paranormal investigators, scientific tools like EMF meters (used to detect electromagnetic fields) are repurposed to identify changes and anomalies that they believe indicate supernatural activity. Seer is, in many ways, simply an expansion of that practice, another way to scan an empty room and believe that something may be there. The app, which requires a paid monthly subscription, has more than 1m downloads, according to its Google Play store listing. But for others in the ghost hunting world, AI is an unwelcome presence. Since the release of ChatGPT in 2022, AI-generated ghost stories and images of the supernatural have flooded online spaces, so much so that popular forums like the r/Nosleep subreddit, meant for scary stories, have implemented a strict policy against AI-generated material.
summary: Ghost Hunters Amy Waine and Jarrad Cutting Release First AI Ghost Hunting Tool.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Christa Pike survived failed execution after two doses of pentobarbital
content: Pike survived two doses of pentobarbital during her attempted execution on 30 September. She was sentenced to death for torturing and killing her classmate Colleen Slemmer in 1995, when she was 18.
summary: Christa Pike survived two doses of pentobarbital during her attempted execution on 30 September. She was sentenced to death for torturing and killing her classmate Colleen Slemmer in 1995 when she was 18.

title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang sees Kazakhstan as potential AI hub for Europe
content: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, during his first visit to Kazakhstan, said the country’s growing computing capacity could make it a major AI hub for Europe as Kazakhstan expands its energy and digital infrastructure.
summary: During his first visit to Kazakhstan, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said the country's growing computing capacity could make it a major AI hub for Europe. He noted that Kazakhstan is expanding its energy and digital infrastructure.

summary: Novaya Gazeta, an independent Russian newspaper, announced it will shut down. It is one of the few Russian outlets openly critical of Russia's war in Ukraine and has faced increasing pressure from Moscow.

content: A zoo near Islamabad has launched a “Coffee with Alpaca” attraction, allowing visitors to have drinks and snacks while watching, feeding and petting the animals. The exhibit includes ten imported alpacas, which the zoo says are the first alpacas in Pakistan.
summary: The zoo near Islamabad has introduced a "Coffee with Alpaca" attraction where visitors can enjoy drinks and snacks while watching, feeding and petting alpacas. The attraction features ten imported alpacas, which the zoo says are the first in Pakistan.

title: Turkic states push Asia-Europe transport projects; Uzbekistan proposes 100 projects
content:
The Ankara Declaration underscored trade and transport cooperation among the Turkish states, marking a continued push toward Asia‑Europe connectivity.

title: EU diplomats protest G20 Lavrov photo, US cancels; Atlanta meeting proceeds
content: EU diplomats objected to a G20 photo featuring Russian Foreign Minister Lavrov, prompting a United States cancellation. The meeting in Atlanta will proceed as scheduled, preceding the G20 leaders’ summit hosted by President Donald Trump at his Miami golf club in December.

title: EU says Trump‑Putin diesel deal pushes transatlantic ties to new low
content:
The second Trump presidency has been described as more destabilizing for the EU than his first term. The source cites several actions that have strained transatlantic relations, including the false claim that the European Union was established to “screw” the United States, the imposition of tariffs on European goods, and territorial claims regarding Greenland. content: Russian made an unprecedented combative move this month as one of its military satellites, the Cosmos-2612, encroached upon the orbit of Ukrainian commercial satellite, Iceye-X36, in behaviour deemed "threatening" by the US State Department. summary: Russian made an unprecedented combative move this month as one of its military satellites, the Cosmos-2612, encroached upon the orbit of Ukrainian commercial satellite, Iceye-X36, in behaviour deemed "threatening" by the US State Department. content: During a brief U.S.-brokered ceasefire that ended Sunday evening, some residents of the Russian‑occupied town of Oleshky in southern Ukraine left the area. Ukrainian and Russian officials visited the town together on Friday, delivering aid and coordinating those who wanted to depart.
summary: Some residents of Oleshky, a Russian-occupied town in southern Ukraine, left on Friday during a rare ceasefire brokered by the United States that is set to end on Sunday evening. Ukrainian and Russian officials visited the town together on Friday, delivering aid and organizing those who wanted to leave.

title: CJEU President Koen Lenaerts says International Criminal Court deserves Sakharov Prize
content:
Koen Lenaerts, president of the Court of Justice of the European Union, said that the International Criminal Court deserves the Sakharov Prize.

The CJEU is the EU’s supreme judicial authority, responsible for ensuring that European law is interpreted and applied across all 27 member states.
summary: CJEU President Koen Lenaerts said the International Criminal Court deserves the Sakharov Prize. He leads the Court of Justice of the European Union, the EU's supreme judicial authority responsible for ensuring European law is interpreted and applied across all 27 member states.
author: France 24

title: Novaya Gazeta to cease publication after three decades amid Kremlin crackdown
content: Novaya Gazeta, Russia’s most renowned independent newspaper, announced on Friday that it would cease publication after more than three decades. The flagship outlet said a Kremlin crackdown and ban had made it impossible to continue its work, noting its history of courageous investigative journalism.
summary: Novaya Gazeta announced on Friday that it will cease publication after more than three decades of operation. The newspaper said the Kremlin’s crackdown and a ban on the outlet made it impossible to continue its work.
author: France 24

title: Oleshky Ceasefire Offers Limited Humanitarian Access Amid Russian Occupation
content:
Catherine Viette welcomed Jens Schumacher, Solidarity International’s Field Coordinator for Mykolaiv and Kherson, to discuss conditions in Oleshky. The Russian‑occupied town lies only a few kilometres from the Ukrainian‑controlled city of Kherson, yet proximity does not ensure access to essential services for the roughly 2,000 civilians still present.

Schumacher noted that a temporary ceasefire around Oleshky has created a limited window for humanitarian operations, but the agreement’s geographical scope, the feasibility of evacuations and the likelihood of sustained humanitarian access remain uncertain. Consequently, residents continue to face disrupted essential services and limited access to life‑saving assistance.
summary: A temporary ceasefire around the Russian‑occupied city of Oleshky has created a limited window for humanitarian operations, but access remains uncertain due to the agreement's limited geographic scope and evacuation challenges. Approximately 2,000 civilians are reported to remain in Oleshky, with disrupted essential services and uncertain evacuation arrangements.
author: France 24

title: MAGA fractures over Iran war, fuel prices, Epstein files before 2026 midterms
content: As the 2026 midterm elections approach, divisions within the MAGA camp are becoming increasingly visible. From the war in Iran and rising fuel prices to the Epstein files, several of Trump’s decisions are fuelling divisions among his most loyal supporters. Once united by a shared vision of America, MAGA now brings together factions that increasingly disagree over foreign policy, the economy and what “America First” should actually mean. Yet Trump remains the central figure holding this political coalition together – and he is fighting to keep it that way. Why are some of the president’s longtime allies distancing themselves from him? Can MAGA remain united despite these disagreements? And can Trump still mobilise his base ahead of the midterms? 🔍 Our journalist Stella Elgersma breaks down the divisions within the MAGA movement and Donald Trump’s strategy to rally his supporters, once again.
summary: Divisions within the MAGA camp are becoming increasingly visible as the 2026 midterm elections approach, with disagreements over the war in Iran, rising fuel prices and the Epstein files. Donald Trump remains the central figure trying to keep the coalition together and mobilise his base, according to journalist Stella Elgersma.
author: France 24

title: Claim Muslims burned five French churches on Oct. 17 is false
content:
Several social media accounts that share anti‑immigrant views circulated a claim that French Muslims had set fire to five churches on October 17, the same day the country experienced mass protests. The accounts asserted that the fires were part of a coordinated attack.

The story is untrue. France’s government agency that monitors religious heritage sites confirmed that only one church fire had occurred in recent days, and the cause of that fire remains unknown. No evidence supports the allegation that five churches were burned or that Muslims were responsible.
summary: Several anti‑immigrant social media accounts alleged French Muslims set fire to five churches on October 17. The French government agency that monitors religious heritage sites confirmed only one church fire occurred in recent days and its cause is unknown.
author: France 24

title: Shootings, extortion threats hit Bollywood, claimed by groups unlike 1990s underworld
content: India’s film industry is rattled by a wave of shootings and extortion threats. Those claiming responsibility differ from the Mumbai underworld that once dominated Bollywood in the 1990s.
summary: A wave of shootings and extortion threats has rattled India's film industry. The groups claiming responsibility are very different from the Mumbai underworld that had Bollywood in its grip in the 1990s.
author: DW World

title: Seoul worries US‑North Korea talks could sideline South Korea
content: South Korea’s government has expressed concern that the United States, under President Donald Trump, may prioritize a diplomatic breakthrough with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un at the expense of Seoul. Tensions between the South Korean administration and the Trump administration have heightened worries that the U.S. outreach could sideline South Korea’s interests.
summary: Ties between South Korea and the Trump administration are strained. The South Korean government worries that Donald Trump's pursuit of a diplomatic breakthrough with Kim Jong Un may come at Seoul's expense.
author: DW World

title: Siarhei Tsikhanouski attacks wife Sviatlana's legitimacy, sparking opposition rift
content:
Siarhei Tsikhanouski has publicly criticized the work of his wife, Sviatlana Tsikhanouskaya, and her office, and has questioned her legitimacy.  
This internal disagreement raises questions about the unity and direction of Belarusian political forces operating in exile.
summary: Siarhei Tsikhanouski criticizes the work of his wife, Sviatlana Tsikhanouskaya, and her office. He also questions her legitimacy.
author: DW World

title: UNHCR: Over 280,000 displaced in Yemen cannot safely reach lifesaving aid
content: The UN refugee agency (UNHCR) reported on Friday that more than 280,000 people have been displaced by fighting in Yemen. It added that many vulnerable individuals cannot reach lifesaving relief because the conditions are too dangerous.
summary: More than 280,000 people have been displaced by fighting in Yemen. UNHCR said on Friday that many vulnerable people cannot access lifesaving relief because it is too dangerous.
author: UN News

title: UN rights office warns Israeli actions deepening displacement nightmare in Gaza
content: The UN human rights office (OHCHR) warned on Friday that Israeli forces are forcing Palestinians into increasingly limited areas of the Gaza Strip, while destroying civilian infrastructure and attacking sites for displaced persons. The office expressed concern that these actions could amount to ethnic cleansing.
summary: Israeli forces continue to push Palestinians into ever‑smaller areas of the Gaza Strip while destroying civilian infrastructure and attacking displacement sites. The UN human rights office (OHCHR) warned on Friday that the situation raises concerns of ethnic cleansing.
author: UN News

title: DR Congo faces hunger for over 28 million as conflict, Ebola and climate shocks persist
content: More than 28 million people in the Democratic Republic of the Congo are currently not getting enough to eat, and the IPC global food‑security monitor warns that the number is likely to rise in the coming months. The hunger crisis is deepening amid ongoing conflict, Ebola outbreaks and climate‑related shocks.
summary: More than 28 million people in the Democratic Republic of the Congo are not getting enough to eat. The IPC global food security monitor says the number is expected to rise in the coming months.
author: UN News

title: Man on trial says assault of drugged woman was “their kink” after meeting couple online
content: Two of four men on trial say they met couple via online ads and swinging website and had no idea wife had been drugged Men accused of sexually assaulting a woman whose then husband drugged her for years and allowed her to be abused have described being invited to the couple’s home via online adverts and a swinging website. One of those accused of assaulting Joanne Young, who has waived her legal right to anonymity, as she lay restrained and blindfolded said he was a young man “trying out things” and had no idea she was drugged.
summary: A man accused of sexually assaulting Joanne Young, who was drugged by her husband, said he believed the act was part of a shared kink and that he did not know she had been drugged. He and three other men said they met the couple through online advertisements and a swinging website.
author: Guardian World

title: Friday briefing: Israel has a dilemma - can its opposition govern with Palestinian parties?
content:
Israel’s latest election has left Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu without a governing majority. According to the briefing, many Israelis described the vote as the most consequential in the country’s history, and the final tally produced a result that creates a “significant dilemma” for the nation.

Netanyahu’s far‑right coalition has lost its mandate, while the opposition bloc now holds a clear majority of seats. The opposition is organized as a Jewish Israeli bloc led by retired General Gadi Eisenkot. However, the bloc’s ability to form a government depends on whether it is willing to enter a governing pact with Palestinian Israeli parties, which the briefing notes have secured a historic electoral result.

The situation therefore hinges on the opposition’s decision to collaborate across the Jewish‑Palestinian divide. If such a partnership is pursued, it could define a new political moment for Israel; if not, the country faces uncertainty over how to assemble a functional government.
summary: In today’s newsletter: Benjamin Netanyahu has been left without a majority, now it is up to the coalition to find out whether the desire for change will prove to be a defining political moment Good morning. It was described by many Israelis as the most consequential election in their country’s history.
author: Guardian World

title: Cost of living protests set to spread to Germany and revive in France on Halloween
content:
Street protests that have been sweeping several European countries are expected to spread to Germany and to reignite in France on Saturday, coinciding with Halloween. Organisers say they hope the rallies will remain peaceful, while police have been mobilised to prevent potential looting and rioting on the fringes of the demonstrations.

Activists are urging participants to voice anger over the cost of living and what they describe as deficient public services, including education and housing. In recent weeks, student demonstrations—sometimes violent—have taken place in Italy, Spain, Portugal, Albania and France, prompting renewed calls for action on Halloween.
summary: Activists are calling for peaceful rallies on Saturday (Halloween) in Germany and France to protest the cost of living and poor public services such as education and housing. Police have been mobilised to prevent looting and rioting after weeks of sometimes violent student demonstrations in Italy, Spain, Portugal, Albania and France.
author: Guardian World

title: Archaeologists find perfume bottle, child's necklace in Pompeii wardrobe
content:
Archaeologists have uncovered a collection of personal items, including jewelry, cosmetics, and coins, within a wooden wardrobe in Pompeii that had been sealed since the eruption of Mount Vesuvius in AD79. The artifacts, which comprise fragments of makeup tools, a perfume bottle, and a child’s necklace, offer an intimate glimpse into the daily life of residents in the ancient Roman city before its destruction.

The discovery took place in a room of a home located on Via dell’Abbondanza, described as one of the most bustling streets in Pompeii. These findings highlight the preservation of everyday objects that had been tucked away for nearly two millennia.
summary: Archaeologists uncovered jewellery, cosmetics, coins and a child's necklace inside a wooden wardrobe sealed since the AD79 eruption of Mount Vesuvius in Pompeii. The wardrobe was found in a room of a home on Via dell’Abbondanza, one of the city's busiest streets.
author: Guardian World

title: Civilians evacuated from besieged Russian‑held city of Oleshky in joint relief operation
content:
On Friday, a joint relief operation began evacuating civilians from the besieged Russian‑held city of Oleshky in southern Ukraine. The operation marks the first evacuation of its kind in the four years and eight months of war.

Oleshky lies on the Russian‑occupied side of the Dnipro River, opposite Kherson. Residents have endured months of severe food and medical shortages, prompting warnings of starvation among the few thousand people still there, including about 50 children. A humanitarian convoy delivered food and medicine to the city.
summary: Civilians evacuated from besieged Russian‑held city of Oleshky in joint relief operation.
author: Guardian World

title: Experts warn AI copyright changes could breach Australian constitution, spark huge claims
content: Scraping copyrighted material from internet could ‘potentially’ amount to acquisition of property by government, Anne Twomey says Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast Altering copyright law to allow AI companies to scrape music, books and journalism could trigger a constitutional breach, Coalition senators and the recording industry have warned, as they raise new fears it could open Australia to massive legal action and compensation claims from rights holders worldwide. The attorney general’s department admitted it was “extremely alive” to the issue, and Australia’s leading constitutional expert, Anne Twomey, agreed there was “potentially” a concern – depending how legislation was drafted – that granting AI companies permission to scrape copyrighted material from the internet could amount to an acquisition of property by the government.
summary: Experts warn AI copyright changes could breach Australian constitution, spark huge claims.
author: Guardian World

title: Crypto theft estimated to supply half of North Korea’s foreign currency earnings
content:
North Korea’s foreign‑currency earnings are heavily dependent on cryptocurrency theft, which analysts estimate accounts for about half of the country’s income. The isolated, secretive regime is largely cut off from the global economic system, yet it turns to sophisticated hacking to generate foreign funds.

Experts at TRM Labs quickly linked the extraordinary $6.3 billion (£4.7 billion) theft from Binance to TraderTraitor, an elite North Korean hacking unit also known as the Lazarus Group. While the direct connection has not yet been proven, the pattern of behaviour is familiar to those monitoring the group’s activities.
summary: Cryptocurrency theft is estimated to generate about half of North Korea’s foreign currency income. TRM Labs linked the $6.3 billion Binance theft to the North Korean hacking unit TraderTraitor, also known as the Lazarus Group.
author: Guardian World

title: Flávio Bolsonaro’s brief self‑declaration as Brazil’s president‑elect mocked by media
content: Brazilian media ridicule defeated candidate over ‘shameful’ absconsion to US and bizarre letter with wrong coat of arms Flávio Bolsonaro had hoped that by Sunday night people would be calling him the next president of Brazil. Instead, the far-right politician’s decision to flee to the US after losing the election and – for 58 minutes – to declare himself “Brazil’s true president-elect”, has made him a laughing stock, with Brazilian newspapers and commentators raining a barrage of scornful adjectives down on the conquered candidate.
summary: Flávio Bolsonaro’s brief self‑declaration as Brazil’s president‑elect mocked by media.
author: Guardian World

title: Pope Leo XIV first pontiff to mail ballot in US midterm election
content: Pope Leo XIV, a Chicago‑born pontiff, became the first pope to cast a vote in a U.S. election when he mailed a ballot for the midterm elections that will determine control of Congress. The Vatican leader’s relationship with former President Trump is described as tense.
summary: The Chicago-born pontiff, who has a tense relationship with Trump, mailed in a ballot for the US midterm elections. The election will decide control of the US Congress.
author: BBC World

title: China's secretive space plane is flying over the US this week — here's how to see it for yourself
content:
China’s Shenlong space plane is currently orbiting Earth on its fourth mission and is scheduled to make a series of visible passes over the United States between October 30 and early November. According to satellite-tracking website Heavens-Above, skywatchers across the U.S. have multiple opportunities to spot the spacecraft, provided weather conditions are favorable. The viewing windows are typically in the predawn sky, requiring observers to wake up early to catch the passes.

Specific viewing times and maximum elevations are predicted for four major U.S. cities. In New York, the best predicted pass is on November 1 from 5:20 to 5:28 a.m. EST, reaching a maximum elevation of 78 degrees. Chicago offers a pass on November 3 from 4:37 to 4:42 a.m. CST, with a maximum elevation of 85 degrees. Denver’s optimal window is on November 2 from 5:05 to 5:12 a.m. MST, at a 73-degree elevation, while Los Angeles can observe a pass on November 2 from 5:42 to 5:51 a.m. PST, reaching 83 degrees. Additional viewing opportunities are listed for these cities on dates ranging from October 31 to November 6, with varying elevations and time windows.

To locate specific viewing times for other locations, observers are advised to use the Heavens-Above website. By entering their location and searching for "PRC TEST SPACECRAFT 4" in the satellite database, users can select "visible only" to view upcoming passes. Clicking on a specific date provides a detailed sky chart that illustrates the spacecraft’s predicted path, indicating where and when to look.

Shenlong is described as a reusable spacecraft that launches on a rocket and returns to Earth for a runway landing, similar to the U.S. Military’s X-37B space plane. While China has revealed limited information about the spacecraft’s activities, its space agency has stated that it is testing technologies intended to "pave the way for more convenient and affordable round-trip methods for the peaceful use of space in the future." The spacecraft has also been observed interacting with other objects in orbit.

Visually, Shenlong appears to the naked eye as a small, steadily moving point of light, akin to a satellite gliding across the sky. Its brightness varies significantly; veteran satellite observer Paul Maley reported spotting it from Paarl, South Africa, in February 2026, estimating its brightness at between magnitude +2.5 and +3.5 at its brightest. Maley noted that while it was easily visible under dark, moonless skies, it could also become much fainter, potentially dropping to magnitude +6. For the best chance of spotting the spacecraft, observers are recommended to view from dark locations away from city lights.

Recently, the U.S. Defense Intelligence Agency released a new photograph of Shenlong, providing a rare visual glimpse of the mysterious spacecraft.
summary: China's secretive space plane is making a series of passes over the United States in the coming days and you could spot it with your own eyes! The mysterious spacecraft, Shenlong, is currently orbiting Earth on its fourth mission.
author: Space.com

title: Watch Virgin Galactic's new 'Delta-class' space plane take to the skies for the 1st time (video)
content: Virgin Galactic's first "Delta-class" space plane just made its maiden voyage. The next-gen suborbital vehicle, named Apeiron (Greek for "Boundless"), lifted off for the first time ever on Thursday (Oct. 28). Flying beneath the wings of its carrier aircraft, VMS Eve, Apeiron traveled from Virgin's manufacturing site in Mesa, Arizona, to its launch site, Spaceport America in New Mexico. "Seeing the ship fly beneath Eve to Spaceport America was a moment years in the making," Virgin Galactic CEO Michael Colglazier said in a statement on Thursday. "To our team and our astronaut community: your Spaceship has arrived." Virgin Galactic's first Delta-class space plane, named Apeiron, takes to the skies for the first time on Oct. 28, 2026, beneath the wings of its carrier plane, VMS Eve. (Image credit: Virgin Galactic) Apeiron will undergo a series of checks and tests at Spaceport America, leading up to a planned start of commercial service in the spring of 2027. During those customer flights, Eve will carry Apeiron to an altitude of about 45,000 feet (13,700 meters), then drop the space plane. Apeiron will fire up its onboard rocket motor, which will carry the six-passenger, two-pilot vehicle to suborbital space. Passengers will experience a few minutes of weightlessness and get to see the curve of Earth against the blackness of space before coming down for a runway landing back at Spaceport America. Virgin Galactic has done this before, with its VSS Unity space plane. Unity flew seven commercial suborbital missions during its operational life, which ran from June 2023 to June 2024. Apeiron and other Delta-class planes are built for a much heavier workload, according to Virgin Galactic. "Designed to fly twice per week with a vehicle lifetime of more than 500 missions, each Spaceship in the next-generation fleet is built to support the economics of a scaled commercial operation, with increased flight cadence and a cost profile unprecedented in the industry," company representatives wrote in the same statement. And there will indeed be a fleet, if all goes to plan. The second Delta ship is under construction, for example, and is expected to enter service in mid-2027, according to Virgin Galactic. Apeiron and its Delta-class siblings will need to fly a lot to deal with Virgin Galactic's backlog: Nearly 700 ticket-holders are currently waiting to fly, according to the company. And demand remains high; the latest batch of seats, which were priced at $750,000 apiece, sold out. Virgin plans to sell the next tranche of tickets for $850,000 each, LATTE Luxury News reported. Another look at Apeiron. (Image credit: Virgin Galactic) When Apeiron gets up and running, it will be the only game in town for suborbital space tourists. Virgin Galactic once shared the skies with Jeff Bezos' Blue Origin, which flew paying customers to the final frontier on its New Shepard vehicle. New Shepard conducted 14 crewed suborbital flights between July 2021 and January 2026 but is currently grounded while the company focuses on helping NASA land Artemis astronauts on the moon.
summary: Virgin Galactic's first "Delta-class" space plane just made its maiden voyage. The next-gen suborbital vehicle, named Apeiron (Greek for "Boundless"), lifted off for the first time ever on Thursday (Oct.
author: Space.com

title: The week’s best new tracks and the act you need to know: Dutch squat-punks Bombstrap’s uncompromising racket
content:
Rotterdam-based band Bombstrap has released their debut album, Big Enemy, via Tartarus. The group is described as a riotous and theatrical fusion of sound, look, and attitude, led by Eva Kah, who is noted as both a living artwork and a phenomenal live performer. The band is recommended for fans of Gnod, Discharge, and Gwar, and is currently playing at the Le Guess Who festival.

Bombstrap draws inspiration from Het Poortgebouw, one of Rotterdam’s most famous squatted centers. The article characterizes the band as an embodied version of John Milton’s Pandæmonium with the amp turned up to 11. They revel in hardcore alternative living, internet wormholes, art-school pretensions, and a "gungy" form of hardcore. The text positions the band as a noisy counterblast to what it describes as the increasing and overwhelmingly witless “circuses-and-bread” gentrification of Rotterdam.
summary: The week’s best new tracks and the act you need to know: Dutch squat-punks Bombstrap’s uncompromising racket.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Basketweavers question Alexander Skarsgård's Wicker Husband construction
content: Why is he not made of willow? Why is he plaited and not woven? World’s basket makers have plenty of questions Hollywood heart-throbs are known for their good looks and charisma. But in a classic plot twist, the latest big-screen dreamboat causing viewers to get hot and bothered isn’t even human. Alexander Skarsgård’s Wicker Husband character in the romcom Wicker has sent the internet into a frenzy.
summary: World's basket makers are questioning why Alexander Skarsgård's character in the film Wicker is plaited rather than woven and not made of willow. The character, known as the Wicker Husband, has caused a frenzy among viewers.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Awkwafina Revives Family Cantonese Restaurant in New Apple TV Series
content:
Awkwafina, the star of Crazy Rich Asians and Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings, is set to star in a new Apple TV series titled Awkwafina: The Unlikely Cook. The show follows the rapper and actor as she travels across the United States to learn from a new generation of Asian American chefs. Her ultimate goal is to revive her family’s long-closed Cantonese restaurant, a challenge she undertakes despite admitting that she cannot cook.

In a recent interview, Awkwafina discussed the personal nature of the project, including the stress of rewatching her sitcom and the experience of nearly becoming a meat inspector. She also reflected on her relationship with her grandmother, who served as the matriarch of the family. Awkwafina noted that her grandmother passed away after the filming of the series concluded. The interview took place the morning after the BAFTA TV awards, where Awkwafina, known professionally as Nora Lum, discussed these deeply personal aspects of her new television work.
summary: Awkwafina stars in the Apple TV series Awkwafina: The Unlikely Cook, where she travels across the US to learn from Asian American chefs to revive her family's long-closed Cantonese restaurant. The project is deeply personal as her grandmother, the family matriarch, passed away after the series was filmed.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Guardian writers pick scariest non-horror films for Halloween
content:
Guardian writers have selected the most terrifying non-horror films for a Halloween feature, with choices ranging from How to Have Sex to The Hunchback of Notre Dame. The article includes minor spoilers and begins with a review of Lee Chang-dong’s Burning, starring Jeon Jong-seo, Steven Yeun, and Yoo Ah-in. In the film, a spirited young woman disappears while a wealthy playboy exhibits serial killer tendencies, creating an atmosphere of disaffected male rage.

Radheyan Simonpillai’s review focuses on Yoo Ah-in’s performance as Jong-su, an aspiring writer who works odd jobs and tends to his incarcerated father’s farm. Jong-su is described as quietly frustrated and desperate for control, which drives the film’s scary elements. The review characterizes Chang-dong as a master dramatist who shifts the movie into thriller territory, drawing on influences from Taxi Driver, The Vanishing, and Michael Haneke’s Caché. This approach uses horror movie language to generate creeping anxiety that ultimately erupts into existential fear.
summary: Guardian writers selected the most efficiently terrifying films outside the horror genre for a Halloween feature. The article includes a review of Lee Chang-dong's Burning, which is described as tilting into thriller territory to create existential fear.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Patrick Stewart dies at 86, remembered for his role as Jean-Luc Picard
content: As Jean-Luc Picard in seven seasons, four films and a sequel, Stewart made us believe the most interesting person in the room might also be the most humane Patrick Stewart dies age 86 His life in pictures Patrick Stewart brought gravitas and complexity to the screen, from Star Trek to X-Men ‘He stood for the best of us’: William Shatner and more pay tribute What might humanity look like in 400 years’ time if we really do become wiser and more compassionate with each passing decade? The creators of Star Trek: The Next Generation clearly felt the answer closely resembled Patrick Stewart, who has died aged 86 after a short illness. Their decision may well have opened up an entirely new future for Gene Roddenberry’s enduring, resolutely utopian space saga. Prior to the casting of the classically trained Yorkshireman in 1987, Star Trek was best known for the interplay between William Shatner’s charismatic, impulsive Captain Kirk and Leonard Nimoy’s drily logical Spock. Stewart brought something of both men to the captain’s chair as Jean-Luc Picard, combining analytical rigour with a depth of feeling his imposing formality could never quite conceal.
summary: Patrick Stewart has died aged 86 after a short illness. He is celebrated for his portrayal of Jean-Luc Picard in Star Trek: The Next Generation and four films.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Fans pay tribute to Sir Patrick Stewart at Hollywood Walk of Fame
content: Fans of the Star Trek actor gathered at his Hollywood Walk of Fame Star in Los Angeles to honor Sir Patrick Stewart following his death. The admirers paid tribute to his life and acting career, describing the loss as significant.
summary: Admirers of the Star Trek actor gathered at his Hollywood Walk of Fame Star in Los Angeles. They paid tribute to his life and acting career.
author: BBC Entertainment

title: Sir Patrick Stewart's 70-Year Career Highlighted by Iconic Sci-Fi Roles
content: Sir Patrick Stewart’s career, spanning seven decades across stages and screens, was defined by his roles in some of the most popular sci-fi franchises in history.
summary: Sir Patrick Stewart's career on stages and screens spanned seven decades. He became best known for his roles on some of the most popular sci‑fi franchises in history.
author: BBC Entertainment

title: English prodigies keep giant‑killing tradition from Penrose to Short
content:
Young British chess talents have a history of defeating established stars, a tradition spanning from Jonathan Penrose to Bodhana Sivanandan. The article highlights a specific example from the Brighton 1977 national title contest, where 10-time British champion Jonathan Penrose faced 12-year-old Nigel Short in round three. Short had previously gained a fast-growing reputation by defeating Viktor Korchnoi in a London simultaneous display the prior year.

During the 1977 match, observer David Bronstein noted that Short’s rook infiltration via the fifth rank after move 40 compared to José Capablanca’s strategy against Aron Nimzowitsch at New York 1927. This incident illustrates the broader narrative of English prodigies specializing in giant-killing across different generations.
summary: At the 1977 Brighton British Championship, 10‑time champion Jonathan Penrose faced 12‑year‑old Nigel Short, who had earlier defeated Viktor Korchnoi in a simultaneous display. Observing the game, David Bronstein compared Short’s rook infiltration to José Capablanca’s strategy against Aron Nimzowitsch in New York 1927.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Bella Vogel Nominated for World Rugby Breakthrough Player Ahead of USA-England Match
content:
Bella Vogel, a 19-year-old center and fly-half from Washington Boro, Pennsylvania, has become the first American nominated for the Women’s 15s Breakthrough Player of the Year award. The rising star, who is currently a student at Life University in Marietta, Georgia, is preparing for a significant test as the US Eagles women face the world champion Red Roses in Harrison, New Jersey. This upcoming WXV Global Series match will be the Eagles’ first encounter with England after securing five successive wins.

Vogel, who plays for the squad that blends experience with youth, acknowledged the high expectations placed on her. She joked about frequently being told not to let her head get too big due to her rapid rise in the sport. The match against the Red Roses is described as her stiffest Test to date, offering a challenging opportunity for the young player to prove her capabilities on the international stage.

The USA women’s rugby team will also be featured in a separate match against the Australia XV. Coverage of these games will be available to viewers in the US on Paramount Plus, while audiences in the UK can watch via the England Rugby YouTube channel and BBC iPlayer.
summary: Bella Vogel is the first American ever nominated for the Women’s 15s Breakthrough Player of the Year award. The 19-year-old center from Pennsylvania is preparing for a WXV Global Series game against England in New Jersey.
author: Guardian Sport

title: England's World Cup exit after 34-12 win over Papua New Guinea
content:
England’s Rugby League World Cup campaign is effectively over following a 34-12 victory over Papua New Guinea in their final Pool B and C group stage match in Wollongong. Despite the win, Brian McDermott’s team failed to secure the necessary point margin to qualify for the semi-finals. The result leaves England with a 22-point margin of victory, meaning they now rely on Tonga defeating Samoa by 46 points on Sunday to advance.

This scenario renders England’s qualification near-impossible, as they were previously trailing Samoa by 68 points. The men’s and women’s sides are set to exit the tournament within hours of one another. While the win against the Kumuls was a technical success, it did not provide the substantial point swing required to overturn the deficit against Samoa, leaving the team with no realistic path forward in the competition.
summary: England won 34-12 against Papua New Guinea but did not reach the required points margin to qualify for the semi-finals. Their exit depends on a 46-point win by Tonga over Samoa, which is highly unlikely.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Jimmy Anderson says he felt sadness and shock after surprise Lancashire dismissal
content: England great talks for first time since surprise dismissal Bowler optimistic about future within or outside sport Jimmy Anderson has revealed the “sadness and shock” he felt at his surprise Lancashire dismissal while he weighs up whether his future involves playing cricket or “something different”. Speaking for the first time since being told he will not have his county contract renewed, the England great told the BBC’s Tailenders podcast that the decision even made him question whether there is “something fundamentally wrong with me as a person”.
summary: Jimmy Anderson says he felt sadness and shock after surprise Lancashire dismissal.
author: Guardian Sport

title: FIFA to miss equal Women's World Cup prize money target set by Infantino
content:
Fifa will not achieve its 2027 goal for equal prize money at the Women’s World Cup, despite generating a record $15bn in revenue from the men’s tournament held this summer. In 2023, Fifa president Gianni Infantino stated that the organization aimed for prize pot equality by 2027, asserting that “Fifa is stepping up with actions, not just with words.”

While prize money for the women’s tournament could double, a significant gap with the men’s competition will remain. This outcome falls short of the widespread hope within the women’s game that the 2027 prize pot would match the men’s on at least a per-team basis.
summary: FIFA will fail to achieve equal prize money for the 2027 Women's World Cup despite President Gianni Infantino's 2023 ambition for equality. The prize pot is expected to double but a significant gap with the men's tournament will remain.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Carrick urged to trust Manchester United academy youth after recent defeats
content:
Manchester United’s recent defeats to Como and Bournemouth have prompted comparisons to the club’s historic eras built on academy talent, such as the Busby Babes and Class of 92. The source suggests this may be an appropriate moment for manager Michael Carrick to provide meaningful opportunities for the club’s current young players.

The article references a February 2025 FA Youth Cup match where United defeated Arsenal 3-2 at the Emirates Stadium. In that game, Jack Fletcher, Tyler Fletcher, and Harry Amass performed well for United, while Max Dowman, described as a generational talent, starred for Arsenal.

title: Hiroshima University study links hyperactive YAP/TAZ to immune recognition and PD‑L2 suppression
content:
Researchers at Hiroshima University and international collaborators recently identified a dual role for hyperactive YAP and TAZ (YAP/TAZ), two cancer-promoting proteins. The study found that these proteins are associated with genomic instability, a condition that may make cancer cells more recognizable to the immune system.

However, the research also revealed that YAP/TAZ activity increases PD-L2 levels. This protein helps cancer cells suppress T-cell attacks, potentially allowing tumors to evade immune destruction even when they are initially recognized.

title: Study finds participants who feel an extra finger perceive hand abilities differently
content:
The brain can sometimes create the illusion of an extra appendage or an extended body part when visual and tactile signals become mixed in the environment. This phenomenon, which has been examined in several studies, shows that crossed neural signals can alter bodily perception.

A new study published in the Journal of Experimental Psychology: Human Perception and Performance extends this line of research. Instead of merely inducing the sensation of an additional limb, the researchers investigated whether such induced sensations also change how participants perceive the capabilities of their own body.
summary: Participants were induced to feel an extra finger through a mix of visual and tactile cues. The resulting change in perception of hand capabilities was reported in a study published in the Journal of Experimental Psychology: Human Perception and Performance.

title: New Scientist Book Club reads Dark Eden by Chris Beckett
content: The New Scientist Book Club is reading Dark Eden by Chris Beckett We went out by a path that led through a big clump of flickering starflowers and then into Batwing. A whole bunch of Batwing grownups and newhairs were in their clearing banging away at a giant redlantern tree with their blackglass axes, working in the pink light of its flowers. We walked round the edge of their clearing to Family Fence, dragged away the branches at the opening, and went out into open forest. No more shelters and campfires ahead of us now: nothing but shining trees. Hmmmph, hmmmph, hmmmph, went the trees. Hmmmmmm, went forest. We walked for a waking under the light of the treelanterns, slashing down whatever birds and bats and fruit we could get as we went along, and finally stopped to rest at the big lump of rock called Lava Blob. Old Roger handed us out a gritty little seedcake each, made of ground-up starflower seeds, so we could have something in our bellies, and then we settled down with our backs against the rock, so we didn’t have to worry about leopards sneaking up behind us. There were lots of yellowlantern trees round there, which we didn’t get so much back in Family, and also yellow animals called hoppers that came bouncing out of forest on their back legs and wrung their four hands together while they looked at us with their big flat eyes and went Peep peep peep. But hoppers were no good to eat and their skins were no use either, so we just chucked stones at them to make them go away and let us sleep in peace. Advertisement Free newsletter Sign up to Book Club Sign up to newsletter When we woke up, Starry Swirl was still bright bright in sky. We ate a bit of dry cake and off we went again, under redlanterns and whitelanterns and spiketrees, with flutterbyes darting and glittering all round us and bats chasing the flutterbyes and trees going hmmph, hmmph, hmmph like always, until it all blurred together into that hmmmmmmmmm that was the background of our lives. After a few miles we came to a small pool full of shiny wavyweed and all us newhairs took off our wraps and dived into the warm water for crabfish and oysters to eat. All the boys watched Tina Spiketree diving in, and they all thought how graceful she was with her long legs, and how smooth her skin was, and how much they wanted to slip with her. But when she came up she swam straight to me, and gave me a dying oyster with the bright pink light still shining out of it. “You know what they say about oysters, don’t you, John?” she said. Tom’s neck, she was pretty pretty, the prettiest in whole of Family. And she knew it well well. In another couple of hours we reached the place where Peckham Hills began to rise up out of forest of Circle Valley, and started to climb up through them by Monkey Path, which isn’t really a path, but just a way we know through the trees. The trees carried on up the slopes – redlanterns and whitelanterns and scalding hot spiketrees – and there were flickering starflowers growing beneath them, just like in the rest of forest. Streams ran through them down from darkness and ice, heading towards Greatpool, still cold cold but already bright and glittering with life. And small creatures called monkeys jumped from tree to tree. They had little thin bodies, and six long arms with a hand on the end of each. Handsome Fox shot one with an arrow, and was pleased pleased with himself, even though they were all bones and sinews and only give a mouthful of meat, because they move fast and are hard to aim at with those big blotches on their skin that flash on and off as they swing among the lanternflowers. As we climbed up it got colder. The starflowers disappeared, the trees became smaller, and there weren’t any monkeys any more, only the occasional smallbuck darting away through the trees. And then the trees stopped and we came out from the top edge of forest onto bare ground. Pretty soon, when we’d climbed above the height of those last few little trees, we could see whole of Circle Valley spread out below us – whole of Eden that we knew, with thousands and thousands of lanterns shining all the way from where we stood on Peckham Hills to Dark shadow of Blue Mountains away in the distance, and from Rockies over the left, with the red glow of Mount Snellins smouldering in middle, to the deep darkness over to our right that was Alps. And above all of it the huge spiral of Starry Swirl was still shining down. Of course, with no trees to give off light with their lanternflowers or to warm the air with their trunks, it was dark dark up there – you could only just barely make things out in the starlight and the light from the edge of forest – and it was cold cold, specially on our feet. But us newhairs dared each other to run up as far as the snow. The ice felt like it was burning, it was so cold, and most kids took ten twenty steps, yelled and came running down again. But I took Gerry right up to the ridge of the hill and then, ignoring Old Roger yelling at us to come back, went far enough down the other side so that the others couldn’t see us. “We’ve made our point now, haven’t we, John?” Gerry said, shivering. We only had waistwraps on, and buckskins round our shoulders, and our feet were hurting like they’d been skinned. “Shall we go back down to rest of them now?” Our writers pick their favourite science fiction books of all time My cousin Gerry was about a wombtime younger than me – his dad was giving his mum a slip, in other words, about the time that I was born – and he was devoted to me, he thought I was wonderful, he’d do just about anything I asked. “No, wait a minute. Wait a minute. Be quiet and listen.” “Listen to what?” “To the silence, you idiot.” There was no hmmmmmmmm of forest, no hmmph, hmmph, hmmph of pumping trees, no starbirds going hoom, hoom, hoom in the distance, no flutterbyes flapping and flicking, no whoosh of diving bats. There was no sound at all except a quiet little tinkle of water all around us coming out from under the snow in hundreds of little streams. And it was dark dark. No tree-light up there. The only light came from Starry Swirl. We could barely make out each other’s faces. It made me think about that place called Earth where Tommy and Angela first came from, way back in the beginning with the Three Companions, and where one waking we would all return, if only we stayed in the right place and were good good good. There were no lanterntrees back there on Earth, no glittery flutterbyes or shiny flowers, but they had a big big light that we don’t have at all. It came from a giant star. And it was so bright that it would burn out your eyes if you stared at it. “When people talk about Earth,” I said to Gerry, “they always talk about that huge bright star, don’t they, and all the lovely light it must have given? But Earth turned round and round, didn’t it, and half the time it wasn’t facing the star at all but was dark dark, without lanterns or anything, only the light the Earth people made for themselves.” “What are you talking about, John?” Gerry said, with his teeth chattering. “And why can’t we go back down again if you just want to talk?” “I was thinking about that darkness. They called it Night, didn’t they? I’m just thinking that it must have been like this. What you get up here on Snowy Dark: it’s what they would have called Night.” © Chris Beckett This is an extract from Dark Eden by Chris Beckett (Corvus), the November read for the New Scientist Book Club. Sign up for the club here, and join the discussion on Discord here. When you make a purchase via the links on this page, we receive a commission.
summary: The New Scientist Book Club is reading Dark Eden by Chris Beckett. The excerpt describes a journey through a forest with starflowers, redlantern trees, and creatures such as hoppers and monkeys.

title: Scientists find fruit and vegetable skins contain more fibre than flesh
content: Fruit and vegetable skin is often rich in fibre Ekaterina Vasileva-Bagler/Getty Images Some people are convinced that fruit and vegetable skin are particularly nutritious, and now scientists have confirmed the idea. They have discovered that these parts of fruits and vegetables often contain far more fibre than the flesh we normally consume. The finding suggests cooks are unwittingly discarding fibre-rich food by chucking out the seeds, skins and stems of fruits and vegetables when preparing a meal. Home cooks and caterers should adopt “root to tip” eating and start cooking with squash peel, watermelon rind and pepper stalks to improve the public’s intake of dietary fibre, the team says. Advertisement Our food system is vulnerable to El Niño, warns UK climate minister “We’ve really got to shift our purchasing habits to buy whole fruits and vegetables, and then use all of the fruits and vegetables in dishes,” says Rachel Gibson at King’s College London. Gibson and her colleagues tested the fibre content of 12 fruits and vegetables, including butternut squash, kiwi fruit, watermelon, broccoli and bell pepper. The team measured the fibre content both in the parts typically consumed and the parts that usually go to waste. They found that, in 10 of the 12 produce types, the normally wasted components contain more fibre than the commonly consumed parts. Butternut squash seeds and skin, for example, contained 9.25 grams of fibre per 100 grams, compared with 2 g of fibre per 100 g of squash flesh. Meanwhile, the skin and core of a pineapple core contains 450 per cent more fibre than the flesh. These skin and core components are often tough to chew, but the researchers say they can be blended, grated or roasted to make them more palatable. Free newsletter Sign up to The Weekly Sign up to newsletter Just 4 per cent of British adults meet the recommended minimum daily intake of 30 g of dietary fibre, with the average adult consuming around half that per day. Gibson suggests caterers could use the findings to design fibre-rich meals using more produce that would otherwise go to waste. This could reduce food waste and cut costs for commercial kitchens, as well as increasing dietary fibre intake, she says. King’s College London’s canteen piloted a “root to tip” menu in May 2025. Meals included a West African peanut stew made with all of a butternut squash, kale stalks and leek tops, and a watermelon salad featuring pickled watermelon rind. Simple menu tweak can nudge people into choosing climate-friendly food Rejigging the meal choices on offer in a canteen can prompt people to make healthier, climate-friendlier decisions Eating a larger proportion of harvested fruit and vegetables will also improve the resilience of the food system in the face of climate shocks, says Gibson. “Everything we pull out of the ground that we can eat, we should be eating.” Christian Reynolds at City St George’s University of London says the research is an “exciting investigation”. But he points out that the most carbon-intensive food waste is meat and dairy products. Reducing fruit and vegetable waste is therefore “part of the solution, but it’s not the only thing we need to do”, he says. Journal Reference: International Journal of Food Sciences and Nutrition DOI: 10.1080/09637486.2026.2734852
summary: Researchers from King’s College London measured fibre in 12 produce items and found that in 10 of them the skins, seeds or cores contain more fibre than the flesh. The study suggests adopting a “root to tip” approach could boost dietary fibre intake and reduce food waste.
author: New Scientist

title: Binance Hit by Biggest Crypto Heist, $6.36B Stolen in 20 Minutes
content: Binance is the biggest cryptocurrency exchange ZUMA Press Wire/Shutterstock The world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange Binance has been hit with the biggest ever cryptocurrency heist, in which billions of dollars of reserves were drained in just 20 minutes. From 8:05pm on 29 October, $6.36 billion in cryptocurrencies were shifted from wallets in a coordinated attack believed to have originated from a North Korean-linked hacking unit called TraderTraitor. This group was also behind a $1.5 billion hack of the Bybit crypto exchange in February 2025. The US Treasury has previously said that such stolen funds are used to finance North Korea’s nuclear missile programme. Advertisement Despite cryptocurrency’s founding idea of decentralisation, meaning no one has singular control over the money flowing through the network, there are some large single points of failure. It is thought one of these was the cause of the Binance hack, which gave access to a system the exchange uses to authorise transfers out of customers’ accounts. Quantum computer quickly mines cryptocurrency while using less energy In a statement, Binance said its early investigations indicate the security incident may stem from a compromised laptop belonging to an engineer. TRM Labs, a cybersecurity firm, suggests that preparations for the attack may have begun several days ago. The company claims it has found no evidence that the private cryptographic keys used to authorise transactions were stolen. Instead, the attackers appear to have gained access to the software that requests withdrawals, potentially allowing them to instruct Binance’s own systems to approve the transfers. However, the investigation is continuing and the firm has said in a subsequent statement there may have been “additional points of breach”. “It shouldn’t be possible for a single [developer] PC to be compromised and somehow for that to allow the entire exchange to be compromised,” says Alan Woodward at the University of Surrey, UK. “I don’t understand how that can happen unless they’ve got the most ridiculous operational security.” If that is the case, it highlights how precarious major financial hubs in the crypto world can be to single points of failure. Free newsletter Sign up to The Weekly Sign up to newsletter “You can build a vault with mathematical firewalls, but if the individual holding the keys can be duped, the vault is opened,” says Clive Summerfield at FARx, a cybersecurity company. “Most crypto platforms are as centralised as any bank, with a small number of privileged individuals controlling billions. The difference is that once crypto is transferred, it’s gone.” That centralisation can be a blessing as well as a curse, though: cryptocurrencies Tether and Circle have been able to freeze billions of dollars of stolen coins, stymying the hackers in attempts to transfer about half the stolen funds any further. Woodward says the Binance incident potentially strikes a distinction between crypto security and more traditional finance. “You would hope there’d be things like two-man rules [where two separate people have to approve a change] or things that banks have for changing critical systems, but it doesn’t look like those were in place.”
summary: Binance Hit by Biggest Crypto Heist, $6.36B Stolen in 20 Minutes.

title: Birmingham physicists create miniature universe, observe time emerging without a clock
content:
Scientists created a miniature universe in the laboratory, a setup that could help answer one of physics' biggest mysteries: what is time and where it comes from.  

Using 24,000 ultracold atoms, a University of Birmingham researcher built an isolated quantum system that repeatedly expands and contracts, mimicking the Big Bang and a possible Big Crunch.  

The experiment showed that time could emerge from changes happening inside the system, without relying on an external clock.
summary: Using 24,000 ultracold atoms, a University of Birmingham researcher built an isolated quantum system that repeatedly expands and contracts, mimicking the Big Bang and a possible Big Crunch. The experiment showed that time could emerge from changes inside the system without relying on an external clock.

title: Hubble Finds Wind From Exploding Stars Blocks Radiation, Challenging Early Universe Theory
content: Astronomers using the Hubble Space Telescope have made a discovery that challenges the leading explanation for how the early universe emerged from a dense hydrogen fog roughly 13 billion years ago. Previous scientific consensus held that powerful winds from exploding stars helped radiation escape galaxies, thereby clearing the cosmic fog. However, new observations indicate that these winds actually block radiation instead.
summary: Astronomers using the Hubble Space Telescope discovered that winds from exploding stars block radiation instead of helping it escape galaxies. This finding challenges the leading explanation that such winds cleared the early universe's dense hydrogen fog about 13 billion years ago.

content: A new study indicates that 54% of adults under 45 with type 2 diabetes achieved remission after six months of an intensive low-calorie diet and structured exercise program. This result stands in contrast to the 4% remission rate observed in participants receiving usual care, suggesting the potential efficacy of this combined approach for younger adults.
summary: A new study found that 54% of participants under age 45 with type 2 diabetes achieved remission after six months of an intensive diet and exercise program. Only 4% of participants receiving usual care achieved remission.

title: Computer scientist overcomes 25-year-old network distance calculation limit
content:
A computer scientist has broken a limit that has stood since 1996 by solving a nearly 25‑year‑old problem about calculating distances across huge networks. The new algorithm provides more reliable estimates for closely connected points while maintaining speed, surpassing earlier methods.

The improvement comes from a smarter way of sampling network connections at multiple scales, enabling faster and more accurate distance calculations.
summary: A computer scientist achieved a breakthrough in a nearly 25‑year‑old problem of calculating distances across large networks. The new algorithm provides more reliable estimates for closely connected points while maintaining speed, using a smarter multi‑scale sampling of network connections.
author: Science Daily

title: Scientists Explain How Crocodiles Survived the Asteroid that Killed Dinosaurs
content: Scientists may have solved a 66‑million‑year‑old mystery: how crocodiles survived the asteroid that wiped out the dinosaurs. A sweeping analysis of fossils and ancient climates suggests that the reptiles’ preference for warm environments placed them in tropical refuges that stayed habitable even after the catastrophic impact.
summary: Scientists have analyzed fossils and ancient climates to explain how crocodiles survived the asteroid that killed the dinosaurs. Their preference for warm environments kept them in tropical refuges that remained habitable after the impact.
author: Science Daily

title: Astronauts complete 7‑hour spacewalk installing new solar array on ISS
content: Two astronauts completed a 7‑hour, 11‑minute spacewalk to install a new solar array on the International Space Station. The installation brings NASA closer to a major power upgrade, and once the final array is installed on November 5, the station will have up to 30 % more available power to support critical operations and its eventual controlled deorbit.
summary: Two astronauts completed a 7‑hour, 11‑minute spacewalk to install a new solar array on the International Space Station. The final array will be installed on November 5, giving the station up to 30% more power for critical operations and its eventual controlled deorbit.
