title: Voyager 1 to Reach One Light‑Day from Sun on Nov 18 2026
content:
November’s Night Sky Notes: Light‑Day Away

In 1977 NASA launched two identical spacecraft, Voyager 1 and Voyager 2, to take advantage of a planetary alignment that occurs once every 175 years. The alignment of Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune allowed the twin probes to use six gravity assists to visit each of the four largest planets in the outer solar system. The mission delivered close‑up images and scientific data on the gas and ice giants, including several of their moons.

After completing their encounters with Saturn in the early 1980s, the Voyager probes went their separate ways. Voyager 2 continued toward Uranus and Neptune, while Voyager 1 captured a final portrait of the solar system—excluding Mercury and Mars—including the last image of Earth, the pale blue dot. The Voyager missions set the stage for later orbiter missions such as Galileo to Jupiter and Cassini to Saturn.

Each spacecraft carries a 12‑inch phonograph record known as the Golden Record. The record contains spoken greetings in 55 languages, 27 musical tracks, 116 images, and other sounds from Earth. The outer cover is etched with the Sun’s position relative to 14 pulsars and includes instructions for playback. The record itself is plated with copper and gold, while the cover is made of aluminum and electroplated with an ultra‑pure sample of the isotope uranium‑238, which has a half‑life of 4.468 billion years.

Both Voyager probes crossed the heliopause—the boundary where the Sun’s solar wind meets the interstellar medium—in August 2012 (Voyager 1) and November 2018 (Voyager 2). NASA’s Deep Space Network continues to communicate with the spacecraft and track their positions. At the time of this article, the Canberra antenna was tracking Voyager 1 at a distance of 25.80 billion km, or just over 16 billion miles, from Earth.

On November 18, 2026, 49 years after launch, Voyager 1 will reach the one‑light‑day mark, 16.1 billion miles from the Sun. This milestone highlights the vast distances measured in light‑time units, a concept familiar from science‑fiction and stargazing alike. The Voyager spacecraft remain outside the heliosphere, the protective bubble created by the Sun that extends well beyond Pluto’s orbit.
summary: 2 min read November’s Night Sky Notes: Light-Day Away NASA’s Voyager mission took advantage of a once-every-175-year alignment of the outer planets for a grand tour of the solar system. The twin spacecraft revealed details about Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune – using each planet’s gravity to send them on to the next destination.
author: NASA News

title: GLP-1 weight‑loss drugs may worsen rising eating disorder rates
content:
A new report published in JAMA Psychiatry indicates that the global incidence of anorexia nervosa and bulimia nervosa increased by 71% between 1990 and 2023. By 2023, an estimated 18.1 million people were living with one of these two disorders, a figure researchers expect to rise to 21.8 million by 2050. The study, led by Ruhai Bai at the Children’s Hospital of Nanjing Medical University, utilized statistical models to analyze data from 204 countries and territories. The researchers calculated that these conditions cost the world the equivalent of approximately 3.83 million years of healthy life in 2023, measured in disability-adjusted life years.

Clinical experts suggest that environmental factors, including social media and the COVID-19 pandemic, have contributed to this rise. Cynthia Bulik, a clinical psychologist at the University of North Carolina, notes that social media comparisons, influencers, and diet trends serve as precipitating events for eating disorders. Research from the University of Melbourne found that TikTok algorithms delivered 4,343% more “toxic eating disorder videos” to users with these conditions compared to those without. Additionally, data from 2021 showed that hospitalizations for eating disorders in the US doubled between 2018 and 2020, a trend experts link to the social isolation of lockdowns.

Cheri Levinson, a clinical psychologist at the University of Louisville, reports seeing more patients with severe symptoms than at any point in her 20-year career. She states that many of these patients are misusing GLP-1 weight-loss drugs, which she describes as a potential trigger for worsening conditions. In a small study published earlier this year, Levinson and colleagues found that 30% of people with eating disorders had used GLP-1 drugs, with 10% appearing to misuse them. Levinson believes this misuse rate is an underestimate and reports cases of children developing eating disorders after being prescribed these medications for medical reasons or purchasing them online.

The accessibility of GLP-1s has increased, with a Gallup survey indicating that 15% of Americans have used these drugs for weight loss. Drug companies are developing new formulations, and versions are available through compound pharmacies or online sources. Bulik expresses concern that GLP-1s may lead to faster and more extreme weight loss in individuals with anorexia nervosa, resulting in patients arriving at treatment in advanced stages of illness that are difficult to reverse. Both Levinson and Bulik are continuing to study the impact of these drugs on eating disorders.

In response to these concerns, Bulik contributed to research and clinical guidelines published earlier this month. These guidelines recommend that doctors screen for eating disorders before prescribing GLP-1s, provide more patient education, and implement robust monitoring for individuals taking the drugs. Levinson adds that she is not surprised if the number of eating disorder cases doubles again, noting that she is currently seeing patients as young as eight and nine years old with the conditions. The true impact of eating disorders is likely higher than reported figures, as anorexia and bulimia represent less than half of all eating disorders, according to Levinson.
summary: A JAMA Psychiatry study reported a 71% increase in the incidence of anorexia nervosa and bulimia nervosa from 1990 to 2023, with an estimated 18.1 million people affected in 2023. Clinical psychologists say that GLP‑1 weight‑loss drugs are being misused by people with eating disorders, potentially worsening symptoms and contributing to earlier onset.

title: iOS app Oh My Hours tracks wasted Instagram and TikTok time in hour blocks
content: The iOS app Oh My Hours brutally shames users by tracking how many hours they’ve lost to scrolling. It divides each day into hour‑long blocks and highlights the blocks spent on Instagram and TikTok, offering a new approach to curbing screen time.

title: TraderTraitor linked to $6.3 B Binance hack executed in 20 minutes
content: A $6.3 billion hack of Binance was reportedly executed in just 20 minutes. Multiple crypto‑tracing firms have identified the North Korean hacking group known as TraderTraitor as a possible perpetrator of what they describe as the largest digital heist in history, with billions of cryptocurrency likely unrecoverable.
summary: Multiple crypto‑tracing firms say the North Korean hacker group TraderTraitor may be behind the $6.3 billion Binance hack. The breach reportedly took only 20 minutes and is described as the largest digital heist in history, with billions of crypto likely gone for good.

title: Wikimedia Foundation warns bad AI copyright ruling could harm open web
content:
The Wikimedia Foundation filed an amicus brief on Friday in a group of landmark lawsuits that pit publishers, including The New York Times, against OpenAI and Microsoft. In the brief, the nonprofit behind Wikipedia argues that courts should legally protect large‑language models that train on copyrighted material while exempting chatbots that merely regurgitate that material to users.  

Wikimedia warns that a strictly black‑and‑white ruling could either strip Wikipedians of useful AI‑based tools or threaten the open web. The foundation takes no side in the litigation but expresses concern that the parties’ positions push for an overbroad approach.
summary: Wikimedia Foundation warns bad AI copyright ruling could harm open web.

But the fear echoing through the auditorium wasn't so easily dismissed. Just days before voters head to the polls, the rapid expansion of resource-hungry data centers has exploded into one of Maine's most volatile campaign issues. Maine drew national headlines in April when the state Le …

title: Binance Reports $6.3 Billion Crypto Theft, Claims to Cover Losses
content:
Binance announced that $6.3 billion worth of cryptocurrency has been stolen from its platform, a theft that is believed to be the largest hack in the history of digital assets. The exchange has stated that the loss is the result of a coordinated cyberattack and that the incident represents a record‑breaking breach.

In a series of updates posted to X, Binance confirmed that user funds remain safe and that roughly $3 billion of the impacted assets have already been frozen. The company has pledged to cover any losses incurred by users as a result of the hack.

Binance also disclosed that it has an emergency reserve fund of about $1.3 billion, based on its last valuation, to protect user assets in such situations. Additionally, the company has set aside more than $6.34 billion of its own funds to cover the incident, with $5 billion of those funds earmarked for this purpose.
summary: Binance says it will cover all loses resulting from the hack. | Image: Cath Virginia / The Verge, Turbosquid Binance has disclosed that $6.3 billion worth of crypto funds have been stolen from the platform, in what's believed to be the biggest cryptocurrency hack on record.

title: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman says AI math output will continue despite mathematicians' concerns
content:
OpenAI CEO Sam Altman acknowledged the company’s recent flood of AI‑generated mathematical results and expressed sympathy for researchers who are trying to keep up. In a Thursday episode of the Cheeky Pint podcast, he said, “I think, on net, the world deserves to understand how the universe works,” while adding, “But I do have empathy for the method.”  

Altman made clear that OpenAI will not pause its output and hinted that more discoveries may follow from the company’s growing stockpile. His remarks are among the first public statements in which the OpenAI chief directly addressed the impact of the firm’s work on the mathematics community.
summary: Sam Altman, OpenAI CEO, said he sympathizes with mathematicians overwhelmed by the company's AI-generated results. He told the Cheeky Pint podcast released Thursday that OpenAI will not stop the math onslaught and may release more discoveries.

To some extent, Anthropic suggests in a letter at the top of its S-1 filing, you have to just believe. Anthropic's 335-page S-1 prospectus, filed Monday, is part of a steady hype escalation in Silicon Valley's interactions with Wall Street. In some ways, it's not even that bizarre; SpaceX IPO'd in June after filing an S-1 that referenced din …

content: Welcome to Edition 9.17 of the Rocket Report! title: Film “You Can See Everything” portrays Elizabeth Holmes’ final days before prison
content:
In 2015, Elizabeth Holmes was celebrated as Silicon Valley’s youngest and richest self‑made female billionaire, with her company Theranos valued at $9 billion. The company’s reputation collapsed after accusations of fraud regarding its blood‑testing device, leading to a high‑profile trial. Holmes was convicted on four counts and sentenced to 11 years in prison.

The former entrepreneur has returned to the headlines with the film You Can See Everything, which portrays the final days before Holmes entered prison after exhausting her appeals. The movie is co‑directed by Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim and has been described as a surreal, absurdist piece that has generated widespread enthusiasm and hype, with some calling it the best film of the year.

Critics, however, have offered counter‑views. The reviewer notes that while the film contains entertaining moments—particularly in its second half—it delivers little new insight into Holmes or the Theranos saga. The film is described as shallow, running in circles, and not justifying the intense hype surrounding it.
summary: The documentary, co‑directed by Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim, depicts the period just before Elizabeth Holmes began her 11‑year sentence after being convicted on four fraud counts. The reviewer calls the film shallow and lacking fresh insight despite its hype.
author: Ars Technica

title: 2027 Nissan Rogue Hybrid launches with 1.5‑L series e‑Power system
content:
Nissan supplied a flight from Washington, DC, to Santa Barbara, California, and lodging so that Ars could test‑drive the company’s new 2027 Rogue Hybrid. The outlet notes that it does not accept paid editorial content.

The 2027 model is the latest iteration of Nissan’s best‑selling Rogue SUV and is being introduced with the newest version of the brand’s e‑Power hybrid system, which Ars evaluated in February. Unlike most current hybrids that operate as parallel systems—using an internal‑combustion engine and an electric motor together to drive the wheels—Nissan’s e‑Power uses a series‑hybrid layout. In this configuration the gasoline engine functions solely as a generator to charge the traction battery, while the electric motor provides propulsion.

Under the hood, the Rogue Hybrid is equipped with a 1.5‑liter, three‑cylinder turbocharged direct‑injection engine that produces 148 hp (110 kW). The engine is limited to 5,200 rpm and is tuned primarily to charge the battery rather than to handle direct drivetrain loads. This design enables a reported thermal efficiency of 42 percent, a figure the article compares only to Formula 1 power units.

Visually, the vehicle features a crisp shut line and slim horizontal headlights that the writer likens to a Range Rover aesthetic. These details, combined with the series‑hybrid powertrain, define the 2027 Nissan Rogue Hybrid as a model that aims to deliver electric‑vehicle‑like driving dynamics without requiring external charging.
summary: Nissan introduced the 2027 Rogue Hybrid, the latest version of its best‑selling Rogue SUV equipped with the e‑Power series‑hybrid system. It is powered by a 1.5‑liter three‑cylinder turbocharged engine that produces 148 hp (110 kW), revs to 5,200 rpm to charge the traction battery, and achieves roughly 42 % thermal efficiency.

title: Voice actor stars in Black Tides Draga’s Wake after 50 years of gaming
content:
Greg Strangis initiated a creative partnership 16 months ago by inviting the author to his garage to review his game, Black Tides Draga’s Wake. Strangis introduced himself by telling the author, “I listen to you on the radio and I keep hearing your voice in my head!” This request led to the author voicing the main character in the title.

The experience of performing the role involved making noises the author had not produced since their honeymoon. It also resulted in a favorite moment as a father, marking a unique milestone for the individual who has been playing video games for 50 years.

title: Meta staff discussed a ‘whisper strategy’ to discredit critic Jonathan Haidt, court papers show
content:
Court documents show Meta employees discussed a “whisper strategy” aimed at undermining Jonathan Haidt, a U.S. social psychologist whose book The Anxious Generation influenced debates on online safety. The internal memos indicate staff considered ways to get the academic community to disavow Haidt and to discredit him publicly.

The documents also note that Haidt’s work helped shift discussion toward stricter measures, including Australia’s under‑16 ban on certain social‑media features. Meta’s planning centered on countering his influence.
summary: Court documents reveal Meta employees considered a “whisper strategy” to get the academic community to disavow Jonathan Haidt. The staff sought to discredit Haidt, a social psychologist and author of The Anxious Generation, whose book helped tip the debate toward stricter online safety measures such as Australia’s under‑16 ban.

title: Workers face unsafe conditions and fear retaliation at European datacentres
content:
Investigations by the Guardian and Investigate Europe have highlighted that workers constructing the growing number of datacentres across Europe face hazardous conditions and fear retaliation for speaking out. The reporting points to instances of unsafe practices and concerns about exploitation among the workforce.

One example involves a 34‑year‑old electrical tester named Sandu at a Google datacentre in Saint‑Ghislain, Belgium. In March, after nearly ten hours on duty, he received a call for a last‑minute assignment that required testing the safety and integrity of electrical wiring. Sandu said such late‑night jobs were routine and that refusing could lead to dismissal. Although a protective suit was stored nearby, retrieving it would have added about fifteen minutes, and with people waiting he chose to proceed without it.
summary: Workers face unsafe conditions and fear retaliation at European datacentres.
author: Guardian Technology

title: North Korean group blamed for $6.3bn Binance hack, biggest crypto theft
content: Cryptocurrency exchange scrambles to freeze affected assets, with about $3bn located so far, and says it will cover losses Tell us: have you been affected by the Binance hack? Business live – latest updates The world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange has been hit by an industry-record $6.3bn (£4.7bn) hack, with experts identifying North Korea as the likely culprit. Binance has scrambled to freeze the affected assets, with about $3bn located so far. The company gave no update on the other $3.3bn as Binance’s co-founder Yi He said the company would cover “all hacking losses”.
summary: The world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange, Binance, was hit by an industry‑record $6.3bn hack, with experts identifying North Korea as the likely culprit. Binance has frozen the affected assets, has located about $3bn so far, and co‑founder Yi He said the company will cover all hacking losses.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Donald and Melania Trump give sweets to costumed children as Air Force One flies overhead
content: Donald and Melania Trump welcomed children in Halloween costumes to the White House on Thursday. The couple handed out sweets, posed for photographs and watched Air Force One fly overhead.
summary: Donald and Melania Trump welcomed children in Halloween costumes to the White House on Thursday. They handed out sweets, posed for photographs and watched Air Force One fly overhead.
author: Euronews

title: Trump berates Reuters reporter who asked if he was tired of campaigning
content: US President Donald Trump berated a Reuters reporter after the journalist asked whether Trump had cancelled a planned Kansas rally because he was tired of campaigning ahead of the midterm elections. The exchange occurred during the reporter’s questioning of Trump’s campaign schedule.
summary: US President Donald Trump berated a Reuters reporter who questioned whether he had cancelled a planned Kansas rally because he was tired of campaigning. The exchange took place ahead of the midterm elections.
author: Euronews

title: Flowers placed at Patrick Stewart's Hollywood Walk of Fame star after death
content: Flowers were placed at Patrick Stewart’s Hollywood Walk of Fame star after reports of the British actor’s death at age 86. In Los Angeles, visitors gathered around the star to remember Stewart’s celebrated screen roles.
summary: Flowers have been placed at Patrick Stewart's Hollywood Walk of Fame star following reports of the British actor's death at 86. Visitors gathered in Los Angeles to remember his celebrated screen roles.
author: Euronews

title: Nine rescued orangutans return to Borneo forest after wildfire rehabilitation
content:
Nine orangutans rescued from devastating wildfires in Indonesian Borneo have returned to the forest after weeks of rehabilitation.  
Among the rescued group are four mothers with their young, and three of those females are expecting another baby.
summary: Nine orangutans rescued from devastating wildfires in Indonesian Borneo have been released back into the forest after weeks of rehabilitation. The group includes four mothers with their young, and three of the females are expecting another baby.
author: Euronews

title: China rejects report of spy plot targeting Nvidia's Jensen Huang
content: China has denied allegations that a spy plot was aimed at Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. Nvidia’s spokesperson told AFP on Friday that the company’s regional cloud customers receive only ordinary business information, not sensitive trade secrets, and that no data relevant to national security is shared.
summary: Nvidia spokesperson said regional cloud customers receive ordinary business information, not sensitive NVIDIA trade secrets. The company also said no information relevant to national security is shared.
author: Euronews

title: North Korea warns South Korea with ballistic missiles as Seoul calls for talks
content: North Korea warned South Korea with ballistic missiles as missile launches and a dispute over a land‑mine incident heightened tensions between the two Koreas. Seoul is seeking military talks to prevent accidental clashes, but Pyongyang has not yet responded.
summary: Missile launches and a landmine dispute have heightened tensions between the two Koreas. Seoul is seeking military talks to prevent accidental clashes, but Pyongyang has yet to respond.
author: Euronews

title: TotalEnergies posts record quarterly profit while keeping fuel prices below rivals
content:
Hundreds of thousands of French citizens are expected to protest the high cost of living again this weekend. The demonstrations come amid a backdrop of rising consumer concerns over everyday expenses.

Oil and gas giant TotalEnergies has reported record profits for the quarter ending September. The company has maintained fuel prices lower than those of its rivals at its pumps, yet motorists are questioning whether the firm could reduce prices further.
summary: TotalEnergies reported record profits for the quarter to September. It has kept fuel prices at its pumps lower than rivals, even as hundreds of thousands in France are expected to protest the high cost of living.
author: France 24

title: Tanzania marks one year since violent 2025 election that left many traumatised
content: Tanzania is marking the first anniversary of the bloody 2025 election that has left many people traumatised. The vote held on October 29, 2025 saw President Samia Suluhu Hassan win with 98 percent of the vote after most opposition candidates were excluded. The result triggered days of protests that security forces brutally suppressed. Many government critics continue to fear abduction, arbitrary arrest and politically motivated prosecutions.
summary: Tanzania is marking the first anniversary of the October 29, 2025 election that saw President Samia Suluhu Hassan declared winner with 98 percent of the vote after most opposition candidates were excluded. Critics say they continue to fear abduction, arbitrary arrest and politically motivated prosecutions following the security forces’ brutal suppression of days of protests.
author: France 24

title: Senegal prepares for historic 2026 Youth Olympic Games, first in Africa
content: The International Olympic Committee expressed optimism just 24 hours before the start of the 2026 Youth Olympic Games in Senegal, noting that venues are ready to host the first Olympic event on the African continent. France 24’s correspondent Aminatou Diallo reported from the ground.
summary: The International Olympic Committee expressed optimism a day before the 2026 Youth Olympic Games begin in Senegal. Venues are prepared to host the first Olympic event ever held on the African continent, according to FRANCE 24 correspondent Aminatou Diallo.
author: France 24

title: At least 60 Christians Killed in Ethiopia Amid Rising Religious Violence
content: The Orthodox Church has declared the killings of at least 60 Christians in Ethiopia a case of religious violence. The perpetrators remain unclear, with rebels and the local government blaming each other. According to FRANCE 24 correspondent Tom Canetti, about 20 houses were burned.
summary: At least 60 Christians were killed in Ethiopia in an incident the Orthodox Church has described as religious violence. Rebels and the local government blame each other, and about 20 houses were burned, according to Tom Canetti of France 24.
author: France 24

title: Foiled Illinois Hindu temple plot highlights growing anti-Indian sentiment in US
content: The latest edition of Access Asia examines the increase in anti‑Indian sentiment in the United States following a foiled plot aimed at a Hindu temple in Illinois. The program features a conversation with the executive director of the Center for the Study of Organized Hate, who is asked to explain the factors behind the trend and to assess whether rhetoric from the Trump White House may be contributing to the rise. The discussion centers on the recent temple plot and its broader implications for anti‑Indian attitudes.
summary: A plot targeting a Hindu temple in Illinois was foiled, prompting an examination of rising anti-Indian sentiment in the United States. The discussion includes the executive director of the Center for the Study of Organized Hate and considers whether rhetoric from the Trump White House contributes to the trend.
author: France 24

title: Russia recruits over 1,400 Africans to fight in Ukraine, families in Tunisia seek answers
content:
At the Africa‑Russia summit, leaders and officials from both sides convened to discuss security, trade and political cooperation. A sensitive topic, however, was noticeably missing from the agenda: the recruitment of Africans to fight for Russia in Ukraine.  

Since 2023, more than 1,400 Africans have been enlisted for service in Ukraine. In Tunisia, families of several men who had travelled to Russia for work or study are still seeking answers about the fate of their loved ones, according to FRANCE 24’s team on the ground.
summary: More than 1,400 Africans have been enlisted by Russia to fight in Ukraine since 2023. In Tunisia, families of men who travelled to Russia for work or study are still searching for answers about their fate.
author: France 24

title: Arizona Yuma farms depend on daily Mexican labor despite border fears
content: Yuma County’s extensive produce farms depend on foreign workers who cross the Mexico‑U.S. border each day. Farmer John Boelts, who identifies as a staunch supporter of President Donald Trump, commends the administration’s strict border controls but says that competing Republican factions have made it harder to recruit those foreign laborers.
summary: The produce farms in Yuma County, Arizona rely heavily on foreign workers who cross the border from Mexico each day. Farmer John Boelts, a staunch supporter of President Donald Trump, praises strict border controls but says competing Republican factions have complicated efforts to hire foreign labourers.
author: France 24

title: Texas Republicans cut Tarrant County polling sites by nearly 30% amid rule changes
content: Republicans in Texas are being accused of altering electoral rules ahead of the upcoming U.S. midterm elections. In Tarrant County, near Dallas, the number of election‑day polling places has been reduced by nearly 30 percent, a change that is now being challenged in court. The move follows last year’s statewide redistricting, which was described as a measure intended to benefit Republicans, and officials note it could also energize Democratic opposition. The report was delivered by France 24’s Pierrick Leurent, with Wassim Cornet.
summary: Republicans in Texas are accused of changing electoral rules, including cutting election‑day polling places in Tarrant County by nearly 30 percent. The reduction is being challenged in court and follows last year’s statewide redistricting designed to benefit Republicans, which Democrats say could galvanize their opposition.
author: France 24

title: Germany cautious on Israeli election results, politicians await coalition
content: German politicians are responding cautiously to the Israeli election outcome, waiting to determine the likely composition of the next coalition. Many also express a preference for a German government that does not include religious hard‑liners.
summary: German politicians have been slow to respond to the Israeli election results as they wait to see who will likely comprise the next coalition. Many are hoping for a government without religious hardliners.
author: DW World

title: Houthis siege pushes Taiz toward “stone age,” governor says
content: Oxygen, food and water supplies running low and massacres taking place, says Nabil Shamsan The Houthis are trying to send the city of Taiz back to the stone age, the city’s governor said in a briefing designed to urge the international community to do more to lift the month-long siege. Nabil Shamsan said massacres were taking place in Yemen’s third city, that oxygen and water supplies were running out and that rubbish was piling up in the streets due to landfill sites being either full or inaccessible.
summary: Governor Nabil Shamsan said the Houthis are trying to send Taiz back to the stone age during a month‑long siege. He reported that oxygen, food and water supplies are running low, massacres are occurring, and rubbish is piling up because landfill sites are full or inaccessible.
author: Guardian World

title: Spain's snap election reshaped after train disaster, Sánchez defends safety record
content:
Spain’s snap general election, scheduled for next month, follows a recent train disaster, reshaping the political contest. Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez, leader of the Spanish Socialist Workers’ Party (PSOE), now faces the task of defending his government’s safety record amid the heightened scrutiny.

The election was called after right‑wing and far‑right parties voted down housing reforms that Sánchez’s coalition had announced in response to angry protests, altering the dynamics of the race.
summary: Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez called a snap general election for next month after right‑wing and far‑right parties voted down his coalition’s housing reforms. The election now forces Sánchez to defend his government’s safety record.
author: Guardian World

title: Novaya Gazeta to close citing pressure from Russian special services
content:
The Russian independent newspaper Novaya Gazeta has announced it will shut down, citing pressure from authorities. In a video statement posted on YouTube, editor‑in‑chief Sergei Sokolov said the paper is “ceasing to exist” because the Russian special services have forced the editorial team to end its work.

The closure follows recent actions by Russian authorities, including a search of the home of the newspaper’s senior editor and the detention of one of its journalists earlier this year. The outlet, noted for its independent reporting and for having a former editor who won a Nobel Peace Prize, has not provided further details on the circumstances leading to its shutdown.
summary: Novaya Gazeta announced it will cease operations, saying Russian authorities forced the decision. The closure follows a recent search of a senior editor’s home and the earlier detention of a journalist, according to editor-in-chief Sergei Sokolov.
author: Guardian World

title: Student List supporters vow to dismiss senior police officials after election win
content: After improbable election victory, the unconventional grassroots movement says it will prioritise dismissal of corrupt officials In Belgrade’s Pioneers Park, just across from the national assembly, a small crowd craned their necks to listen. One woman held aloft a placard reading “Love prevailed for the people and Serbia”. With a bouquet of media microphones in front of them, members of the Student List, the direct democracy movement that won an improbable but decisive victory in Sunday’s election, gathered under the trees. Having spent days bathing in the euphoria of their unexpected triumph, the candidates’ focus was now clear: the cleaning up of the rotten institutions that had increasingly blighted the lives of Serbs over the 14 years of government by the populist leader Aleksandar Vučić and his Serbian Progressive party (SNS). They called for the dismissal of many senior law enforcement officials, among them the chiefs of the criminal police, the paramilitary gendarmerie and an anti-terrorism unit.
summary: The Student List, a direct‑democracy movement that won an improbable but decisive victory in Sunday’s election, gathered in Belgrade’s Pioneers Park and said it will prioritize removing corrupt officials. It called for the dismissal of senior law‑enforcement leaders, including the chiefs of the criminal police, the paramilitary gendarmerie and an anti‑terrorism unit.
author: Guardian World

title: 27 nationalities may be among victims of Spain train crash, Sánchez says
content:
Some 69 people have been confirmed dead in the Spain train crash, with the toll possibly rising as at least 70 people are reported missing. According to Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez, victims may include people of 27 different nationalities.

Peunte began by paying tribute to all affected by the incident. He said that “at present, evidence points to a failure within Adif’s command and control centre,” while noting that investigators are still working “to clarify what exactly happened.” Peunte added that he still has confidence in the system.
summary: Some 69 people have been confirmed dead and at least 70 are reported missing after the crash. Sánchez said evidence points to a failure in Adif’s command and control centre while investigators continue to clarify what happened.
author: Guardian World

title: Beijing Queer Film Festival cancelled after harassment by authorities
content: Beijing’s annual independent queer film festival, one of the country’s oldest independent film festivals, was cancelled after what is understood to have been a campaign of sustained harassment from authorities. The event had been scheduled to begin on Friday in the capital. Experts note that forums for discussion of feminist and LGBTQ + views are encountering growing intolerance from the Chinese state.
summary: Beijing’s annual independent queer film festival was cancelled after what is understood to have been a campaign of sustained harassment from authorities. The festival, one of China’s oldest independent film festivals, was due to begin on Friday in the capital.
author: Guardian World

title: Severe rain and flood warnings issued for central Greece, western Turkey
content:
Turkey has experienced powerful thunderstorms this week, including a tornado in Antalya that killed four construction workers on Tuesday. The storms are part of a low‑pressure system that is also bringing heavy rain and strong winds to parts of south‑eastern Europe and Turkey.

In response, authorities in Greece and Turkey have issued severe rainfall and flood warnings for central Greece and western Turkey, where 100‑150 mm of rain is forecast for the week, with the possibility of higher local totals.

The same weather pattern is affecting India, where Cyclone Arnab made landfall in Odisha and Andhra Pradesh, producing wind gusts over 85 mph and rainfall exceeding 200 mm. The cyclone has prompted evacuations of more than 180,000 people and disrupted energy and transport services, and it is expected to weaken while continuing to bring rain to northern and central India.
summary: Authorities in Greece and Turkey have issued severe rainfall and flood warnings as 100‑150 mm of rain is forecast for central Greece and western Turkey this week. A powerful thunderstorm in Antalya produced a tornado that killed four construction workers.
author: Guardian World

title: Liverpool beat Chelsea as three join penalty hall of shame
content: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Football Daily isn’t suggesting standards at Chelsea have slipped in recent years, but the quality of their players who miss penalties in shootouts against Liverpool certainly appears to be on the slide. Before last night, footballing royalty such as Arjen Robben, Geremi, Tammy Abraham, César Azpilicueta, Mason Mount and even goalkeeper Kepa Arrizabalaga had all missed from the spot in four consecutive post-match deciders against Liverpool across 19 years and four different competitions. On Wednesday, a flame-haired Argentinian irritant, a striker we’d never previously heard of before yesterday and a defensive liability whose boots increasingly look to have been welded on to the wrong feet each added their names to the roll of shame. Valentín Barco, Emanuel Emegha and Wesley Fofana, take a collective bow. The reaction when Fleetwood made the final penalty was the best example I’ve ever seen of pandemonium! – Jim Geissman A few random thoughts from one of the Wednesday fans who saw Harry Kane’s first goal at Orient ( Tuesday’s Football Daily ). Main after match conversation topics were how we’d shipped four goals in the second half, our new signing Gary Madine, and those people on the balconies of the new flats who watched the game for free. Without cameras I’d have no recall of Harry Kane’s goal but funnily enough I do genuinely remember Dean Cox having a very good game. We’ve talked about it loads since, but I don’t think any of us at the time thought Kane stood out in that game. Which just goes to show. A thoroughly deserved award for a career of consistent & often under-appreciated excellence. And what a superb motto: “Work in silence. Let success be your voice” – Alan. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version, just visit this page and follow the instructions.
summary: Liverpool beat Chelsea, and three players—Valentín Barco, Emanuel Emegha and Wesley Fofana—joined the penalty hall of shame. They missed penalties in shootouts against Liverpool across 19 years and four competitions.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Fleetwood Town defeat Arsenal in League Cup as Michael Carrick stays on United bench
content: In a Football Weekly Extra video, Max Rushden is joined by Barry Glendenning, Dan Bardell and Seb Hutchinson. They discuss Fleetwood Town’s League Cup win over Arsenal and note that Michael Carrick remains in the dugout at Manchester United.
summary: Fleetwood Town beat Arsenal in the League Cup. Michael Carrick remains in the dugout at Manchester United.
author: Guardian Sport

title: MLS sets 2027 sprint season start for Feb 19, Cup on Memorial Day
content: Season will begin on 19 February in Miami MLS Cup due to be played on Memorial Day weekend Decision Day lands on 8 May Major League Soccer’s 2027 “sprint season” will begin on 19 February, with MLS Cup taking place during Memorial Day weekend at the end of May. The stopgap half-season is a one-off, as the North American league inverts its calendar to align with most top leagues around the world beginning with the 2027-28 season. The nuts and bolts of the change were initially announced in March.
summary: Major League Soccer announced that its 2027 sprint season will begin on 19 February, with MLS Cup played during Memorial Day weekend. This one-off stopgap half-season precedes the league's permanent calendar inversion starting with the 2027-28 season.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Les Kiss backs Beale to compete for Wallabies World Cup spot
content: Australia coach says recalled 37-year-old adds depth to tour squad Tom Hooper overcomes injury to be available for Nations Championship Coach Les Kiss says veteran playmaker Kurtley Beale is in consideration for Australia’s Rugby World Cup squad after his shock recall for the Wallabies’ spring tour of the UK. Beale answered Kiss’s SOS call for next month’s three Tests against England, Scotland and Wales, before the inaugural Nations Championship finals from November 21-23.
summary: Australia coach Les Kiss states that recalled 37-year-old Kurtley Beale is in consideration for the Rugby World Cup squad following his selection for the spring tour. Beale will join the Wallabies for three Tests against England, Scotland, and Wales before the Nations Championship finals.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Packers beat Panthers 27-19 as Christian Watson returns after hospital visit
content:
The Green Bay Packers defeated the Carolina Panthers 27-19 on Thursday night, overcoming three turnovers to secure a victory that improved their record to 5-3. Quarterback Jordan Love completed 30 of 41 passes for 288 yards and three touchdowns, while also throwing one interception. His scoring plays came on passes to Tucker Kraft, Matthew Golden, and running back Josh Jacobs. Jacobs contributed significantly on the ground and in the end zone, rushing for 39 yards on 21 carries and scoring on a four-yard reception and a one-yard run.

Wide receiver Christian Watson returned to the game after a mid-game hospital visit, finishing with 113 receiving yards despite the injury interruption. The Packers successfully managed the game against the Panthers, who finished with 19 points, in a match where Green Bay’s offensive performance highlighted their ability to convert drives into touchdowns.
summary: Green Bay defeated Carolina 27-19 on Thursday night despite three turnovers, with Jordan Love throwing three touchdown passes. Wide receiver Christian Watson recorded 113 receiving yards after returning from a mid-game hospital visit.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Senators Warren, Collins Press Kalshi and Polymarket Over Election Markets
content: Senators Elizabeth Warren (D‑Mass.) and a bipartisan partner have written to Kalshi and Polymarket, expressing concerns about election‑related prediction markets tied to the Nov. 3 midterm elections. They request detailed information on the companies’ measures to prevent insider trading, market manipulation, and wagers based on material nonpublic information.
summary: A bipartisan pair of senators is requesting information from Kalshi and Polymarket regarding their efforts to prevent insider trading and market manipulation. The senators expressed concerns about prediction markets tied to the Nov. 3 midterm elections.
author: The Hill

title: Trump launches culture war attacks on Andrews during final rally for Graham
content: President Trump delivered culture war attacks against Democratic Senate nominee Annie Andrews during his third and final campaign rally for Sen. Darline Graham (R) in South Carolina on Thursday. In his remarks, Trump stated that Graham has devoted her life to the state and is running to protect residents from a radical left.
summary: President Trump attacked Democratic Senate nominee Annie Andrews during his third and final campaign rally for Sen. Darline Graham (R) in South Carolina. He described Graham as devoted to the state and said she is running to protect voters from a radical left.
author: The Hill

title: Arizona reports first New World screwworm case in dog
content: Arizona reported its first confirmed case of New World screwworm on Wednesday, becoming the third state affected by the parasite. The case was identified in a domestic dog in Cochise County, which borders Mexico, according to a U.S. Department of Agriculture press release.
summary: Arizona reported its first case of New World screwworm, making it the third state impacted by the parasite. The confirmed case was found in a domestic dog in Cochise County, which shares a border with Mexico.
author: The Hill

title: Alaska Governor Says Election Certification Could Be Stopped Over Peltola Probe
content: Alaska Governor Mike Dunleavy (R) said on Thursday that the state’s midterm election certification process could be “stopped or changed” because of an investigation into ballot‑stacking allegations against Democratic Senate candidate Mary Peltola. The probe was announced by the governor earlier that day, and NewsNation’s Blake Burman asked whether it could affect the certification.
summary: Alaska Governor Mike Dunleavy said the state's midterm election certification could be stopped or changed because of a probe into ballot stacking allegations against Democratic Senate candidate Mary Peltola. He announced the probe earlier that day during a NewsNation interview with Blake Burman.
author: The Hill

title: Trump to hold tele-rallies in 19 states after canceling in-person events
content: The Republican National Committee announced Thursday that President Trump will participate in tele-rallies across 19 states before Election Day. This 72-hour campaign sprint follows the cancellation of two in-person events in Iowa and Kansas. The RNC stated that voters across the country want to hear from the President, describing the upcoming appearances as a significant boost for the party.
summary: The Republican National Committee announced that President Trump will hold tele-rallies in 19 states before Election Day. The announcement followed his cancellations of in-person events in Iowa and Kansas and is part of a 72‑hour sprint to boost voter outreach.
author: The Hill

title: Bresnahan and Cognetti Clash Over Iran War and Data Centers in PA House Debate
content: On Thursday night, Rep. Rob Bresnahan (R‑Pa.) and Democrat Paige Cognetti faced off on the Pennsylvania House debate stage. They debated the war in Iran, the expanding presence of data centers in their district, and other hot‑button topics. Cognetti, mayor of Scranton since 2020, and Bresnahan are competing to represent Pennsylvania’s 8th Congressional District.
summary: Rep. Rob Bresnahan (R-Pa.) and Democrat Paige Cognetti clashed on the debate stage Thursday night over the ongoing war in Iran, the growing presence of data centers in their district and other hot-button issues.
author: The Hill

title: Binance suspected hack prompts $3B freeze by crypto firms
content: Binance announced that a suspected hack has led crypto firms to freeze roughly $3 billion in assets. The exchange described the situation as a “security issue” and has temporarily halted deposits and withdrawals while it conducts security checks, freezes funds, and works with law enforcement. Binance vowed to cover all losses.
summary: A suspected hack at Binance prompted cryptocurrency firms to freeze about $3 billion in assets. Binance has temporarily suspended deposits and withdrawals, is conducting security checks, freezing funds, working with law enforcement, and vows to cover all losses.
author: The Hill

title: Senate Democrats’ PAC Spends $750,000 on Digital Ads in South Carolina for First Time
content:
Senate Democrats are buying ads in South Carolina for the first time as polls indicate a close Senate contest in the deep‑red state.  

The Senate Majority PAC (SMP), the main political action committee for Senate Democrats in the midterms, will spend $750,000 on digital ads in the Palmetto State for the race between Sen. Darline Graham (R) and the Democratic challenger.
summary: Senate Democrats’ PAC Spends $750,000 on Digital Ads in South Carolina for First Time.
author: The Hill

title: Justice Department Subpoenas Los Angeles Election Workers Amid Trump Administration Tension
content: The Justice Department issued grand jury subpoenas to election workers in Los Angeles last week. These legal actions come amid escalating tensions between the Trump administration and California election officials regarding the state's voter rolls.
summary: The Justice Department issued grand jury subpoenas to election workers in Los Angeles. The subpoenas come amid escalating tensions between the Trump administration and California election officials over the state's voter rolls.
author: NPR Politics

title: First Dog cartoon celebrates small acts of grace
content: First Dog on the Moon has released a cartoon that celebrates small acts of grace. Fans can sign up to receive email notifications whenever new First Dog cartoons are published. The First Dog shop offers merchandise and prints to meet those looking to support the series.
summary: The First Dog cartoon celebrates small acts of grace. Readers can sign up for email updates and buy First Dog merchandise in the shop.
author: Guardian Environment

title: Study links tumor mutations and immune profile to dasatinib response in TFHL patients
content:
Researchers at the University of Tsukuba carried out a physician‑initiated phase 2 clinical trial of dasatinib in patients with relapsed or refractory T‑follicular helper cell lymphoma (TFHL), an aggressive and difficult‑to‑treat blood cancer. The study examined tumor samples and the immune microenvironment of participants receiving the drug.

The investigators identified specific genetic alterations and immune‑activity features that correlated with treatment response. These biomarkers may indicate which patients are more likely to benefit from dasatinib.

The findings, published in Nature Communications, could guide the selection of patients for dasatinib therapy and support the design of personalized treatment strategies and new immunotherapeutic approaches.
summary: Researchers at the University of Tsukuba conducted a physician‑initiated phase 2 trial of dasatinib in patients with relapsed or refractory T‑follicular helper cell lymphoma. The trial identified genetic alterations and immune‑microenvironment features associated with treatment response, which may help select patients likely to benefit.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Brains Trick Us Into Hearing Things That Aren't There at Night
content: The provided text describes a common experience where individuals wake at 3 a.m. after hearing sounds like a thud or creaking floorboard, or feeling the sensation of not being alone. These instances illustrate how the brain can trick people into perceiving auditory or physical sensations that may not correspond to actual external events.
summary: The brain can trick individuals into hearing sounds that are not present in the darkness. These auditory illusions may occur when waking from sleep due to perceived thuds or creaks.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Study Links Low Protein Intake to Kidney Failure Risk in CKD Patients
content:
A study published online on Oct. 22 in JAMA Network Open found that among patients with non‑dialysis‑dependent chronic kidney disease, low protein intake is linked to a higher risk of kidney failure requiring replacement therapy and to increased all‑cause mortality.

The research was released to coincide with Kidney Week, the American Society of Nephrology’s annual meeting, which ran from Oct. 21 to 25 in Denver.
summary: A study published in JAMA Network Open found that low protein intake is associated with an increased risk of kidney failure and all-cause mortality in patients with non-dialysis-dependent chronic kidney disease. The research was released to coincide with the annual meeting of the American Society of Nephrology held in Denver.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Spinal cord injury reshapes gut microbes, study suggests
content: Scientists investigating the relationship between spinal cord injuries, inflammation, and immune function have initiated a genome-level analysis of gut microbial communities. Early results from these studies suggest potential new approaches to facilitate healing.
summary: Scientists exploring the links between a spinal cord injury, inflammation and immune function have turned their attention to a genome-level analysis of the gut microbial community. Early study results offer hints at potential new approaches to aid healing.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Xenon-based method measures MRI contrast metal more sensitively than earlier techniques
content: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) utilizes magnetic fields and low-energy radio waves to generate detailed internal body images without exposing patients to radiation. This procedure is considered indispensable for the diagnosis and treatment planning of various cancers, as it allows for the clear distinction between healthy tissue and pathological changes, such as tumors.
summary: The xenon-based method measures a key MRI contrast metal more sensitively than earlier techniques. MRI uses magnetic fields and low-energy radio waves to produce detailed images that distinguish tumors from healthy tissue without exposing the body to radiation.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Half of Women Unaware of Rising Heart Disease Risk During Menopause, Study Finds
content: Heart disease remains the leading cause of death among women, with risk increasing during menopause. An international study finds that only about half of women are aware of this fact. Many have never discussed heart health with a clinician, and most report experiencing multiple symptoms.
summary: Heart disease is the leading cause of death in women, and the risk rises during menopause. An international study found only half of women know this, many have never talked to a doctor or nurse about their heart, and most are living with multiple symptoms.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Passive Tobacco Smoke Linked to Worse Atopic Dermatitis in 0-2 Year Olds
content:
A study in Advances in Dermatology and Allergology reports that passive tobacco smoke exposure is linked to increased disease severity in children aged 0 to 2 years with nonallergic atopic dermatitis.  

The association is strongest with paternal smoking and postnatal household exposure.
summary: The study found that passive tobacco smoke exposure, especially from fathers and postnatal household exposure, is linked to greater severity of nonallergic atopic dermatitis in children aged 0 to 2 years. The findings were published in Advances in Dermatology and Allergology.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Police to triage 999 mental health calls, attend only if risk or crime
content: A new policy is altering police responses to mental‑health emergencies. All 999 calls will now be triaged. Police will still attend any call that involves a risk of harm to the individual or others, a risk to life, or a crime.
summary: 999 calls will be triaged. If there is any risk of harm or to life, or if a crime is involved, the police will still attend.
author: BBC Health

title: Work Collapse Reveals Hidden Vitamin D Deficiency in UK Youth
content: Doctors report that vitamin D deficiency is becoming more common across the UK, particularly among young people. The condition’s symptoms are subtle and often overlooked, which can delay diagnosis and treatment.
summary: Doctors find vitamin D deficiency increasingly widespread in the UK, especially among young people. Symptoms are difficult to spot and can be missed.
author: BBC Health

title: New Travel Recommendation System Uses Three Algorithms to Personalize Destinations
content: Researchers have created a tourist recommendation system that blends three algorithms to help travelers locate destinations that match their preferences, budgets, and travel routes. The study, published in the International Journal of Work Innovation, tackles a common issue with digital platforms that tend to prioritize popularity over practical considerations.
summary: Researchers have created a tourist recommendation system that combines three algorithms to match travelers with destinations based on preferences, budgets, and travel routes. The system was described in the International Journal of Work Innovation and seeks to counter digital platforms that prioritize popularity over practical considerations.
author: Phys.org

title: New X-ray technique isolates weak interfacial water signals from bulk water
content:
A research team from Toyohashi University of Technology, the Institute for Molecular Science, and the Institute of Science Tokyo, led by Yu Kinjo and professor Ryugo Tero, has developed a new X‑ray method to study water near material surfaces.

The method combines X‑ray absorption spectroscopy with data analysis to isolate the weak signals of interfacial water from the much larger signals of surrounding water, enabling investigation of the state of water at material interfaces.
summary: New X-ray technique isolates weak interfacial water signals from bulk water.
author: Phys.org

title: University of Alicante study finds TV still strong alongside VOD platforms
content: A University of Alicante study of 325 Spanish fiction series released between 2020 and 2024 found that video‑on‑demand platforms have not displaced traditional television. The research indicates that the two distribution models are instead creating new forms of collaboration and content sharing.
summary: A University of Alicante study of 325 fiction series released in Spain between 2020 and 2024 found that video‑on‑demand (VOD) platforms have not replaced traditional television. The research says the two distribution models are developing new ways of collaborating and sharing content.
author: Phys.org

title: Hebrew University researchers develop AI tool to identify hidden soil bacteria
content: Researchers at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem, together with partner institutions, have created an artificial‑intelligence tool designed to interpret DNA collected from soil. While a small amount of soil contains a dense community of bacteria, fungi and other organisms, much of the genetic material remains hard to identify; the new AI system aims to clarify this complex genetic picture.
summary: Soil holds a crowded world of bacteria, fungi and other organisms whose DNA is hard to identify. Researchers at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem and partner institutions have created an artificial intelligence tool to help make sense of this genetic puzzle.
author: Phys.org

title: Study examines aging of lab microplastics and their binding to contaminants
content:
A new study has expanded understanding of how microplastics (MPs) age in the environment and whether they bind to other contaminants during that process. The research examined MPs that are smaller than 5 millimetres (about 0.2 inches) in length, a size range that classifies them as microplastics.

The investigation focused on MPs made from three common polymer chemicals—polyethylene, polyethylene terephthalate, and polypropylene—to determine if aging altered their properties and how such changes might influence the interaction with nearby contaminants.
summary: A newly published study investigated how microplastics age in the environment and whether they stick to other contaminants. The researchers examined aging of polyethylene, polyethylene terephthalate and polypropylene microplastics, which are particles under 5 mm, to assess changes and effects on nearby contaminants.
author: Phys.org

title: U.N. report: 252 million hectares restored in 149 countries, creating 1M+ green jobs
content: A U.N. report says restoration efforts are working but must accelerate to meet targets. It records that 252 million hectares (623 million acres) are being restored in 149 countries, generating more than one million green jobs, and represents the largest documented global restoration effort to date.
summary: U.N. report: 252 million hectares restored in 149 countries, creating 1M+ green jobs.
author: Phys.org

title: NASA, UF researchers test plant disease on ISS for moon and Mars missions
content: NASA and its partners are preparing for longer human missions beyond Earth, and a space‑station experiment will examine plant disease risks that could affect astronauts’ ability to grow fresh food. University of Florida researchers are conducting the study to assess how such diseases might impact future lunar and Mars missions.
summary: NASA and its partners are preparing for longer human missions beyond Earth and are conducting a space‑station experiment on plant disease risks. University of Florida researchers are studying how plant disease could affect astronauts’ ability to grow fresh food for future moon and Mars missions.
author: Phys.org

title: Researchers identify molecular twists that may boost cryptochrome magnetic compass
content: A research team headed by Yasuhiro Kobori of Kobe University, together with collaborators from Toho University, Saitama University, Nagoya Institute of Technology and the University of Freiburg, has identified a potential molecular mechanism that may enhance magnetic‑compass responses in cryptochrome, a blue‑light‑sensitive protein linked to magnetoreception.
summary: A collaborative research team led by Yasuhiro Kobori at Kobe University, together with researchers from Toho University, Saitama University, Nagoya Institute of Technology and the University of Freiburg identified a potential molecular mechanism. The mechanism could enhance magnetic compass responses in cryptochrome, a blue‑light‑sensitive protein implicated in magnetoreception.

title: MIT engineers develop modular nanoparticle platform for personalized cancer vaccines
content:
MIT engineers have designed a nanoscale particle that can serve as a customizable delivery vehicle for personalized cancer vaccines. The platform is built on a modified, harmless bacteriophage known as M13, which forms a nanofiber that can be coated with cancer antigens. By controlling the density of those antigens on the phage’s capsid, the researchers were able to prevent the development of colon tumors in mice.

The study, led by research scientist Shengnan Huang and senior author Angela Belcher, James Mason Crafts Professor of Biological Engineering and Materials Science and Engineering at MIT, appears in the journal Advanced Healthcare Materials. The team also included graduate students Jack Rudrum, Huaiyao Peng and Hao Nghi Luu, all from the Koch Institute. Belcher’s laboratory has used the M13 phage for more than two decades to create nanoscale scaffolds for a variety of applications, and the current work adapts that toolkit for vaccine therapeutics.

To create the vaccine particles, the researchers modified the phage’s major coat protein pVIII by attaching an antigen to its C‑terminus. Adding one or two negatively charged amino acids to the protein sequence increased the density of the displayed antigens, and a separate genetic mutation allowed further fine‑tuning of antigen production. The phage’s single‑stranded DNA also functions as an intrinsic adjuvant by activating the TLR9 pathway, eliminating the need for external adjuvants such as aluminum hydroxide.

In mouse experiments, phages displaying the model antigen SIINFEKL at 35 % density provided stronger protection against melanoma cells than particles with 6 % density, generating more SIINFEKL‑specific T cells and enhancing dendritic‑cell uptake. A separate vaccine displaying the colon‑tumor neoantigen ADPGK at higher density reduced the incidence of colon tumors in a mouse model. The authors suggest that the modular nature of the platform could allow rapid swapping of different antigens to create patient‑specific vaccines for various cancers.

Funding for the research came from the Koch Institute Frontier Research Program, the Marble Center for Cancer Nanomedicine, and the U.S. Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency. Independent commentary from Alberto Danielli, associate professor of molecular biology at the University of Bologna, highlighted the work’s potential to expand the translational use of the M13 phage platform for cancer immunotherapy.
summary: MIT researchers created a nanoscale particle using a modified M13 bacteriophage that can be coated with cancer antigens and whose antigen density can be precisely controlled. In mouse studies, higher‑density versions of the particle prevented colon tumors and protected against melanoma, showing potential for personalized cancer vaccines.
author: MIT News

title: Merryn Glover reflects on shortening autumn days at Loch Insh in the Highlands
content: Loch Insh, Cairngorms: In my three decades in Scotland I’ve adjusted to the darkness of this time of year, and found glory in the quality of light It is the one clear day in a fortnight of heavy cloud, wind and rain, so I am out by the loch, basking in the rays of light, breathing them in, hoarding for the weeks to come. This time of year makes them all the more precious. Here in the Highlands, once we are past the autumnal equinox, we can almost feel the Earth tipping away from the sun as the light grows shorter each day and the night steals back. It’s a turn that is especially obvious when the clocks change and our evenings are suddenly dark.
summary: Merryn Glover describes a rare clear day at Loch Insh in the Cairngorms after a fortnight of heavy cloud, wind and rain. She notes that after the autumnal equinox daylight grows shorter each day, especially when the clocks change and evenings become dark.
author: Guardian Science

title: NASA map identifies 13 possible source sites for ancient Martian meteorite Teghaza 001
content:
A new global map of Mars highlights thirteen sites whose mineralogy and chemistry correspond to those of the Martian meteorite Teghaza 001, one of the most ancient meteorites recovered on Earth. The map, released by NASA’s Photojournal, notes that while the exact source of any Martian meteorite cannot be confirmed, Teghaza 001 contains characteristics that point to the southern‑hemisphere highlands of the planet.

The underlying base map was generated using data from the Mars Orbiter Laser Altimeter aboard NASA’s Mars Global Surveyor mission. Researchers then overlaid information from NASA’s Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter, marking the matching locations with white circles. The image, available as a 1.22 MB JPEG, visualizes these potential source regions for further scientific exploration.
summary: A global map of Mars shows 13 locations whose mineralogy and chemistry match the ancient meteorite Teghaza 001. The map uses data from the Mars Orbiter Laser Altimeter on Mars Global Surveyor and mineralogical data from Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter, linking the meteorite to southern‑hemisphere highlands.
author: NASA News

title: Vega Island Appears as Smirking Skull in Landsat Images
content: Earth Observatory Science Earth Observatory Vega Island Frozen in Fright Earth Earth Observatory Image of the Day EO Explorer Topics All Topics Atmosphere Land Heat & Radiation Life on Earth Human Dimensions Natural Events Oceans Remote Sensing Technology Snow & Ice Water More Content Collections Global Maps World of Change Articles Earth Matters Blog Blue Marble: Next Generation EO Kids Mission: Biomes About About Us Subscribe 🛜 RSS Contact Us Search March 22, 2025 October 10, 2026 Part of an ice-covered Antarctic island has the appearance of a grinning skull in profile, with a rock outcrop as an eye socket and lateral moraine as a mouth. NASA Earth Observatory / Lauren Dauphin Part of an ice-covered Antarctic island has the appearance of a grinning skull in profile. Some of the face has a gray appearance where seasonal snow is gone and bare ice is exposed. NASA Earth Observatory / Lauren Dauphin March 22, 2025 October 10, 2026 Part of an ice-covered Antarctic island has the appearance of a grinning skull in profile, with a rock outcrop as an eye socket and lateral moraine as a mouth. NASA Earth Observatory / Lauren Dauphin Part of an ice-covered Antarctic island has the appearance of a grinning skull in profile. Some of the face has a gray appearance where seasonal snow is gone and bare ice is exposed. NASA Earth Observatory / Lauren Dauphin March 22, 2025 October 10, 2026 Curtain Toggle 2-Up Shrouded in ice in the lonely Weddell Sea, Vega Island is an eerie sight to behold. On this speck of land east of the Antarctic Peninsula, ice, rock outcrops, and glacial moraines combine to create the appearance of a smirking skull in profile looking toward Devil Island. These images show Vega Island’s creepy countenance at the start of austral autumn (left) and in spring (right). They were acquired with the OLI (Operational Land Imager) on Landsat 9 on March 22, 2025, and October 10, 2026, respectively. (Clouds obscured the island in March 2026.) A nunatak jutting out of the ice has the appearance of an eye socket, a lateral moraine forms a mouth, and Bahía del Diablo (Devil’s Bay) Glacier constitutes a jawbone. In the March 2025 image, a layer of snow coats the ice, which is typical of the region’s wettest month. That contrasts with the October 2026 image, when snow is absent from large areas and darker ice surfaces are visible. Above-average temperatures in winter 2026 —particularly in June —were partly responsible for so much bare ice in October, said glaciologist Mauri Pelto of Nichols College. The ice exposed on Vega and nearby islands indicates limited new snow accumulation over the winter, further reduced by sublimation and wind scouring, he said. “The winter season was no treat for these glaciers.” The melt season ahead may also be more trick than treat. Bare ice is darker than snow and absorbs more solar energy, meaning that melting is poised to speed up as the days grow longer and warmer. “Even a thin cover of new snow from a spring storm would be helpful in the short run,” Pelto said. “When entombed in snow and ice, the skull is preserved. But when exposed to melt, it weathers away, which will lead to a changing jawline and expanding eye socket.” October 10, 2026 NASA Earth Observatory/Lauren Dauphin The first comprehensive mapping of Vega Island’s ice was aided by Landsat imagery. In a study published in 1982, scientists described the island’s four ice caps with protruding rocky cliffs and outlet glaciers. They leveraged early Landsat observations along with aerial photos and topographic maps to catalog 29 glaciers on Vega. Of those glaciers, Devil’s Bay Glacier has been closely monitored since the austral summer of 1998-1999, with researchers measuring an overall decline in its mass. Satellite images acquired in recent decades show ice loss from other glaciers on the island as well, with increased areas of exposed bedrock. Long before scientists began tracking its glaciers, Vega was a bright spot in a tale of terror born out of early exploration of the area. The Swedish Antarctic Expedition of 1901-1903 set out to study the geography, geology, climate, and wildlife on and around the eastern Antarctic Peninsula. The party became split into three groups during their explorations, isolated for a winter in different locations. Adding to the horror, they lost their ship to the pack ice. Cape Well-met, as it would come to be known, off the “forehead” of the Vega Island skull, was the site of a happy reunion of two of the groups in spring 1903. Soon thereafter, an Argentinean expedition rescued the survivors of the ordeal. NASA Earth Observatory images by Lauren Dauphin, using Landsat data from the U. S. Geological Survey. title: APOD: 2026 October 30 – Haunting the Cepheus Flare
content: APOD Science APOD APOD: 2026 October 30 –… Today’s APOD Archive Submissions Index Search Calendar RSS Education About Discuss APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. Haunting the Cepheus Flare Explanation: Spooky shapes seem to haunt this dusty expanse, drifting through the night in the royal constellation Cepheus. Of course, the shapes are cosmic dust clouds visible in dimly reflected starlight. Far from your own neighborhood, they lurk above the plane of the Milky Way at the edge of the Cepheus Flare molecular cloud complex some 1,200 light-years away. Over 2 light-years across and brighter than most of the other ghostly apparitions, vdB 141 or Sh2-136 is also known as the Ghost Nebula. It lies at lower right in the starry field of view. Inside the Ghost Nebula are reddish telltale signs of dense cores collapsing in the early stages of star formation. With the eerie hue of interstellar dust reflecting bluish light from hot young stars of NGC 7023, the Iris Nebula stands out against the dark just left of center. In the broad telescopic frame, these fertile interstellar dust fields stretch almost six full moons across the sky.
