title: Show HN: Lasm Enables Formal Verification of Web Apps in Lean for Node, Serverless, Edge
content:
Lasm is a new project that extends the Lean programming language to browser, Node, serverless and edge environments, enabling developers to write full‑stack web applications—both frontend and backend—in Lean and to formally verify those applications. The author describes Lasm as a long‑standing goal for 2026 and positions it as a way to combine general‑purpose software development with Lean’s built‑in formal verification capabilities.

According to the post, the system can support typical web‑server frameworks such as Express or Hono running on platforms like Cloudflare Workers, with the specification of the server formally verified. The author identifies themselves as an “agentic engineer” focused on software engineering and notes that most of the implementation was generated by the language model Claude Opus 5.5 under their high‑level direction. The announcement was shared as a Show HN entry on Hacker News, receiving 21 points and three comments.
summary: Lasm brings Lean to the browser, Node, serverless, and edge environments, allowing developers to write and formally verify web applications from frontend to backend. The project was built largely by Claude Opus 5.5 with the author's high‑level direction, and the author describes themselves as an agentic engineer with an emphasis in software engineering.
author: Hacker News

title: SuperMe raises $20M for its network of AI expert profiles
content: SuperMe announced that it has raised $20 million to grow its network of AI expert profiles. The platform creates AI representations of real‑life specialists and, when a user submits a question, it selects the most suitable experts and initiates a group chat with their AI profiles.
summary: SuperMe is a network of AI profiles that draws on the knowledge of real-life experts. The platform creates a group chat of the best‑suited AI profiles to answer a user's question.
author: TechCrunch

title: Ex-Palantir execs launch Dream with $17M a16z to build AI construction world models
content:
Ex‑Palantir executives have launched Dream, a new AI venture focused on construction, with $17 million in funding from a16z.  

Dream’s world model is built on real physics and construction standards. It is trained on more than 100 million square feet of building data gathered from permit archives across the United States.
summary: Dream is grounded in real physics and construction standards. Just as LLMs learn from text, Dream's world model is trained on more than 100 million square feet of building data gathered from permit archives across the United States.
author: TechCrunch

title: Midterms could punish Republicans after promise of change
content: The article notes that two years after the wave of discontent that helped Donald Trump and the Republicans gain total control of Washington, the same call for change is now directed at them. It suggests that America’s midterm elections could serve as a punishment for the party that once promised change.
summary: The change message that propelled Donald Trump and the Republicans to total control of Washington is now aimed at them. The upcoming midterms could punish the party that promised change.
author: Euronews

title: India’s food safety faces rising adulteration and regulatory challenges
content: India’s food industry supplies more than a billion people each day, but guaranteeing that the products reaching consumers are safe has become increasingly difficult. The country has seen a rise in food‑adulteration incidents, some of which have resulted in fatal outcomes. Growing concerns about adulteration and poor hygiene are prompting questions about whether regulators can effectively oversee such a vast sector.
summary: India's food industry feeds more than a billion people every day, but ensuring safety has become an increasingly difficult challenge. A rise in food adulteration cases with sometimes fatal consequences has led to questions about regulators' ability to effectively oversee the sprawling sector.
author: France 24

title: US fires Army Lt. Gen. Brett Sylvia, top Joint Chiefs strategist
content: The United States has dismissed its top military planner, a move reported by The Atlantic on Wednesday. Army Lieutenant General Brett Sylvia was removed this week from his position as head of strategy, plans and policy on the Joint Chiefs of Staff. The ouster comes amid a surprise shake‑up as President Donald Trump appears to be preparing to resume large‑scale strikes against Iran. According to the report, Sylvia’s departure is the latest in a series of high‑profile military exits since Trump returned to power a year ago.
summary: The United States fired Army Lieutenant General Brett Sylvia, who headed strategy, plans and policy on the Joint Chiefs of Staff. The Atlantic reported the surprise removal on Wednesday as President Donald Trump appears to be preparing to resume large‑scale strikes against Iran.
author: France 24

title: Ireland welcomes Americans fleeing President Donald Trump
content: FRANCE 24 reports that tens of thousands of U.S. citizens have left the United States since Donald Trump returned to power two years ago. Ireland, citing a common language and shared history, is among the top destinations for these Americans, with the country reportedly opening its arms to those fleeing the Trump administration.
summary: Tens of thousands of US citizens have fled the United States since Donald Trump's return to power two years ago. Ireland has been among the top choices for those Americans, FRANCE 24's team reports.
author: France 24

title: Real estate scams rise in Ivory Coast amid housing shortage
content: Severe housing shortages in Ivory Coast have driven up demand for land, according to this week’s “Across Africa” briefing. The heightened demand has opened a window for fraudsters who are selling fake properties and plots that do not exist, indicating a growth in real‑estate scams across the country. The report highlights the link between the shortage and the rise in fraudulent land sales, underscoring a widening problem for prospective buyers in Ivory Coast.
summary: In Ivory Coast, a severe housing shortage has driven demand for land, prompting fraudsters to sell fake properties and nonexistent plots. Kenya’s female athletes are delivering major sporting successes, and Addis Ababa is advancing plans to become East Africa’s clean‑energy powerhouse.
author: France 24

title: Tunisia families seek answers for men conscripted into Russia's war in Ukraine
content:
Concern is growing in Tunisia as families of several men who travelled to Russia for work or study remain without answers about the fate of their loved ones who have been forcibly conscripted into the war in Ukraine. The families are still searching for information on the men’s whereabouts and status.

In related regional coverage, a year after Tanzania’s controversial election, fear among the population has not faded, while Dakar prepares to host the first Olympic event ever held on African soil, set to begin this weekend.
summary: Concern is growing in Tunisia as families of several men who travelled to Russia for work or study search for answers about the fate of loved ones forcibly conscripted to the war in Ukraine. The story is featured in tonight's edition.
author: France 24

title: North Korea tests attack drones, missiles, rockets as Kim urges faster AI development
content: North Korea conducted a weapons demonstration in which it tested attack drones, cruise missiles and rocket launchers, state media reported on Friday. During the event, Kim Jong Un urged accelerated development of military drone and artificial‑intelligence technology. The drills come after earlier weapons trials amid heightened tensions with South Korea.
summary: North Korea tested attack drones, cruise missiles and rocket launchers at a weapons demonstration, state media reported Friday. Kim Jong Un called for faster development of military drone and artificial intelligence technology amid rising tensions with South Korea.
author: France 24

title: Netanyahu coalition leads but lacks majority after Israel election
content: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s coalition secured the largest share of seats in the recent general election but finished eight seats shy of a parliamentary majority, according to the final results released on Friday. Arab party groupings are now seen as potential kingmakers, while allegations of foreign interference are reported to complicate the coalition‑building process.
summary: Netanyahu's coalition won the most seats in the election but was eight seats short of a parliamentary majority, according to final results released Friday. Arab party groupings could become kingmakers, and allegations of foreign interference may complicate government formation.
author: France 24

title: Binance breach impacts $6.3 billion, could be biggest crypto heist
content: Binance announced Thursday that a security breach impacted roughly $6.3 billion in assets, a figure that could represent the largest cryptocurrency theft on record. The exchange, described as the world’s largest crypto platform, said it has recovered or frozen about $3 billion of the affected funds, and the incident caused Bitcoin and other digital currencies to fall.
summary: Binance said a security breach affected an estimated $6.3 billion in assets, potentially the biggest cryptocurrency heist on record. The exchange said it had recovered or frozen about $3 billion, and the incident sent Bitcoin and other digital currencies lower.
author: France 24

title: Antisemitism envoy Jillian Segal proposes ombudsman to monitor ABC, SBS Gaza coverage
content: Jillian Segal says perception of link between coverage of conflicts and hostility towards Jewish Australians ‘is itself a matter of public importance’ Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast The federal government’s antisemitism envoy has proposed an “external independent ombudsman” to monitor ABC and SBS coverage of the war in Gaza, and a requirement that all visa applicants be screened for “the risk of holding antisemitic views”. In an updated plan released on Friday, Jillian Segal said Australia’s two public broadcasters should be subjected to greater oversight.
summary: The federal government’s antisemitism envoy Jillian Segal has proposed an external independent ombudsman to monitor ABC and SBS coverage of the war in Gaza. The updated plan also calls for visa applicants to be screened for the risk of holding antisemitic views and for greater oversight of the two public broadcasters.
author: Guardian World

title: Report warns feral deer could become Australia’s next feral pig problem
content:
An unpublished government report on feral deer warns that Australia is not succeeding in halting the species’ expansion. The assessment of the national feral‑deer action plan for the five‑year period 2020‑2025 found that the invasive animal has spread further and increased in numbers, imposing costs of millions of dollars on farmers.

The report notes that feral deer are now encroaching on major cities, leading to more frequent human‑deer encounters. One highlighted incident involved two men who were fined after becoming lost in the bush when they were startled by deer while nude sunbathing. The advocate cited in the report cautions that, without prompt action, feral deer could become “Australia’s next feral pig” problem.
summary: Report warns feral deer could become Australia’s next feral pig problem.
author: Guardian World

title: Former Sydney childcare worker Ashley Paul Griffith charged with 202 more child abuse offences
content: NSW police say charges include child rape and relate to 23 alleged victims aged between one and five at a Sydney childcare centre Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast One of Australia’s most notorious paedophiles is facing hundreds more child abuse charges, including for the alleged rape of children as young as one. Days after being extradited from Queensland to New South Wales, Ashley Paul Griffith was hit with 202 charges dating from between 2014 and 2017, with police labelling the allegations “deeply disturbing”.
summary: NSW police say the 202 charges include child rape and involve 23 alleged victims aged one to five at a Sydney childcare centre. The charges, dating from 2014 to 2017, were laid days after Griffith was extradited from Queensland to New South Wales.
author: Guardian World

title: El Niño drought triggers national crisis in Papua New Guinea as rivers dry and farms fail
content: As many as 8 million people have been affected by food shortages, electricity blackouts and health clinic closures Extreme drought driven by an historic El Niño is affecting as many as 8 million people in Papua New Guinea, causing a cascade of issues from shortages of food and water, to electricity scarcity and schooling disruption. An influential coalition that includes churches, trade unions and business groups has said the Pacific nation is in the midst of a “national crisis”, but there appears to be “no coordinated plan to protect vulnerable communities from the worsening impacts of El Niño.”
summary: El Niño drought triggers national crisis in Papua New Guinea as rivers dry and farms fail.
author: Guardian World

title: Sudanese diaspora and human rights groups denounce UAE nominee Lana Nusseibeh for UN chief
content:
Members of the Sudanese diaspora and international human‑rights monitors have publicly denounced the candidacy of Emirati diplomat Lana Nusseibeh for the United Nations secretary‑general post. Their criticism focuses on Nusseibeh’s denial of accusations that the United Arab Emirates is fueling Sudan’s war by supporting the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces.

The United Arab Emirates nominated Nusseibeh last week to succeed António Guterres, whose second five‑year term ends this year, disrupting a previously gridlocked selection process.
summary: Sudanese diaspora and human rights groups denounce UAE nominee Lana Nusseibeh for UN chief.
author: Guardian World

title: Illegal gold mining creates sinkholes and scarred land in Johannesburg's Roodepoort
content:
Illegal gold mining remains a persistent problem in the townships west of Johannesburg, as illustrated by the experiences of Cora Bailey, a wildlife‑rehabilitation worker. Since beginning her work in 1991, Bailey has repeatedly encountered illegal miners—known locally as zama zamas—while treating injured animals in the Roodepoort area.

The recent surge in gold prices has intensified activity in abandoned mine shafts. In late September, dozens of zama zamas appeared on a dirt road adjacent to Bailey’s charity, Claw (Community‑Led Animal Welfare), to dig for gold. Police efforts to curb the practice appear ineffective, leaving the community and wildlife rehabilitation efforts in a precarious position.
summary: Cora Bailey has been encountering illegal miners since she began treating injured animals in Roodepoort townships in 1991. In late September dozens of zama zamas arrived to dig for gold near her charity, Claw, as rising gold prices have spurred activity in abandoned mine shafts while police action appears ineffective.
author: Guardian World

title: Hyrox athlete Joanna Wietrzyk, who soiled herself in race, says backlash was traumatic
content: Hyrox competitor Joanna Wietrzyk, who soiled herself during a race, said in her first BBC interview that she acknowledges putting others at risk and accepts responsibility for the incident. She added that the severe backlash she received was traumatic and undeserved.
summary: Joanna Wietrzyk said she takes responsibility for soiling herself during a Hyrox race and acknowledges she put others at risk. She added that the severe backlash she received was traumatic and undeserved.
author: BBC World

title: Three dead after Robinson R22 and Airbus helicopter collide near Oregon airport
content: Three people were killed when two helicopters collided midair near an Oregon airport on Thursday afternoon. The aircraft involved were a Robinson R22 and an Airbus helicopter, and both fell into a field next to a highway.
summary: A Robinson R22 and an Airbus helicopter collided midair near an Oregon airport on Thursday afternoon, crashing into a field beside a highway. The crash left three people dead.
author: BBC World

title: On this day in space! Oct. 29, 1991: NASA's Galileo spacecraft flies by asteroid Gaspra and snaps amazing photos while flying at 18,000 mph
content:
On October 29, 1991, NASA’s Galileo spacecraft executed a historic flyby of the asteroid Gaspra, marking the first time a spacecraft visited an asteroid. The probe was en route to Jupiter, the largest planet in the solar system, and had been traveling through the asteroid belt for approximately two months prior to the encounter. During the flyby, Galileo was located 990 miles (1,593 kilometers) from Gaspra while moving at a relative speed of about 5 miles (8 km) per second, a velocity equivalent to 18,000 mph. Gaspra orbits near the inner edge of the asteroid belt, and the flyby served as a midpoint in the spacecraft’s six-year journey.

The Galileo spacecraft captured several photographs of Gaspra and utilized an instrument known as the Near-Infrared Mapping Spectrometer to analyze the asteroid’s chemical composition and physical properties. The resulting images revealed that Gaspra possesses an irregular and elongated shape, measuring roughly 12 miles long and 7 miles wide. NASA’s overview described the body as a cratered, complex, irregular object approximately 20 by 12 by 11 kilometers (12.4 by 7.4 by 6.8 miles) in size, covered by a thin layer of dust and rubble. Joseph Veverka, a member of the Galileo imaging team, noted that the asteroid appeared to be a survivor of a series of catastrophic collisions in its history.

Despite the detailed imaging and spectral data, Galileo was unable to determine the mass of Gaspra because the spacecraft was too far away for the asteroid’s gravity to exert a measurable effect on its trajectory. The flyby occurred after Galileo was launched in October 1989 and performed gravity-assist swings by Venus and Earth in 1990. This encounter with Gaspra was a significant milestone in space exploration, demonstrating the capability to conduct close-range observations of small bodies in the solar system.

Following the Gaspra flyby, Galileo continued its mission by flying by Earth a second time in 1992 and passing close to the asteroid Ida in 1993. The spacecraft eventually arrived at Jupiter in 1995, where it was positioned to observe the Comet Shoemaker-Levy 9 breaking apart and colliding with the planet in July 1994. The success of the Gaspra flyby paved the way for future missions, including NASA’s NEAR mission to land on asteroid Eros, sample-return missions such as OSIRIS-REx and Japan’s Hayabusa, and the DART mission, which intentionally crashed into an asteroid to test planetary protection techniques.
summary: On Oct. 29, 1991, the Galileo spacecraft flew by the asteroid Gaspra on its way to Jupiter.

title: Brewers manager Pat Murphy takes shot at ‘horseshit’ Yankees team after World Series win
content:
Milwaukee Brewers manager Pat Murphy criticized the 2023 New York Yankees as a “horseshit” team following his club’s World Series victory on Wednesday night. In a video released after the clinching game, Murphy was heard speaking to Jake Bauers, who is set to become a free agent.

Murphy told Bauers, “You’re going to be a rich fucker. Just remember when you were on that horseshit Yankees team and you guys were all playing for yourself? Just remember, say, ‘This is the way we used to do it.’” The comments were part of a broader discussion where Murphy alleged the Brewers exposed baseball’s biggest lie.

title: George Russell determined not to let disappointing F1 season define career
content: 28-year-old still believes he will win world title one day Kimi Antonelli misses media duties with ‘viral illness’ George Russell has insisted he will not let his difficult Formula One season define his career and believes he still has plenty of years left to come back and win the world championship. Russell has been outdriven by his 20-year-old Mercedes teammate Kimi Antonelli in a bruising season for the British driver. Antonelli is set to win the title and become F1’s youngest world champion at this weekend’s Mexican Grand Prix if he finishes in ninth place or above.
summary: George Russell determined not to let disappointing F1 season define career.

title: Everton beat Newcastle to reach Carabao Cup quarter-final at Fleetwood
content: The biggest night in Everton’s season started with a big call from David Moyes and demanded a big performance from his players. With the exception of Jack Grealish, they did not let him down. A quarter-final at Fleetwood Town is their prize after a clinical, committed display shattered Newcastle’s hopes of lifting the Carabao Cup for a second time in three seasons. Newcastle dominated spells of the fourth round tie and the stats – registering 28 shots to Everton’s 11, although only nine visiting attempts were on target – but individual defensive errors and an ineffective attack proved a ruinous combination. Matthias Jaissle denied his team are a soft touch, despite persuasive evidence to the contrary, yet called Newcastle “naive” and the defeat, in front of almost 8,000 of their fans, “shocking”. Andy Burnham was among the many Evertonians in attendance grateful for Newcastle’s generosity.
summary: Everton defeated Newcastle United in the Carabao Cup fourth round to secure a quarter-final match at Fleetwood Town. Manager David Moyes left Jack Grealish out of the starting lineup for the decisive victory.

title: UCLA researchers find p53 can strengthen cancer-fighting immune cells
content: Researchers at the UCLA Health Jonsson Comprehensive Cancer Center have identified a new strategy to enhance the strength and potential longevity of cancer-fighting immune cells. This discovery could improve the effectiveness of immunotherapies that utilize a patient's own immune cells to attack cancer.

title: Psychedelic therapies advance to late-stage trials for depression treatment
content: Researchers are exploring how psychedelics might provide antidepressant benefits while avoiding hallucinogenic effects, moving the topic beyond basic research. Several therapies based on classical psychedelics have progressed to late-stage clinical development with encouraging results. Specifically, DT120, an LSD-based candidate, and COMP360, a synthetic psilocybin formulation, have both received breakthrough therapy designation from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration.
summary: Could psychedelics become a new generation of treatments for depression and other psychiatric disorders? This question is no longer confined to basic research.

title: Dietary fat breakdown product linked to chronic psoriatic itch
content: Researchers have identified that a breakdown product from a commonly consumed dietary fat can bind to a receptor linked to psoriatic itch and inflammation. In a mouse model, blocking this receptor resulted in a reduction of psoriatic itch. The study, published in Communications Biology, highlights the potential influence of diet on triggers for chronic itch. This work suggests that future therapies for both psoriasis and atopic dermatitis may be developed based on these findings.
summary: Researchers found that a breakdown product from a commonly consumed fat binds to a receptor associated with psoriatic itch and inflammation. Blocking this receptor reduced psoriatic itch in a mouse model, suggesting diet impacts chronic itch triggers.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Noninvasive tests detect advanced liver scarring, reducing reliance on biopsies
content: Two major international studies provide the strongest evidence to date on noninvasive tests that accurately diagnose and measure the severity of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) and its more severe form, MASH. These findings indicate that such tests can reduce reliance on liver biopsies for detecting advanced liver scarring.
summary: Two major international studies provide the strongest evidence to date on noninvasive tests for diagnosing MASLD and MASH. These tests accurately measure disease severity, which can reduce the need for liver biopsies.
author: Medical Xpress

title: UCSF study links brief dietary changes to altered immune response in mice
content: A UC San Francisco research team discovered that a brief dietary change can significantly alter the body's response to skin irritation in mice. This finding builds on the established understanding that diet influences the immune system, suggesting that short-term dietary choices may impact immune reactions.
summary: A UC San Francisco team found that even a brief dietary change can substantially change how the body responds to skin irritation. The research was conducted on mice, building on the long-known connection between diet and the immune system.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Long-term follow-up tracks benefits and risks of stem cell transplants for severe systemic sclerosis
content: An international study reports that 60% of patients with early severe systemic sclerosis achieved progression-free survival at 10 years following autologous bone marrow transplantation. These findings provide additional evidence supporting the sustained positive clinical outcomes and long-term safety of this treatment approach for the condition.
summary: An international study reports 60% progression-free survival at 10 years after autologous bone marrow transplantation, adding evidence of sustained positive clinical outcomes and long-term safety in patients treated for early severe systemic sclerosis.

title: King's College London study: fruit and veg scraps are high‑fiber, good for health and planet
content: Most people discard fruit and vegetable peels, skins, stalks and seeds at meals. New research from King’s College London indicates that these commonly thrown‑away parts are a rich source of dietary fiber, a finding that could support public‑health nutrition and reduce environmental waste.
summary: Most people discard the peels, skins, stalks and seeds of fruits and vegetables at meals. Research from King's College London indicates these scraps are a valuable source of dietary fiber that could benefit public health and the environment.

title: Simplified ancestral enzyme makes ATP without amino acid needed for its usual reaction
content: Proteins perform essential functions in living organisms, such as catalyzing biochemical reactions and supporting cellular energy metabolism. These functions rely on specific amino acid compositions and three-dimensional structures. However, early proteins likely evolved during a period when fewer amino acid types were available compared to those used by most modern proteins.
summary: Proteins perform essential functions in living organisms, from catalyzing biochemical reactions to supporting cellular energy metabolism. Their functions depend on their amino acid composition and three-dimensional structures.

title: New approach uses electrical guardrails to harness graphene for solar cells
content: Graphene, a single layer of carbon atoms, offers high electron mobility suitable for high-speed electronic components but remains inefficient for converting light into electricity. Although light absorption in graphene excites electrons and creates positively charged carriers known as holes, the energy is not effectively harnessed. To utilize this energy, the electrons and holes must be separated and directed to different contacts, a process that currently limits the material’s solar cell efficiency.
summary: Graphene is promising for high-speed electronics due to high electron mobility but is inefficient at converting light into electricity. Absorbed light energy cannot be harnessed effectively unless electrons and holes are separated and directed to different contacts.

title: Rare 4.1-billion-year-old Martian meteorite reveals clues to planet's ancient past
content: Scientists at the University of New Mexico helped identify a rare 4.1-billion-year-old Martian meteorite. This discovery provides new evidence suggesting the red planet may have once possessed a wetter, Earth-like environment.
summary: Scientists at the University of New Mexico have played a key role in identifying a rare, 4.1-billion-year-old Martian meteorite that provides new evidence that the red planet may have once had a wetter, Earth-like environment.

content: Researchers in eThekwini have utilized machine learning and satellite data to identify zones highly susceptible to landslides. A study published in Scientific Reports indicates that urban development activities, such as road construction, property development, and vegetation loss, are significantly increasing landslide risk across parts of the city.
summary: In eThekwini, researchers have harnessed machine learning and satellite data to spot the city's most landslide-prone zones. content: Researchers from the Institute of Science Tokyo, the University of Zagreb Faculty of Science, and ETH Zürich report that evolutionary changes in isoleucyl-tRNA synthetase (IleRS) may help bacteria fine-tune the speed of protein synthesis.
summary: Evolutionary changes in key enzyme may help bacteria make proteins faster.

title: NASA Image Reveals Minerals in Ancient Martian Meteorite Teghaza 001
content:
NASA/JPL-Caltech has released a new image, designated PIA26801, showing a slice of the Martian meteorite Teghaza 001. According to the provided description, this meteorite is one of the most ancient Martian rocks ever found on Earth, and the specific slice was utilized to determine the age of the rock. The reflected light image serves as a guide for scientists to locate minerals of interest for further analysis using various instruments.

The annotated version of the image highlights several key mineral features that provide insights into Mars’ geological history. Brighter grains represent iron-titanium oxides, while medium gray areas indicate pyroxene; both minerals offer information regarding the formation of Mars’ crust and mantle. Additionally, darker gray areas of shocked plagioclase are identified as resulting from extreme pressures during impacts, including the event that ejected the meteorite into space. The description also notes the presence of fine-grain carbonate, sulfate, and clay minerals, which are attributed to alteration processes that occurred on Earth.
summary: A slice of the Martian meteorite Teghaza 001 was used to determine the rock's age and analyze its mineral composition. The image highlights iron-titanium oxides, pyroxene, and shocked plagioclase, which provide insights into Mars' crust and mantle formation.
author: NASA News

title: Developer uses DOOM mechanics to build transformer model DOOMFORMER
content:
A developer has introduced DOOMFORMER, a project that utilizes the mechanics of the game DOOM to create a transformer model. The creator explains that because DOOM is Turing complete, game mechanics and "voodoo dolls" were employed to perform the mathematical operations required for the model, effectively serving as an alternative to NumPy, albeit with a performance 65,000 times slower.

The project demonstrates several capabilities, including the classification of MNIST digits when written directly on the game map. It also features a communication function described as "kinda" talking and can make decisions to play DOOM. In this scenario, the marine’s mind is controlled by DOOM while playing on a map generated by DOOMFORMER.

The developer notes that larger-scale training of the model can be conducted on a T4 GPU. The post concludes with an invitation for others to collaborate on scaling the project and developing additional features. The submission was posted on Hacker News, where it received seven points and one comment.
summary: The project leverages DOOM's Turing-complete game mechanics to perform mathematical operations, creating an alternative to NumPy. DOOMFORMER can classify MNIST digits, make decisions to play DOOM, and is trainable on a T4 GPU.
author: Hacker News

title: Intel Wildcat Lake Chips Sold Out as Demand Outstrips Supply
content:
During Intel’s latest earnings call, CEO Lip-Bu Tan stated that demand for the company’s budget-focused Wildcat Lake chips is outstripping supply. CFO David Zinsner confirmed that the chips are currently sold out, noting significant growth in the product line. Zinsner emphasized that the chips are cost-optimized and arriving at a time when there is considerable focus on affordability.

These processors are appearing in new, lower-cost Windows laptops, such as the Dell XPS 13 and the HP Omnibook 5 14, which are comparable to the MacBook Neo. This availability comes as shortages of RAM and other components have recently driven up PC prices.
summary: Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan stated that demand for budget-focused Wildcat Lake chips is outstripping supply, with CFO David Zinsner confirming the products are sold out. These cost-optimized chips are appearing in new lower-cost Windows laptops as component shortages drive up PC prices.

title: Reddit to require login for all users, CEO says
content: In the future, you won’t be able to use Reddit without logging in. Reddit CEO Steve Huffman confirmed the impending change in a letter (PDF) to shareholders today about Q3 performance. He said that Reddit is shifting “to a logged-in-only experience," adding: Moving to primarily logged-in will ensure our users have the best Reddit experience possible, and can find the content and communities most relevant to them. It is better for our business because we will have more signals for ads targeting, and being logged-in leads to higher engagement generally. It also allows us to protect access to Reddit’s extremely valuable corpus of data, and helps us better adapt to emerging regulations around the world. Huffman also said that the login requirement will help Reddit better retain new users. Read full article Comments
summary: Reddit CEO Steve Huffman announced that the platform will soon require users to be logged in to access it. He said the change will improve user experience, ad targeting, data protection, regulatory compliance, and new‑user retention.

title: America's Cost-of-Living Crisis Drives Focus on US Midterm Elections
content:
The economy has emerged as the primary concern for American voters, driven by anxieties over elevated food and energy prices. This cost-of-living crisis is currently shaping the landscape of the upcoming US midterm elections. However, experts question the extent to which election outcomes can address these economic challenges.

Greg Ip, chief economics commentator at The Wall Street Journal, noted that there are limited actions any candidate can take to resolve the crisis. He stated, "There isn't a ton that anyone can do about it, regardless of who wins the midterms," suggesting that the November election results may have little direct impact on the ongoing economic pressures.

summary: A humanitarian aid mission will enter the Ukrainian town of Oleshky.
