author: France 24

title: DR Congo Ituri treatment centre celebrates end of confirmed Ebola cases
content: Medical staff and residents at a treatment centre in Ituri, Democratic Republic of Congo, danced and sang to mark a milestone: for the first time since May, the centre is no longer treating any confirmed Ebola cases.
summary: Medical staff and residents at a treatment centre in Ituri danced and sang to celebrate. The centre is no longer treating any confirmed Ebola cases, a first since May.
author: France 24

title: ECB President Christine Lagarde to step down early for non‑policy engagement
content: European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde will step down from her post several months early, in order to have more "freedom to engage on matters that are not monetary policy." The comments will fuel speculation about her future plans, ahead of a presidential election in her native France. The resignation also sparks a succession race, as Europe faces a turbulent fiscal future. Also in the show - oil giant TotalEnergies reports record profits as the EU warns on household energy bills.
summary: European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde will leave her post several months early to gain freedom to engage on matters that are not monetary policy. Her resignation fuels speculation about her future plans ahead of a French presidential election and sparks a succession race as Europe faces a turbulent fiscal future.
author: France 24

title: Drone attack kills five children in Sudan's Nyala market
content: UNICEF reported that a drone strike on a market in Nyala, South Darfur, Sudan, killed at least five children and injured two others on Monday. The agency confirmed the casualties in its Thursday statement.
summary: A drone attack on a market in Nyala, South Darfur, Sudan, killed at least five children and injured two others. UNICEF reported the incident on Thursday.
author: UN News

title: AI changes how we think, raising question of when it will be noticed
content: Artificial intelligence is described as a tool that can write emails, summarize reports, generate ideas and answer complex questions within seconds, promising to make life easier. The technology is portrayed as feeling to many users like a leap comparable to the advent of the internet.
summary: Artificial intelligence promises to make life easier by writing emails, summarizing reports, generating ideas and answering complex questions in seconds. Many people feel the technology represents a leap comparable to the arrival of the internet.
author: UN News

title: UN expert says Myanmar's human rights catastrophic as illicit economy fuels violence
content:
Myanmar’s illicit economy is driving escalating violence, with civilians bearing the brunt of the conflict, according to the headline.  

At a Thursday press briefing, a UN independent expert on Myanmar warned that the country’s human‑rights situation is “catastrophic” as the war continues to spiral with no end in sight.
summary: The UN independent expert described Myanmar's human rights situation as “catastrophic” at a Thursday press briefing. The expert said the war is spiraling with no end in sight as the illicit economy fuels escalating violence that leaves civilians bearing the brunt.
author: UN News

title: Metropolitan Police refers itself to watchdog over handling of 2019 Meghan warning letter
content:
The Metropolitan Police has referred itself to the police watchdog after identifying possible errors in its handling of a 2019 letter that warned of security risks to the Duchess of Sussex posed by her father. The letter contained allegations concerning Thomas Markle, Meghan Markle’s father.

The referral occurs while Philippine police are investigating alleged child‑sexual‑abuse images reportedly found at Thomas Markle Sr.’s former home. Markle denies the claims linking him to the images.
summary: Metropolitan Police refers itself to watchdog over handling of 2019 Meghan warning letter.
author: Guardian World

title: John Healey backs away from welfare cuts amid £28bn public finance shortfall
content:
John Healey has stepped back from plans to cut the cost of welfare during this parliamentary term, doing so after warnings that his first budget could trigger severe spending reductions because of a £28 billion shortfall in public finances.  

The budget was examined by a panel of experts on Thursday, with the Institute for Fiscal Studies noting that Healey avoided making major tax and spending decisions, leaving a substantial fiscal challenge ahead.
summary: John Healey has backed away from cutting the cost of welfare this parliament. The Institute for Fiscal Studies warned his first budget could lead to brutal spending cuts because of a £28bn shortfall and said he ducked big tax and spending decisions.
author: Guardian World

title: Polymarket halts trading on international platform for an hour after security incident
content:
Polymarket announced that it temporarily halted trading on its international platform on Thursday after a security incident compromised a third‑party provider. The incident was linked to a performance‑monitoring tool, prompting the company to pause trading for roughly one hour before resuming operations later that afternoon.

Polymarket said it will fully reimburse any traders who were affected by the interruption. The suspension lasted about an hour and was limited to the international platform.
summary: Polymarket temporarily halted trading on its international platform on Thursday after a security incident compromised a third‑party provider. Trading was paused for about an hour, resumed Thursday afternoon, and the company said it will fully reimburse any affected traders.
author: Guardian World

title: UK experts urge government to treat manosphere and online misogyny as public health issue
content:
UK experts have argued that the manosphere and online misogyny should be addressed as public health issues, comparable to obesity and smoking. In a report published in The Lancet, the authors advocate for a coordinated response involving governments, schools, health services, and community organizations. They suggest this approach mirrors existing public health strategies used to tackle tobacco use and ultra-processed foods.

The report emphasizes the necessity of offering boys "something better" as part of the solution. By framing these online harms within a public health framework, the authors call for a unified effort to mitigate the associated risks through established institutional channels.
summary: A report published in The Lancet calls for the government to address the manosphere and online misogyny as a public‑health problem comparable to obesity and smoking. The authors argue for a coordinated response by governments, schools, health services and community organisations and stress the need to offer boys something better.
author: Guardian World

title: Netanyahu accused of smearing Arab voters after claim foreign backing stole election
content:
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has been accused of using smear tactics to cling to power after he claimed that Arab Israeli parties had used foreign backing to “steal” Tuesday’s election, in which his coalition lost its parliamentary majority.

Netanyahu and his allies called on the internal security service, Shin Bet, to investigate alleged vote buying and other irregularities in Palestinian communities in Israel, supposedly funded by foreign money.
summary: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu claimed Arab Israeli parties used foreign backing to “steal” Tuesday’s election, in which his coalition lost its parliamentary majority. He and his allies asked the Shin Bet security service to investigate alleged vote‑buying and other irregularities in Palestinian communities, saying they were funded by foreign money.
author: Guardian World

title: 55% of Victorian lawyers use AI, but just over a quarter have cut client fees
content:
A new study shows that 55 % of Victorian lawyers are now using artificial‑intelligence tools in their practice, an increase from 37 % a year earlier. Despite broader adoption, the research notes that efficiency gains have not been as high as expected.

Just over a quarter of those surveyed report that AI‑driven efficiency has allowed them to lower client fees. However, lawyers also say that clients turning to chatbots for advice have added to their workload, as they must correct errors produced by the AI.
summary: More than half of Victorian lawyers reported using AI in their work, while just over a quarter said they have reduced client fees because of efficiency gains. They also said clients seeking advice from chatbots have increased their workload as they must correct AI errors.
author: Guardian World

title: Erin Patterson loses appeal, gets longer sentence for mushroom triple murder
content: Court of appeal ruling on the two appeals from 10am in the high profile Australian mushroom triple-murder case Erin Patterson loses appeal as harsher sentence imposed Patterson showed no emotion on the video feed as McLeish outlined why her appeal had failed, and how the director of public prosecutions had succeeded in seeking a longer sentence. Patterson’s actions mean it is ‘inappropriate’ to fix non-parole period, justice says The applicant’s murderous intent dated back to the invitations to lunch, it persisted through the lunch that the poison was administered … We have concluded that the case involved such calculated criminality that it is inappropriate to fix a non-parole period.
summary: Erin Patterson, a Victorian woman, lost her appeal in the Australian mushroom triple‑murder case and was given a longer sentence. The court said her calculated criminal intent made it inappropriate to fix a non‑parole period.
author: Guardian World

title: Leaked audio shows train cleared to move despite stalled train in Spain crash
content: Leaked audio recordings between a control centre and train drivers indicate that, during the Spain train crash, one train received clearance to proceed while another train was stalled on the same track. The recordings suggest the clearance was given despite the presence of the stalled train.
summary: Recordings between a control centre and the train drivers were leaked. The audio appears to show one train was given clearance to move while another train had stalled on the track.
author: BBC World

title: Netflix's "The Mosquito Bowl" mixes football and WWII in a by‑the‑numbers drama
content: Peter Berg’s handsomely made second world war drama about a football game before the battle of Okinawa is stirring but filled with eye-rolling dialogue Forgive me, but it is difficult not to be a little cynical about The Mosquito Bowl, Peter Berg’s grimly serious action feature situated (and marketed during many an NFL game) at the intersection of two predominant male interests: football and the second world war. Though both are certainly rich topics for cinema, and though I have been a fan of many a football/war story – most especially Berg’s NBC series Friday Night Lights – it is, let’s say, a tricky time for movies filled with dubiously nostalgic patriotism and masculinity. The trailer practically drips with a borderline parodic virility: a cadre of handsome up-and-coming male actors streaked with dirt; a group of men “trained for glory” and “called to war”, triumphantly hoisting aloft footballs, beer and guns to ponderous music. But Berg is a capable and battle-tested director who knows his way around both a clock-ticking thriller ( Deepwater Horizon, Lone Survivor ) and the football field. So while The Mosquito Bowl, adapted for Netflix by Berg and Mark L Smith from a nonfiction book by Buzz Bissinger, fulfills its promise of American male pablum – there is many a clunky monologue about honor and duty and the “white buzz” of adrenaline – it also delivers on competently made, absorbing action sequences. (In huge news for Friday Night Lights fans, the football scenes here are once again scored by Explosions in the Sky.) Both in sport and in war, Berg has a knack for grace within visual cacophony and chaos; graphic sequences in battle and from the 1944 Christmas Eve pickup game at Guadalcanal that gives the film its name suggest, far more than its anvil-heavy dialogue, the connections between the gridiron and the battlefield, how the fleetness and camaraderie of sport can be wielded for survival and killing. There is a stomach-churning catharsis in experiencing, as in Sam Mendes’s 1917 or Alex Garland’s Warfare, the real-time brutality and capriciousness of war.
summary: Netflix's "The Mosquito Bowl" mixes football and WWII in a by‑the‑numbers drama.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Borussia Dortmund's Yellow Wall goes phone-free during Frankfurt win
content:
Borussia Dortmund’s Signal Iduna Park hosted a sold-out crowd of 81,365 fans for a match against Eintracht Frankfurt last Saturday. The atmosphere on the Yellow Wall, Europe’s largest standing terrace, featured traditional supporter rituals, including the stadium announcer calling out the first names of the starting lineup while tens of thousands of fans responded with their last names. Dozens of black and yellow flags waved over the terrace as the crowd focused on the field.

The home team secured a victory with a lone goal from Max Beier, prompting a roar from the packed stadium. This result placed Borussia Dortmund level on points with Bayern Munich at the top of the Bundesliga standings. While the event appeared routine on the surface, the article frames this scene within a broader discussion about clubs attempting to exclude influencers from games and the resulting dilemma regarding how teams interact with their fan base.
summary: Borussia Dortmund's supporters at the phone-free Yellow Wall celebrated Max Beier's goal in a victory over Eintracht Frankfurt. The match ended with Dortmund even on points with Bayern Munich atop the Bundesliga standings.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Uefa close to selecting candidate to challenge Infantino in Fifa election
content:
UEFA and its allies are reportedly close to selecting a candidate to challenge Gianni Infantino in the upcoming FIFA election, with a decision potentially made as early as next week. While Arsène Wenger is not believed to have entered the race, discussions with potential nominees have gained momentum. This progress occurs despite recent setbacks, including a surprising endorsement of Infantino’s bid for a fourth term by Sheikh Salman bin Ibrahim al-Khalifa, the president of the Asian Football Confederation.

The timeline for opposing Infantino in March is tight, as candidates must confirm their candidacy by 18 November. However, there is growing confidence that the efforts to field a challenger are nearing a successful resolution.
summary: Uefa and its allies are nearing the selection of a candidate to run against Gianni Infantino in the upcoming Fifa election, potentially by next week. This progress occurs despite a setback where Asian Football Confederation president Sheikh Salman bin Ibrahim al-Khalifa endorsed Infantino.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Dream beat Valkyries 80-69 to force first WNBA finals Game 7
content:
The Atlanta Dream defeated the Golden State Valkyries 80-69 on Thursday afternoon to level the WNBA finals series at 3-3. Facing elimination at a lunchtime tipoff, the Dream overwhelmed their opponents to force a decisive seventh game, rediscovering their offensive touch as their championship hopes threatened to slip away.

This victory sets the stage for the first Game 7 in WNBA history, scheduled for Saturday night. The result concludes a best-of-seven series that has reached its ultimate conclusion, with both teams now tied after six contests.
summary: The Atlanta Dream defeated the Golden State Valkyries 80-69 on Thursday to level the best-of-seven series at 3-3. This victory forces the first Game 7 in WNBA history, which is set for Saturday night.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Scottish Premiership invites bids to televise all games from 2029
content:
The Scottish Premiership has initiated the first UK move to eliminate the Saturday 3pm broadcast blackout by inviting bids to televise all its matches from 2029. A tender document issued last week by the Scottish Professional Football League (SPFL) offers broadcasters the option to acquire live rights for every game, including those starting at 3pm on Saturdays. These matches are currently prohibited from domestic broadcast under Article 48 of Uefa’s statutes.

This action is expected to be part of a coordinated effort among UK domestic leagues to end the long-standing restriction. The SPFL’s tender marks the initial step in this process, allowing potential rights holders to consider comprehensive packages that include the previously protected afternoon slot.
summary: The Scottish Professional Football League has issued a tender allowing broadcasters to bid for live rights to all matches from 2029. This move permits the potential broadcast of Saturday 3pm games, which are currently prohibited under UEFA statutes.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Australia gain edge in Test decider after late Bavuma blow hurts South Africa
content:
South Africa found themselves in a perilous position at the close of the third day of the decisive third Test against Australia at Newlands, trailing by 40 runs with six wickets remaining. The Proteas were bowled out for 140 in their second innings, a collapse that included the dismissal of Temba Bavuma for 35 and Lizaad Williams’ partner Ackerman for 62.

Matthew Breetzke will resume batting on the fourth morning on 19, joined by Ryan Rickelton on eight. South Africa now faces the challenge of posting a total that can trouble Australia, who will bat last in the match.
summary: South Africa reached the close of the third day in a perilous position at 140 for four in their second innings at Newlands. The Proteas trail Australia by 40 runs with six wickets remaining as Matthew Breetzke and Ryan Rickelton resume on the fourth morning.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Duckett's 167 and Dawson's four wickets lead England to victory over Sri Lanka
content:
Ben Duckett’s century and Liam Dawson’s four-wicket haul secured a 55-run victory for England over Sri Lanka in Lahore. The match served as a farewell fixture in the tri-series, with Sri Lanka having already qualified for the final against Pakistan.

England posted a total of 386, anchored by Duckett’s 167-run innings. Sri Lanka initially threatened to challenge the target, with Pavan Rathnayake scoring another century. However, despite requiring 87 runs from the final 10 overs, the chasing side was denied a repeat of their earlier success in Rawalpindi, falling short of the 387-run target.
summary: Ben Duckett scored 167 and Liam Dawson took four wickets as England beat Sri Lanka by 55 runs in Lahore. Pavan Rathnayake scored a century for Sri Lanka, who had already qualified for the tri-series final.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Sergio Garcia quits LIV Golf to rejoin DP World Tour and target Ryder Cup
content: Sergio Garcia has confirmed his departure from LIV Golf, becoming the latest prominent player to leave the series. He stated that he will rejoin the DP World Tour and is targeting a return to the Ryder Cup.
summary: Sergio Garcia has confirmed his exit from LIV Golf and stated he will rejoin the DP World Tour. He also indicated that he is targeting a return to the Ryder Cup.
author: BBC Sport

title: Antonelli to miss Mexico City Grand Prix media day with illness
content: Kimi Antonelli will miss the Mexico City Grand Prix media day scheduled for Thursday due to an illness. The driver is currently positioned to secure his first world title.
summary: Kimi Antonelli will miss Thursday's Mexico City Grand Prix media day due to an illness. He is currently standing on the brink of clinching his first world title.
author: BBC Sport

title: Scottish football seeks offers to end 3pm TV blackout
content: Scottish football has initiated the process to solicit offers for the upcoming broadcast cycle, marking the first tentative steps toward ending the 3pm television blackout in the UK.
summary: Scottish football has taken the first tentative steps to end the 3pm television blackout in the UK. The league is currently seeking offers for the next broadcast cycle.
author: BBC Sport

title: WA Secretary of State Hobbs rejects DOJ request to set aside noncitizen ballots
content: Washington Secretary of State Steve Hobbs shot back at the Department of Justice (DOJ) for asking him to order his election officials to set aside ballots for hundreds of people the federal government identified as alleged non-U. S. Citizens. In a Wednesday response to the DOJ’s request, Hobbs said, “Without individualized proof of ineligibility, it would…
summary: Washington Secretary of State Steve Hobbs shot back at the Department of Justice (DOJ) for asking him to order his election officials to set aside ballots for hundreds of people the federal government identified as alleged non-U. S.
author: The Hill

title: Live updates: Trump, Vance zip across South to shore up GOP votes
content: With less than a week until Election Day, President Trump held a lunchtime rally Thursday in Rock Hill, S.C., near the North Carolina border. The event aimed to boost voter enthusiasm for Sen. Darline Graham (R-S.C.), who is facing a tougher-than-expected Senate race against a Democratic opponent.
summary: With less than a week out until Election Day, candidates are attempting to leave their final mark on voters. President Trump held a lunchtime rally Thursday in Rock Hill, S.
author: The Hill

title: Mortgage rates fall below 7.25 percent
content: Mortgage rates have dropped to below 7.25 percent, marking a second consecutive weekly decline, according to The Hill’s Business & Economy newsletter. The reduction offers prospective homebuyers some relief amid a costly housing market. © Nam Y. Huh, Associated.
summary: Mortgage rates declined for the second straight week, dropping to under 7.25 percent. The decline offers prospective homebuyers some relief in a pricey housing market.
author: The Hill

title: Finnish police launch criminal probe over forest cleared for Google data center
content: Finnish police initiated a criminal investigation on Thursday regarding Google’s construction activities for a planned data center in northern Finland. The probe was launched because the company cleared hundreds of acres of forest without finishing mandatory environmental reviews. This legal action intensifies scrutiny on Google’s $1.5 billion investment in artificial intelligence infrastructure within the country.
summary: Finnish police launch criminal probe over forest cleared for Google data center.
author: The Hill

title: Eight of nine England water companies fail environmental standards, report finds
content: Angela Eagle tells industry ‘people are sick of excuses’ as pollution levels remain high despite billions in investment Angela Eagle, the environment secretary, has summoned water industry bosses to Whitehall after a report found that the environmental performance of the big companies has worsened despite investment. “People are sick of excuses,” Dame Angela said, after the Environment Agency joined the Drinking Water Inspectorate, Natural Resources Wales and Ofwat for a joint report that rated eight of the nine water companies in England as “poor” or “requiring improvement”.
summary: A joint report rated eight of the nine water companies in England as “poor” or “requiring improvement” despite billions in investment. Environment Secretary Angela Eagle summoned industry bosses to Whitehall after the report found that pollution levels remain high and environmental performance has worsened.
author: Guardian Environment

title: Oxford study finds jet lag disrupts Manx shearwater navigation
content:
A study from Oxford University indicates that Manx shearwaters can be displaced hundreds of miles from their intended path due to a form of jet lag. This disorientation occurs when the birds' internal body clocks become out of sync with local time, affecting their navigation capabilities.

Researchers analyzed tracking data from these seabirds on the west coast of the UK. The findings showed that after foraging trips over the Atlantic, the birds’ rapid eastward return flights to their colonies disrupted their sense of time and direction.
summary: Researchers from Oxford found that Manx shearwaters can be thrown hundreds of miles off course when their body clocks get out of sync with local time. Tracking data showed that the birds' rapid eastward flights after Atlantic foraging trips disrupted their sense of time and navigation.
author: Guardian Environment

title: Blood test tracks small cell lung cancer burden and molecular traits
content: Northwestern Medicine scientists and collaborators have developed a novel liquid biopsy technique to track small cell lung cancer (SCLC). The method, detailed in a study published in the Journal of Clinical Investigation, can measure cancer burden and identify the molecular characteristics of the disease.
summary: Northwestern Medicine scientists and collaborators demonstrated a novel liquid biopsy technique to measure cancer burden and reveal molecular characteristics of small cell lung cancer. The findings were published in the Journal of Clinical Investigation.
author: Medical Xpress

title: COMPASS pathway helps T cells prevent autoimmune responses to gut bacteria
content: Scientists at St. Jude Children's Research Hospital have identified a gene-regulatory pathway that helps maintain immune balance in the human gut. In a study published in Science Advances, the researchers demonstrated that regulatory T cells utilize a general gene expression pathway known as COMPASS. This mechanism allows these immune cells to suppress inappropriate responses, thereby preventing lethal inflammation and autoimmunity triggered by the trillions of bacteria residing in the gut.
summary: St. Jude Children's Research Hospital scientists discovered that regulatory T cells use the COMPASS gene-regulatory pathway to suppress inappropriate immune reactions. This mechanism prevents lethal inflammation and autoimmunity while maintaining balance with gut bacteria.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Type 2 diabetes increases vulnerability to air pollution's cellular effects
content: Air pollution impacts health beyond the respiratory system, with fine particulate matter (PM2.5) capable of triggering systemic inflammation. Individuals with type 2 diabetes may face heightened vulnerability to these effects. The condition can already compromise stem cell function within the bone marrow, a critical organ responsible for producing blood cells and maintaining bone health.
summary: Fine particulate matter can trigger systemic inflammation that extends beyond the lungs. People with type 2 diabetes are particularly vulnerable because the disease impairs stem cell function in the bone marrow.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Study Links Heat Waves to Increased Stroke Risk in Older Adults
content: A study conducted in Brazil by researchers at the University of São Paulo (USP) found that each additional day spent under a heat wave in São Paulo is associated with an increased risk of acute stroke in people ages 65 and older. The research defined a heat wave as at least two consecutive days with maximum temperatures of 33.1 °C (92 degrees Fahrenheit) or higher.
summary: Researchers at the University of São Paulo found that each additional day under a heat wave increases the risk of acute stroke in people ages 65 and older. The study defined a heat wave as at least two consecutive days with maximum temperatures of 33.1 °C or higher.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Ciprofloxacin and cefotaxime boost resistant bacteria in hospital sewage, study finds
content: A new study from the University of Gothenburg in Sweden reports that antibiotics excreted by patients promote antibiotic-resistant bacteria in hospital sewers. The researchers note that this phenomenon may contribute to the development and spread of hard-to-treat infections. Identifying the specific antibiotics responsible is expected to pave the way for targeted measures.
summary: A study by University of Gothenburg researchers found that antibiotics excreted by patients promote antibiotic‑resistant bacteria in hospital sewers. Identifying ciprofloxacin and cefotaxime as key contributors could enable targeted measures to curb the spread of hard‑to‑treat infections.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Residential PM2.5 Linked to Minimal Residual Disease in Pediatric B-ALL
content: A study published in JNCI Cancer Spectrum reports an association between residential fine particulate matter (PM₂.₅) concentrations and positive end-of-induction (EOI) minimal residual disease (MRD). This finding specifically concerns pediatric patients with high-risk B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (B-ALL) who were undergoing induction therapy.
summary: A study published in JNCI Cancer Spectrum found that residential fine particulate matter concentrations during induction therapy are associated with positive end-of-induction minimal residual disease. This association was observed in pediatric patients with high-risk B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Picobirnavirus Found to Infect Gut Bacteria, Not Human Cells
content: Researchers at Washington University School of Medicine in St. Louis and collaborators have determined that picobirnavirus, a common virus found in the human digestive tract, infects gut bacteria rather than human cells. This finding corrects previous scientific assumptions that the virus directly infected human tissue and contributed to gastrointestinal illness. The discovery redefines the role of this widespread pathogen within the gut microbiome.
summary: Researchers at Washington University School of Medicine in St. Louis discovered that the common gut virus picobirnavirus infects gut bacteria. The virus was previously thought to directly infect human tissue and cause gastrointestinal illness.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Study finds perforin can kill tumor cells without granzymes
content: Scientists have long recognized that perforin, a protein produced by T cells and natural killer (NK) cells, kills tumor cells by creating holes in the cell membrane and delivering proteases known as granzymes. New research from the University of Michigan Health Rogel Cancer Center shows that tumor cells can still be destroyed even when key granzymes are absent. This finding indicates that perforin alone can act as an effective cancer‑killing agent.
summary: Perforin, a protein made by T cells and natural killer cells, kills tumor cells by punching holes and delivering granzymes. Researchers at the University of Michigan Health Rogel Cancer Center reported that tumor cells were killed even when major granzymes were missing.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Altermagnets generate spin current to transport magnetic information
content: Researchers have experimentally demonstrated, for the first time, that altermagnets can produce a spin current capable of transporting magnetic information. This breakthrough is supported by a theoretical model of electron transport developed by the CFM group. Altermagnets represent a new class of materials that can generate such currents despite lacking the net magnetization found in conventional magnets.
summary: Researchers have experimentally demonstrated for the first time that altermagnets can produce a spin current capable of carrying magnetic information. This finding is supported by a theoretical model of electron transport developed by the CFM group.
author: Phys.org

title: Zombie bacteria keep building DNA after death
content: Researchers at Aarhus University have discovered that bacteria can continue producing DNA after death. The team also identified a method to control the specific DNA produced. This discovery may eventually contribute to the development of new biological materials.
summary: Researchers at Aarhus University have discovered that bacteria can continue producing DNA after they die. And they have found a way to control what gets produced.
author: Phys.org

title: Light-emitting nanoparticles help ultrasound direct gene editing to selected mouse brain regions
content:
Researchers at the Wu Tsai Neurosciences Institute have developed a technique to edit genes in precise locations deep within the brain and body without invasive surgery or implants. The method combines ultrasound, light-emitting nanoparticles, and photo-controllable gene-editing proteins to target specific areas.

The team successfully demonstrated this approach by altering genes in selected regions of mouse brains. This advancement allows for non-invasive gene editing in deep tissue locations.
summary: Light-emitting nanoparticles help ultrasound direct gene editing to selected mouse brain regions.
author: Phys.org

title: Snøfrid the Sámi: Matriarch of Norway's royal bloodline?
content: For a long time, some researchers believed that the South Sámi population arrived in Central Norway in the 18th century at the earliest, and that Norwegian farmers were present long before the Sámi. This is known as the "hypothesis of late immigration."
summary: Snøfrid the Sámi: Matriarch of Norway's royal bloodline?
author: Phys.org

title: Microplastic Shape Influences Viral Disease Severity in Rainbow Trout
content: New research from William & Mary's Virginia Institute of Marine Science indicates that microplastic shape influences the severity of viral infections in rainbow trout. The findings suggest certain plastic forms pose greater biological risks than others, potentially guiding efforts to reduce microplastics' environmental impacts.
summary: Research from William & Mary's Virginia Institute of Marine Science shows that the shape of microplastics can affect the severity of viral infection in rainbow trout. The study indicates that some forms of plastic pollution pose greater biological risks than others, offering a potential path toward reducing the environmental impacts of microplastics.
author: Phys.org

title: Simantic builds Rust-based firmware simulation for AI agents
content:
Ahnaf and Seungmin, founders of Simantic, a Y Combinator F26 company, have launched a firmware simulation platform designed to allow engineers and AI agents to test and validate firmware without physical hardware. The founders, formerly firmware engineers at companies including Neuralink and Tesla, previously worked on early prototypes for the Cybertruck and Roadster. They developed Simantic to address the inefficiency of traditional firmware testing, where AI agents could write code rapidly but validation required flashing physical boards and using manual, expensive tools with outdated software.

The platform offers virtual development boards that can be programmed and executed via a single API call, enabling terminal-based operations. It includes an AI code reviewer for firmware that utilizes the simulation as a verification engine to make evidence-based decisions. Additionally, Simantic provides a CI/CD pipeline for hardware projects that validates firmware against simulated microcontrollers on every commit. The founders noted that their own testing time reduced from hours of manual work to seconds using their simulation.

Simantic’s users are applying the technology to bare-metal and RTOS development for flight controllers, electric vehicles, robotics, and satellites. The company highlights the importance of robust simulation for safety-critical systems in avionics and automotive sectors, where firmware changes impact human safety and high-value machinery. In one recent instance, Simantic assisted an early-stage space startup in testing satellite firmware before the hardware was available. This approach allowed the startup to avoid the cost and time associated with development modules that exceed $100,000, achieving validation at a fraction of the expense.

The company initially considered building its software around open-source emulation frameworks such as Renode and QEMU but abandoned this approach due to several limitations. The founders cited bottlenecks in the development speed of Renode, noting that merging their contributions was too slow for a startup. They also identified performance issues stemming from Renode’s use of Dotnet, as well as bloat from unnecessary features that required workarounds. Furthermore, users reported that the simulation accuracy of these open-source emulators was insufficient for systems requiring precise timing validation.

To resolve these issues, Simantic developed a custom simulation engine written entirely in Rust, prioritizing accuracy over the expandability and breadth of models found in open-source tools. The company maintains hardware validation rigs that operate 24/7 to ensure simulation models closely match real-world hardware. These rigs consist of development boards connected to a Saleae Logic MSO and a SWD bus, controlled by a Linux PC running Claude to identify and fix discrepancies. The cloud-hosted simulator is currently available, and a native binary is included with developer plan licenses for local, unlimited use.

Current support includes specific models of STM32F0, F4, and H7 series MCUs, ESP32-S3/C3, and RP2040, with new models being released weekly. The company provides a demo of the simulation in an AI code review session and offers an AI firmware reviewer bot for integration into GitHub repositories.
summary: Simantic builds Rust-based firmware simulation for AI agents.
author: Hacker News

title: Overtone uses multiple AI models to transcribe and format captions for any screen shape
content:
Ruud, co-founder of Lont, has introduced Overtone, an open-source tool designed to transcribe, correct, and format video captions. Lont uses Overtone to convert company emails into personalized videos, a process that previously required significant manual effort to fix misheard words and layout issues. The software employs multiple speech-to-text models, including gpt-transcribe, Azure STT, and Elevenlabs Scribe, to analyze audio. When these models produce conflicting results, Overtone re-sends small clips to the models and uses a large language model (LLM) to determine the accurate transcription. This LLM acts as a sanity check, utilizing context prompts and world knowledge to resolve ambiguities, which results in a lower Word Error Rate compared to using a single model alone.

While the use of up to three STT models and an LLM increases processing costs, Overtone reduces the time required for manual caption correction. The tool includes a rules-based cutter that formats transcripts into visually appropriate captions based on screen dimensions, such as 16:9 or 9:16. This formatting ensures that pauses create breaks, captions are grouped by speaker, and names or numbers are not split across multiple caption segments. For integration, a video.js plugin allows users to toggle between styled, plain, or no captions without burning them into the video file. Alternatively, the command-line tool `overtone burn` can embed captions directly into MP4 files.

Overtone’s initial version has been released under the MIT license, with the goal of making high-quality captioning accessible to a broader audience. The developers have structured the codebase to facilitate community contributions for adding new style packs, languages, and model providers. Users can test the caption cutter via the command `npx overtone-captions recut yoursub. srt` or use the API with a dry-run option to estimate costs. A demo is available at overtone. lont. ai, and the source code and benchmarks are hosted on GitHub at github. com/lonthq/overtone-captions.
summary: Overtone leverages multiple speech-to-text models and an LLM to reduce transcription errors and automatically format captions for various screen sizes. The tool was open-sourced under the MIT license by Lont to allow users to transcribe audio and cut captions without manually burning them into video files.
author: Hacker News

title: Swift app auto-dismisses macOS local network permission popups
content: This popup has been a constant gripe of mine for years. I almost NEVER want to allow this permission and there is no system setting to disable it globally and prevent the popup from interrupting your typing, etc. This tiny swift app I built will autoclose it in 1/4th of a second and leave behind a little notification that it did so. Would love to hear feedback! Comments URL: https://news. Ycombinator. Com/item? Id=50294506 Points: 28 # Comments: 20
summary: A developer created a small Swift application that automatically closes the macOS prompt asking to allow apps to find devices on local networks. The tool operates within a quarter of a second and leaves a notification confirming the dismissal.
author: Hacker News

title: Astronomers Identify 2026 ED138 as Potential New Dwarf Planet Beyond Pluto
content: Astronomers have identified a potential new dwarf planet, 2026 ED138, located beyond Pluto. The object may be as large as 1,500 kilometers in diameter. Scientists are working to confirm whether it satisfies the criteria for a dwarf planet.
summary: The object 2026 ED138 lies beyond Pluto and could be up to 1,500 kilometers in diameter. Astronomers are still working to confirm whether it meets the criteria for a dwarf planet.
author: Wired

title: Law Firm Linked to Elon Musk Starts Election Integrity Group
content: A law firm that helped establish Elon Musk’s America PAC has launched a new “Election Integrity” organization. The group plans to collaborate with election officials to pursue policies that align with Donald Trump’s claims of election fraud, which have been widely labeled false.
summary: The firm that helped set up Elon Musk’s America PAC has launched a new organization focused on election integrity. The group will collaborate with election officials to promote policies that align with Donald Trump’s false election fraud claims.
author: Wired

title: I Gave My Blood to the AI Death Clock
content: The Death Clock app claims to predict when users will die and to help extend their lifespan. After using the service for a month, the author reports feeling as though it was draining their life.
summary: Death Clock promises to predict when you’re going to die and help you extend your time on Earth. After a month, I felt like it was sucking the life out of me.
author: Wired

title: Ridge Wallet 20% Off Sale, 99-Day Risk-Free Trial Available
content: The Ridge Wallet is currently discounted by 20 percent, a promotion that also includes other Ridge gear. The product is described as living up to its hype. Customers can try the wallet risk‑free for 99 days.
summary: The Ridge Wallet is on sale for 20 percent off. Customers can try the wallet risk‑free for 99 days.
author: Wired

title: Accenture employee's personal Claude AI accessed Pentagon DOD network for two months
content: Sources reported to WIRED that an Accenture employee’s personal Claude AI agent operated on a Department of Defense network for two months before it was discovered. The incident revealed a vulnerability that could be patched after identification.
summary: An Accenture employee’s personal Claude agent ran on a Department of Defense network for two months. The presence was identified and the vulnerability could be patched.
author: Wired

title: Utah charges Kalshi and its CEO with illegally promoting online gambling
content:
Utah has filed criminal charges against the prediction‑market firm Kalshi and its top executives, alleging the company has violated state anti‑gambling laws. The state’s complaint lists 14 charges, including 12 counts of illegally promoting online gambling, and names Kalshi, CEO Tarek Mansour and COO Luana Lopes Lara as defendants.  

This filing follows a prior lawsuit in which Utah accused Kalshi of operating illegally within the state. The action is part of a growing national effort, with other states such as New York, Nevada, New Mexico, Washington and Connecticut also pursuing legal challenges against prediction‑market platforms like Kalshi and Polymarket.
summary: Kalshi CEO Tarek Mansour. | Michael Nagle/Bloomberg via Getty Images Utah has filed criminal charges against Kalshi and its executives, accusing the prediction market of breaking anti-gambling laws, as reported by The Salt Lake Tribune and the Associated Press.
author: The Verge

title: Google Gemini Adds Direct Editing for PDFs, Docs, Sheets and More
content:
Google has announced that users can now generate, preview, and edit PDFs, Google Docs, Google Sheets, slide decks, Markdown files, TXT files, and code directly within Gemini. These new file editing capabilities are available to all Gemini users starting today. While PDF previews and editing are supported on both web and mobile platforms, all other file formats are currently available only in the web version.

This update builds on earlier support for generating and downloading files, allowing users to modify documents without leaving the Gemini app. Google stated that users can expand documents to edit them in full-screen mode and highlight text within files to ask questions or provide prompts.
summary: Google Gemini now lets users generate, preview, and edit PDFs, Google Docs, Google Sheets, slide decks, Markdown, TXT, and code directly within the app. The new file editing features are available to all Gemini users today, with PDF editing working on both web and mobile, while other formats are limited to the web version.
author: The Verge

title: GM to pay $220 million to settle data sales claims
content:
General Motors has agreed to pay $220 million to resolve claims that it illegally sold driver and location information to data brokers. This settlement addresses a complaint filed by a coalition of 36 US attorneys general. Under the agreement, GM is required to limit the driving data it collects and must obtain "express consent" from drivers before gathering their information.

The allegations center on GM’s now-discontinued Smart Driver program, which collected data regarding driving habits such as acceleration, braking, and trip length. The company allegedly shared this information with data brokers, which enabled insurance companies to purchase the data.
summary: General Motors agreed to pay $220 million to settle claims that it illegally sold driver and location data to data brokers. The settlement, prompted by a complaint from 36 US attorneys general, requires GM to limit data collection and obtain express consent from drivers.
author: The Verge

title: Rivian R2 becomes best-selling vehicle as Q3 revenue rises 38%
content:
Rivian’s R2 has become the company’s best-selling vehicle, outselling all other electric models for the first time. This milestone was highlighted as Rivian reported its third-quarter 2026 earnings, a period marked by ramping up production of the R2. The company noted that the R2 is now leading sales across its entire electric vehicle lineup.

Financially, Rivian generated $2.155 billion in total revenue, a 38 percent increase from $1.558 billion in the same quarter of 2025. Automotive revenue accounted for $1.55 billion, rising 36 percent year over year, while software and subscription services contributed $605 million, reflecting a 45 percent annual growth.
summary: Rivian reported $2.155 billion in third-quarter revenue, a 38 percent increase from the same period in 2025. The R2 electric vehicle is now outselling all other Rivian models for the first time.
author: The Verge

title: Google says AI search earns less than organic, plans more ads to boost revenue
content:
Alphabet reported its third-quarter financial results on Wednesday, revealing nearly $128 billion in revenue and over $26 billion in net income for the July-to-September period. Despite a 25 percent year-over-year revenue increase, the company’s stock price fell by almost 12 percent, marking one of its largest post-earnings drops in history. The market reaction was driven by earnings per share of $2.12, which fell short of the consensus projection of $3.02, and a net income figure that was approximately $9 billion lower than the previous year.

A key factor in the stock’s decline was Google’s admission that its AI search feature generates less revenue than traditional organic search. This revelation is particularly notable given that the company expects to increase its spending on AI in the coming year. Although Google’s Cloud division exceeded expectations with revenue surpassing $30 billion—roughly $1 billion more than analyst estimates—the overall financial performance failed to satisfy investors. The combination of lower-than-expected profitability and rising AI costs contributed to the significant drop in the company’s share price.
summary: Alphabet posted Q3 2026 revenue of almost $128 billion and net income of $26 billion, but said AI search earns less than organic search. The company’s shares fell about 12 % after the report, and it plans to spend more on AI and add ads to raise revenue.
author: Ars Technica

title: Small company offers concentrated solar system with integrated fossil fuel backup
content:
Concentrated solar energy, which uses mirrors to convert sunlight into heat for driving turbines, initially appeared to have a promising future due to advancements in heat storage that allowed for around-the-clock power generation. However, the technology failed to maintain its competitive edge as the cost of photovoltaic panels dropped significantly, making solar panels the cheapest power source in most locations. Consequently, current solar power generation requires a mix of other facilities, typically batteries and natural gas plants, to manage overnight demands and weather-related shortfalls.

A small company is now offering a solution that aims to eliminate the need for constructing separate backup facilities. Its concentrated solar design integrates a fossil-fueled backup system that shares most of its generating hardware with the solar component. This approach allows the system to function as its own backup, potentially reducing the infrastructure required to ensure continuous power supply.
summary: A small company is promising to reduce the need for separate battery or natural gas facilities by creating a concentrated solar system. Its design allows a fossil-fueled backup system to share most of the generating hardware with the solar side.
author: Ars Technica

title: Trump Declares Foreign-Made Robot Imports a National Security Threat
content:
President Donald Trump issued a presidential proclamation on October 28 declaring that imports of foreign‑made factory robots pose a national security threat. The proclamation orders new negotiations with U.S. trading partners and leaves open the possibility of future tariffs on such robot imports.

The measure heightens scrutiny of foreign‑made industrial robots that could complicate the manufacturing operations of major U.S. companies that rely on them. Trump singled out Detroit automakers General Motors and Ford, electric‑vehicle maker Tesla, and aerospace and defense giants Boeing and Lockheed Martin as examples of firms that could be affected.

In the proclamation, Trump described industrial robots and machinery as essential for producing U.S. military weapon systems and as a “driving force” behind all critical infrastructure sectors of the U.S. economy.

The proclamation cites an investigation conducted under U.S. Secretary of Commerce Howard Lutnick, which found that U.S. imports of such robots “pose[] risks to the United States industrial base and threatens the long‑term competitiveness of the United States in a sector that is increasingly vital to national security.”
summary: Trump Declares Foreign-Made Robot Imports a National Security Threat.
author: Ars Technica

title: Pentagon IG declines to investigate Starlink/Starshield slowdown in Ukraine
content:
The Pentagon inspector‑general’s office has declined a request from U.S. senators to investigate recent restrictions on Ukraine’s use of SpaceX’s satellite services. The inquiry, directed at the Department of Defense inspector general Platte Moring, came after Ukraine reported that its military drones lost satellite connectivity when flying faster than 161 km per hour (100 mph). The Ukrainian military said the speed limit was lifted after roughly ten days.

Five Democratic and four Republican senators sent an October 15 letter to Moring asking for a probe into the reported disruptions of both Starlink and its military‑grade counterpart, Starshield. The letter sought answers on whether any restrictions were directed, authorized, or implemented by SpaceX, the Department of Defense, or other U.S. government entities; whether such restrictions complied with applicable U.S. government contracts; and what actions, if any, the Department of Defense took in response.

The inspector‑general’s office has refused to open an investigation into the matter.
summary: Pentagon IG declines to investigate Starlink/Starshield slowdown in Ukraine.
author: Ars Technica

title: Windows 11 preview update fixes right‑click menu, amid declining PC license sales
content:
Microsoft has begun rolling out a Windows 11 preview update, KB5127936, that addresses a long‑standing complaint from power users about the operating system’s right‑click menu. The update, which is cumulative for Windows 11 versions 26H2 and 25H2, will be delivered gradually before moving to a normal rollout for all devices once it reaches general availability.

The new preview introduces a “customize menu” button that lets users control which commands appear when they right‑click. Built‑in items such as Send To or Create Shortcut can be toggled on or off, the order of main‑menu items can be rearranged, and third‑party extensions can be assigned to either the main menu or the “Show more options” submenu. The change is intended to restore the muscle memory that many users had lost when familiar commands were hidden behind icons or moved to a submenu.

Alongside the menu overhaul, the preview highlights a new feature called Cloud Rebuild. This recovery option can reinstall Windows 11 directly from the cloud when the current installation fails to boot. The process pulls the Windows 11 image and required system drivers from Windows Update, eliminating the need for a custom recovery image or external media. Cloud Rebuild behaves more like a fresh installation than a repair, as existing applications and files are not retained; users can also choose to sanitize entire system drives before reinstalling.

The announcement comes at the same time Microsoft released its quarterly financial report, which noted a continued decline in the business of selling Windows licenses for new PCs. For a complete list of improvements included in the preview—such as changes to Xbox mode and settings—see the official Microsoft release announcement.
summary: The preview update KB5127936 for Windows 11 26H2 and 25H2 adds a customizable right‑click menu that lets users toggle, rearrange, and control built‑in and third‑party commands. It also introduces Cloud Rebuild, a recovery option that reinstalls Windows 11 from the cloud without external media but does not preserve existing applications or files.
author: Ars Technica

title: Granola Adds Dictation to Meeting Notetaker to Compete with Wispr
content: Wispr recently expanded its dictation app to include meeting notes. In response, Granola is adding dictation functionality to its meeting‑notetaking tool. The move signals a growing competition in the voice‑AI space.
summary: After Wispr added meeting notes to its dictation app, Granola is adding dictation to its meeting notetaker. The voice AI wars are getting interesting.
author: TechCrunch

title: Meta launches AI fashion app Style Sketch
content: Meta has quietly launched an AI‑driven fashion app called Style Sketch. The app links to Instagram to automatically create a virtual closet from photos users have already posted. It also allows users to add items manually by snapping a photo, recording a short video, or uploading images from their camera roll.
summary: Meta has launched an AI fashion app called Style Sketch. The app connects to Instagram to build a virtual closet from shared photos and lets users add items by snapping a photo, recording a video, or uploading images from their camera roll.
author: TechCrunch

title: AI Agents Replace Human Roles at Startup Anything
content: Using AI for roles from executive assistants to chiefs of staff, companies are boasting about doing more with less, creating tension with their human workers On an average workday, Dhruv Amin chats with dozens of colleagues to get things done at his AI startup Anything. He might ask Gwen, his executive assistant, to schedule a meeting, then troubleshoot a technical problem with Cody, his coding partner. Then he might check in with Betsy for search engine optimization, or Juno for onboarding customers. If the office runs out of snacks, he sends a Slack message to Justin, the office manager charged with stocking the kitchen. But none of these co-workers are people. They’re artificial intelligence agents, software that handles tasks without human intervention. Anything is one of several startups building them, and betting on a future where workplaces will increasingly turn over their sales, marketing, coding and other tasks to semi-autonomous AI. At Anything, there are 15 human employees and roughly 150 agents – a ratio that Amin believes will soon be the norm.
summary: Dhruv Amin, founder of AI startup Anything, uses AI agents named Gwen, Cody, Betsy, Juno, and Justin to handle tasks such as scheduling, coding, SEO, onboarding, and snack stocking. The company has 15 human employees and about 150 AI agents, a ratio Amin believes will become common.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Vatican Displays Eight Historic Popemobiles Tracing Century-Long Papal Transport
content: Eight historic popemobiles are now on display at the Vatican Museums, showcasing the evolution of papal transport over nearly a century. The exhibition features a range of vehicles, from silk‑lined limousines to models equipped with bulletproof glass, illustrating how papal transport has changed through the ages.
summary: Eight historic popemobiles, ranging from silk-lined limousines to vehicles fitted with bulletproof glass, are on display at the Vatican Museums. The exhibition traces how papal transport has evolved over nearly a century.
author: Euronews

title: Kazakhstan President Tokayev urges faster construction of nuclear power plants
content: President Tokayev delivered his annual address, outlining Kazakhstan’s priorities for the coming year. He urged the government to accelerate energy and construction projects, specifically calling for faster construction of nuclear power plants. Tokayev also criticized inefficiencies in public policy, urging reforms to improve overall project execution.
summary: President Tokayev said the country should speed up construction of nuclear power plants. In his annual address he outlined priorities for the coming year, urging faster energy and construction projects and criticizing inefficiencies in public policy.
author: Euronews

title: Spain high‑speed train crash expert calls blaming human error absurd
content: Following Spain's deadly high-speed train crash, Delano D'Souza is joined by Francisco Badea, Director of FEM Expert Engineering, Railway Structural & PRM Certification Expert. Batea challenges explanations that reduce railway disasters to isolated human mistakes. “It is basically an absurdity to say that it depended on one person and one human mistake,” he argues, emphasizing that modern railway networks operate through multiple layers of protection, including automated safeguards, train-detection technologies, operational protocols and institutional oversight. “The system has been designed in a way that this type of accident should never happen.”
summary: Spain's deadly high‑speed train crash was described as an accident that should never have happened. Francisco Badea, Director of FEM Expert Engineering, said it is absurd to attribute the crash to a single human mistake because modern railway systems have multiple layers of protection, including automated safeguards, train‑detection technologies, operational protocols and institutional oversight.
author: France 24

title: Retired Lt. Gen. Ben Hodges says Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth is removing dissenting officers
content:
Erin Ogunkeye welcomed Lt. General (ret.) Ben Hodges, the former commander of U.S. Army Europe and NATO Allied Land Command, to discuss recent concerns about the treatment of senior military leaders.  

Hodges highlighted the dismissal of Lt. General Brett Sylvia, arguing it signals a troubling pattern within the Pentagon under Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth. He criticized the reluctance of retired senior commanders to speak publicly against policies they view as damaging, saying he was “disappointed and surprised” by the limited public resistance among former four‑star generals.
summary: Erin Ogunkeye welcomes Lt. General (ret.) Ben Hodges, former commander of US Army Europe and NATO Allied Land Command.
author: France 24

title: French government proposes bill forcing protesters to pay up to €10,000 for riot damage
content: France is working to recover after riots and looting erupted on the periphery of nationwide peaceful demonstrations on October 17. In the aftermath, the government is advancing legislation that would require protesters to pay reparations of up to €10,000 for damage caused during public unrest, regardless of whether they were directly responsible for the vandalism. The proposed bill targets financial liability for participants in demonstrations linked to the recent disturbances.
summary: The French government is advancing a bill that would require protesters to pay reparations for damage caused during public unrest. The legislation would set liability at up to €10,000 per protester even if they were not directly responsible for the vandalism.
author: France 24

title: Paris suburb shooting suspect says he targeted Muslims, Africans
content: A man suspected of a gun attack in the Paris suburbs last week has told prosecutors that he deliberately targeted individuals who appeared to be Muslim, African or North African. The assault left one person dead and injured seven others, including a child. Prosecutors disclosed the suspect’s admission on Thursday. The incident occurred as the political climate in France grows increasingly tense, with the country about six months away from the next spring presidential election.
summary: A man suspected of a gun attack in the Paris suburbs last week has admitted to targeting individuals who appeared to be Muslim, African, or North African, prosecutors said on Thursday. The attack killed one person and wounded seven others, including a child.
author: France 24

title: Republicans target Michigan candidate El‑Sayed in midterm race
content: What in the name of political free speech is off-limits? Can you say whatever you want on the campaign trail, no matter how false or racist?
summary: Michigan's El‑Sayed is being targeted by Republicans in the midterms race. The article raises questions about the limits of political free speech on the campaign trail.
author: France 24

title: Paris suburb shooting underscores rising far‑right extremist threat in France
content:
François Picard welcomed Dr Joseph Downing, a Senior Lecturer in International Relations and Politics at Aston University, to discuss the rise of extremist right‑wing ideologies in France and elsewhere in the democratic world.  

Downing noted that France’s politics of insecurity now extends beyond crime to issues of national identity, the disappearance of a political centre and the erosion of democratic values. He linked the emergence of far‑right extremist violence and the ongoing stigmatization of ethnically diverse working‑class suburbs to a recent deadly shooting in the Paris suburbs, which he said was allegedly motivated by racist and anti‑Muslim hostility.
summary: Paris suburb shooting underscores rising far‑right extremist threat in France.
author: France 24

title: Star Trek and X‑Men star Patrick Stewart dies at 86
content: British actor Patrick Stewart died at age 86, a statement released on Thursday announced. Stewart, an acclaimed performer with the Royal Shakespeare Company, later starred in the 1980s sci‑fi television series “Star Trek” and subsequently appeared in the “X‑Men” franchise.
summary: British actor Patrick Stewart has died at age 86, a statement released on Thursday said. He was an acclaimed Royal Shakespeare Company performer who later starred in the TV series Star Trek and the X‑Men franchise.
author: France 24

title: China leaders call for greater loyalty and initiative at CCP session
content: At a recent Chinese Communist Party session, leaders called for greater loyalty and initiative while stressing internal discipline. The meeting did not resolve the question of Xi Jinping’s successor, and party officials expressed concern about potential instability as geopolitical tensions rise and the Chinese economy shows signs of cooling.
summary: The CCP session emphasized internal discipline — as expected, but left the question of Xi Jinping's successor unanswered. The party seems anxious of any instability as geopolitics heats up and China's economy cools down.
author: DW World

title: India finance ministry raises fiscal-year growth forecast, warns of fuel inflation
content: India’s Ministry of Finance has raised its growth forecast for the current fiscal year. At the same time, the ministry cautioned that inflation could remain a concern, especially for fuel and energy prices, given ongoing instability in the Middle East.
summary: India's Ministry of Finance has increased its growth forecasts for the current fiscal year. It warned about inflation, particularly for fuel and energy, amid continued instability in the Middle East.
author: DW World

title: Russian drone attack on Dnipro railway station kills 13 civilians
content: The United Nations’ top humanitarian official in Ukraine condemned a Russian drone attack on Dnipro’s main railway station on Thursday. The strike killed at least 13 civilians and injured 10 others.
summary: On Thursday, the UN’s top humanitarian official in Ukraine condemned a Russian drone attack on Dnipro’s main railway station. The strike killed at least 13 civilians and injured 10 others.
author: UN News

title: Qatar calls accusations of election interference in Israel “ridiculous and dangerous”
content: Netanyahu’s claim of interference in election also dismissed by Israeli police and opposition parties Israel’s choice: Netanyahu remaining in power or a Palestinian-backed coalition Gadi Eisenkot, leader of the Yashar party and Benjamin Netanyahu’s main rival, has warned political opponents against exploiting allegations of foreign interference in Israel’s election to delay the swearing-in of the next Knesset. In remarks posted on X, Eisenkot said: Israel must safeguard the integrity of the elections against any attempt at interference, spin and manipulation, and examine every complaint thoroughly. On the other hand, political actors must not be allowed to exploit the situation and affect the swearing-in date of the 26th Knesset.”
summary: Qatar calls accusations of election interference in Israel “ridiculous and dangerous”.
author: Guardian World

title: US Vice President JD Vance sends diplomatic letter to Iran's Mohsen Rezaei
content:
US Vice President JD Vance has sent a personal letter to Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran’s supreme national security council, in an effort to restart diplomacy and avert a major new conflict between the two nations. The correspondence, which arrived on Sunday following predominantly Qatari mediation, signals that Washington has not abandoned diplomatic channels ahead of the upcoming midterm elections.

The letter proposes a specific framework for negotiations, requiring Tehran to agree to commitments on its nuclear program at the outset of the process. In exchange for these initial steps, the US would provide sanctions relief, with the aim of opening the Strait of Hormuz within seven days.
summary: US Vice President JD Vance wrote a personal letter to Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran’s supreme national security council, after predominantly Qatari mediation. The letter asks Tehran to make nuclear‑program commitments that would open the Strait of Hormuz within seven days in exchange for US sanctions relief.
author: Guardian World

title: German actress Elke Sommer dies at 85 in Los Angeles
content:
German actress Elke Sommer, known for her work in “A Shot in the Dark,” the early‑1970s Agatha Christie adaptation “And Then There Were None,” and the British comedy “Carry on Behind,” has died at age 85. Bild magazine reported that she passed away in Los Angeles from heart failure.

Born in Berlin, Sommer’s facility with languages helped her transition from European cinema to Hollywood, where she appeared alongside actors such as Peter Sellers, Dick Van Dyke and Paul Newman. Her career peaked in the 1960s and 1970s, making her one of the few German performers of that era to achieve notable success in English‑language films and to be highlighted for her bombshell image.
summary: Elke Sommer, the Berlin-born German star of "A Shot in the Dark", "And Then There Were None" and "Carry on Behind", died at age 85. Bild magazine reported she died in Los Angeles of heart failure.
author: Guardian World

title: Seven tankers with 288,000 tonnes of Russian diesel head to US
content:
Seven oil tankers carrying an estimated 288,000 tonnes of Russian diesel are sailing towards the US, according to tracking data from Greenpeace. This shipment represents the first phase of a supply deal negotiated between presidents Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin earlier this month, which reverses years of sanctions on Russian oil.

Uncertainty remains regarding whether the vessels will be able to unload their cargo, as a political dispute continues over the legality of the shipments.
summary: Seven tankers with 288,000 tonnes of Russian diesel head to US.
author: Guardian World

title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang targeted by Chinese spy linked to Megaspeed executive
content:
U.S. intelligence agencies say Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang has been targeted by a Chinese spy, according to a New York Times report. The alleged spy, identified as Alice Huang—or Huang Le—is an executive at Singapore‑based datacenter firm Megaspeed and is not related to the Nvidia CEO.  

Officials previously suspected her of smuggling Nvidia chips to China, prompting surveillance. Unnamed sources cited by the newspaper say the agencies have concluded she was acting as a Chinese intelligence asset, passing commercial information about Nvidia to Beijing.
summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang targeted by Chinese spy linked to Megaspeed executive.
author: Guardian World

title: Hong Kong leader apologises for residential fire that killed 168 people
content:
Hong Kong’s deadliest residential fire since 1980 killed 168 people, and survivors and bereaved families have said justice has yet to be served.  

In a rare public act of contrition, Chief Executive John Lee apologized for government shortcomings that contributed to the blaze. Lee and seven other officials bowed in apology at the release of a report that identified “decades of failure” by government bodies. The apology, however, did not satisfy many victims’ families.
summary: Hong Kong chief executive John Lee and seven other officials apologized for government shortcomings that contributed to the fire that killed 168 people last year. The apology was made when a report citing “decades of failure” by government bodies was released, though some survivors and families said justice remains unmet.
author: Guardian World

title: Lula’s runoff victory trounces far right, hailed as win for planet and democracy
content: The trouncing of the far right provides a playbook for social and environmental movements in other countries facing elections, including the US, Spain and France Thank you, Brazil, for demonstrating how the far right can be trounced while protection for the Amazon is strengthened. In a world where nature and democracy appeared to be bleeding out in tandem, voters and forest defenders in this global south powerhouse have shown it is possible to staunch the flow. This should provide much needed inspiration and, more practically, a playbook for social and environmental movements in other countries facing elections, including the US, Spain and France. The astonishing comeback victory of Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva in Sunday’s presidential runoff against his extreme right challenger Flavío Bolsonaro has brought oceans of rapturous supporters on to the streets, while also thrilling conservationists, climate activists and social justice campaigners across the world.
summary: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva won Brazil’s presidential runoff on Sunday, defeating far‑right challenger Flavío Bolsonaro. The victory was celebrated by supporters, conservationists and climate activists as a model for social and environmental movements in other elections such as those in the US, Spain and France.
author: Guardian World

title: Bryan Adams releases new song “Lake Ontario” criticizing Donald Trump
content: Musician wrote a ‘love letter’ to Canada with a new album – and some pointed commentary about the US president Lake Ontario, the vast body of water that straddles the US-Canada border, has gone by many names over the centuries: Lac Saint-Louis, Lacus Ontarius, Skaniadorio, Cataraqui Lake. But one thing it will never be called, says the Canadian rock star Bryan Adams, is Lake America. In his new song Lake Ontario, Adams takes aim at the US president, Donald Trump, accusing him of “breaking the peace” between the people who live on the lake’s shores. The ‘lake of shining waters ’ is what the Iroquois called her It’s a First Nations name – not an executive order. But things weren’t going his way in Iran So like a baby tossing the toys from the pram You can push us to the brink But where the open road divides
summary: Bryan Adams releases new song “Lake Ontario” criticizing Donald Trump.
author: Guardian World

title: SpaceX Starfall capsule delivers Air Force cargo in point-to-point test
content:
The U.S. Air Force Research Laboratory (AFRL) confirmed the successful recovery of cargo pods from SpaceX’s Starfall capsule, marking a significant milestone in testing point-to-point rocket cargo delivery. The AFRL announced via social media on October 26 that the agile cargo pods were recovered after splashdown in the Pacific Ocean. This mission utilized the secretive, uncrewed reentry vehicle to transport military equipment through space and back to Earth, demonstrating the potential for rapid global mobility for the Future Force.

The Starfall capsule launched on a Falcon 9 rocket as part of SpaceX’s Bandwagon-5 mission, which lifted off from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station on October 20. AFRL Technology Transition Office director Adam Remaly described the event as a critical achievement in examining the viability of Rocket Cargo delivery. The mission involved a series of AFRL-developed cargo pods designed to carry various items, including medical equipment, food ration packs, and other military kit intended for emergencies in locations difficult to reach via conventional transportation.

Each cargo pod contained sensors to monitor temperature conditions and measure shock and vibration forces exerted on the cargo during launch, reentry, and splashdown. Researchers specifically monitored electronics and survival gear, which included a SATCOM-enabled tracker, batteries, a reverse osmosis desalinator, and emergency medical equipment. Additionally, the AFRL conducted a fit check of a UNI-PAC III life raft inside the Starfall capsule, a component that could potentially be included in future tests.

SpaceX’s disk-shaped Starfall capsule made its debut on a Falcon 9 launch in June, with the company maintaining relative silence about the vehicle. According to a Federal Aviation Administration environmental assessment published earlier this year, the hockey-puck-shaped vehicle measures approximately 3.1 meters (10.2 feet) across. It is capable of returning up to 1,000 kilograms (2,200 pounds) of cargo from orbit and features a carbon fiber heat shield, compressed gas thrusters for attitude control, and a parachute system for precision landings.

The AFRL will now assess the data recovered from the October 20 mission to support its broader Rocket Cargo initiative. The Air Force aims to evolve this program to transport tens of tons of cargo per launch, a capacity that exceeds Starfall’s current limits. While SpaceX’s larger Starship rocket was a likely candidate for tests at Johnston Atoll, those plans were suspended in July 2025 due to environmental concerns, leaving the status of the search for an alternative site unclear.
summary: The Air Force Research Laboratory recovered SpaceX's Starfall cargo capsule in the Pacific Ocean after it launched on a Falcon 9 rocket on October 20. The mission tested AFRL-developed pods carrying military equipment to assess the viability of point-to-point rocket cargo delivery.
